item.title: Appian targets about $2 billion for Africa but warns policy risk is driving capital away
item.description: Appian Capital Advisory plans to deploy $5 billion to $7 billion globally over the next 12 to 24 months, with roughly $2 billion for Africa, CEO Michael Scherb said, though policy uncertainty is pushing investment toward Latin America.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Adombila
item.content:encoded: Appian Capital Advisory plans to deploy $5 billion to $7 billion globally over the next 12 to 24 months, with roughly $2 billion for Africa, CEO Michael Scherb said, though policy uncertainty is pushing investment toward Latin America. The London-based mining private equity firm currently holds three active investments in Africa and has exited three others. Those exits include projects in Burkina Faso and Tanzania, which came amid a coup and an election crisis, respectively. Appian has four active investments in Latin America, mainly in Brazil. African governments have [USN:L8N4431YW TEXT:"tightened control"] over their mining sectors in recent years, revising mining codes, [USN:L8N3ZX0RE TEXT:"raising royalties"] and demanding greater local participation as they seek a larger share of mineral wealth. Latin America has generally maintained more stable fiscal and permitting regimes, despite resource nationalism in major producers like Chile, Peru and Mexico. "The geology doesn't change, but government policy does," Scherb told Reuters on Tuesday. "It's costly for investors to leave, but it's also costly for governments because that capital simply moves elsewhere." Scherb said Appian views Morocco, Namibia and Botswana as top-tier mining jurisdictions and is evaluating opportunities in Ghana, Ivory Coast, Mauritania and Senegal. Appian invests in gold, copper, zinc, rare earths and other critical minerals. It remains bullish on copper, he said, expecting supply growth to struggle to keep pace with demand from electrification, artificial intelligence, data centres and power-grid expansion. He said African countries could capture a significantly larger share of global mining investment by streamlining permitting and improving policy predictability. "The capital is there," Scherb said. "The question is which countries will create the stability and predictability needed to attract it."

item.title: Ibovespa recua na abertura ainda sob ajuste pós-eleição, com balanços e Flávio no radar
item.description: A bolsa paulista abria nesta quarta-feira ainda sob efeito dos ajustes pós-eleição, com investidores também de olho na temporada de balanços, que incluía os números de Santander Brasil e Klabin, e analisando potenciais desdobramentos da ida de Flávio Bolsonaro para os Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A bolsa paulista abria nesta quarta-feira ainda sob efeito dos ajustes pós-eleição, com investidores também de olho na temporada de balanços, que incluía os números de Santander Brasil e Klabin, e analisando potenciais desdobramentos da ida de Flávio Bolsonaro para os Estados Unidos. Às 10h11, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, perdia 0,71%, a 174.466,83 pontos. O contrato futuro do índice com vencimento mais curto , em 16 de dezembro, caía 0,94%.

item.title: Empathy and purpose drive Los Javis' Oscar hopeful 'La Bola Negra'
item.description: Spanish filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi said their sophomore feature "La Bola Negra", which has emerged as an Oscar contender, took them on the journey of their lives and left them with many more ideas they cannot wait to tackle.
item.dc:creator: Hanna Rantala
item.content:encoded: Spanish filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi said their sophomore feature "La Bola Negra", which has emerged as an Oscar contender, took them on the journey of their lives and left them with many more ideas they cannot wait to tackle. Industry buzz over a possible Oscar has built for the film since its launch at the Cannes Film Festival in May where the duo, nicknamed "Los Javis", won a best directing prize. A record-breaking domestic box office performance ensued and Spain last month named the film, whose title literally means the black ball, as its official submission for the 2027 Academy Awards. Co-written by Calvo, Ambrossi and Spanish playwright Alberto Conejero, "La Bola Negra" is inspired by an unfinished work of the same name by Federico Garcia Lorca, one of the most influential figures of 20th-century Spanish literature, who was murdered by fascist forces. It is also based on a play by Conejero, "La Piedra Oscura", the dark stone in English. The film's three intertwined stories span a time-period from Spain's 1936-1939 Civil War to the present day and address the difficulty historically of living openly as a homosexual. "It means so much that a movie with this message, done by two gay men and three gay actors portraying gay characters, in such a queer universal story, is connecting to so many people," Ambrossi told Reuters. "What gives me a lot of energy is that we represent Spanish culture at this moment. It's a very Spanish movie. It's in Spanish, it's about our literature, about Federico Garcia Lorca, and when I'm tired, I remember that it's a movie with a purpose, of empathy." GUITARRICADELAFUENTE'S ACTING DEBUT The film's storylines follow Sebastian in 1937, Carlos in 1932 and Alberto in 2017, portrayed by musician Guitarricadelafuente and actors Milo Quifes and Carlos Gonzalez, respectively. Guitarricadelafuente, 29, makes his acting debut, as Sebastian, a trumpet player tasked with guarding captured soldier Rafael Rodriguez Rapun, the lover of Lorca. Guitarricadelafuente said finding parallels in his own life helped to soothe his nerves. "Musically, at that moment, I was doing an album that was talking about self-discovery, someone that's finding his place in the world," said the singer-songwriter, who also co-wrote "La nieve" (the snow) for the film's soundtrack. "I just put my soul in it and tried to represent the story the most honest way possible." The movie also features Penelope Cruz as a wartime entertainer and Glenn Close playing a Lorca scholar. Netflix won a bidding for the film's US distribution rights and has given it a record 47-day theatrical release before its streaming debut on December 2. "La Bola Negra" is out in UK and Irish cinemas on November 6 and globally from late 2026. The two directors, meanwhile, are eager to get started on their next projects. "I can't wait to get back to my blank paper. I can't wait to get back to shooting, to work," said Calvo. "There's a wide range of stories that we are interested in, so I think we have a lot ahead in terms of different stories and different characters and a lot of things that haven't been told," added Ambrossi.

item.title: UBS revisa al alza previsiones para el Brent, ve al crudo en 110 dólares por barril a finales 2026
item.description: UBS revisó al alza el miércoles sus previsiones sobre los precios del crudo Brent y prevé que el petróleo se mantenga en niveles elevados en los próximos meses, ya que el suministro de Oriente Medio sigue siendo vulnerable a las interrupciones en un contexto de incertidumbre geopolítica.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UBS revisó al alza el miércoles sus previsiones sobre los precios del crudo Brent y prevé que el petróleo se mantenga en niveles elevados en los próximos meses, ya que el suministro de Oriente Medio sigue siendo vulnerable a las interrupciones en un contexto de incertidumbre geopolítica. El banco prevé ahora que el crudo Brent cotice a 110 dólares el barril a finales de 2026, por sobre su proyección anterior de 100 dólares. UBS elevó su previsión para el Brent en marzo de 2027 de 90 a 95 dólares por barril, en junio de 2027 de 85 a 90 dólares y en septiembre de 2027 de 80 a 85 dólares "La incertidumbre en torno a nuestras previsiones sigue siendo elevada, lo que refleja la naturaleza impredecible del conflicto en Oriente Medio, así como el ritmo de recuperación de la producción del golfo Pérsico y de la demanda mundial de petróleo", señaló el banco en una nota. Los embarques de crudo de Oriente Medio se han recuperado sustancialmente de la grave interrupción sufrida a principios de este año, señaló UBS, aunque añadió que los embarques portuarios de crudo y condensado de los países del golfo siguen por debajo de los niveles previos al conflicto El banco también señaló que en octubre se registró un número récord de ataques a buques en el estrecho de Ormuz y sus alrededores, lo que ha elevado los costos de los seguros y del transporte marítimo El aumento de los costos de transporte marítimo está respaldando los precios del Brent, según UBS; las tarifas de los superpetroleros que transportan crudo de Oriente Medio a China se han disparado de 1 a 3 dólares a entre 30 y 40 dólares por barril durante la última década, debido a la mayor duración de los viajes y a la menor disponibilidad de petroleros Los precios del petróleo subían más de un 1% el miércoles, con el crudo Brent superando los 115 dólares por barril, tras un ataque a una refinería saudita

item.title: Rusia recurre a ruta ártica de tiempos de la Segunda Guerra Mundial para exportar cereales
item.description: Rusia, el mayor exportador mundial de trigo, ha recurrido por primera vez a una ruta marítima ártica de tiempos de la Segunda Guerra Mundial para exportar cereales, ya que el conflicto en Ucrania complica el comercio en el mar Negro y las autoridades advierten de los riesgos que entraña el mar Báltico, controlado por la OTAN.
item.dc:creator: Gleb Stolyarov, Olga Popova
item.content:encoded: Rusia, el mayor exportador mundial de trigo, ha recurrido por primera vez a una ruta marítima ártica de tiempos de la Segunda Guerra Mundial para exportar cereales, ya que el conflicto en Ucrania complica el comercio en el mar Negro y las autoridades advierten de los riesgos que entraña el mar Báltico, controlado por la OTAN. Rusia y Ucrania llevan atacando mutuamente sus puertos y buques desde que comenzó la nueva temporada de comercialización de cereales en julio, lo que ha paralizado el comercio agrícola en el mar Negro, que antes estaba en pleno auge. Moscú, que busca conservar a sus principales clientes de cereales en Oriente Medio y Asia, intentó desviar las exportaciones hacia el mar Báltico, subvencionando el transporte ferroviario desde las fértiles regiones del sur, pero también se fijó en las oportunidades que ofrecía el Ártico. El puerto comercial de Múrmansk y Demetra Holding, una de las mayores empresas comerciales del país, anunciaron el miércoles que se está cargando en un buque el primer envío de 3.400 toneladas de cereales procedentes de "regiones agrícolas clave". Múrmansk, situado a casi 2.000 kilómetros al norte de Moscú, cerca de la frontera con Noruega, es accesible a través de aguas neutrales. Los convoyes aliados utilizaron este puerto durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial para entregar mercancías a la Unión Soviética. "En un momento en el que las rutas de exportación tradicionales se enfrentan a restricciones, el Puerto Marítimo Comercial de Múrmansk está abriendo con rapidez una ruta alternativa hacia los mercados extranjeros para los agricultores rusos", afirmó el puerto. Según datos del sector naviero y una fuente del mercado, está previsto que se carguen en Múrmansk unas 28.000 toneladas de trigo en un buque con destino al puerto de Casablanca, en Marruecos. Rusia ha desviado su comercio sobre todo hacia los puertos del mar Báltico, que gestionaron 1,2 millones de toneladas en septiembre, lo que representa más del 60% de todas las exportaciones de cereales por vía marítima. Las empresas han estado reconvirtiendo las terminales de fertilizantes y carbón para gestionar el transporte de cereales. Algunos responsables del Kremlin han advertido de los riesgos que suponen posibles acciones hostiles por parte de países europeos miembros de la OTAN en la zona. Todos los países con acceso al mar Báltico, excepto Rusia, son miembros de la OTAN. Las relaciones de Rusia con Europa se han deteriorado en los últimos meses, ya que el Kremlin acusa a los países europeos de implicación militar directa en el conflicto de Ucrania. Los gobiernos europeos han rechazado las acusaciones rusas de que estén directamente implicados, afirmando que su apoyo militar y financiero a Ucrania tiene como objetivo ayudar a Kiev a defenderse. Turquía, importadora de cereales de Rusia, lideró los esfuerzos para lograr un alto el fuego y reanudar los envíos en el mar Negro, pero Rusia ha declarado que ya no está interesada en un nuevo acuerdo.

item.title: Canada reports limited progress in trade talks with US
item.description: There has been limited progress in trade talks with the United States, a Canadian government official with knowledge of the discussions said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: There has been limited progress in trade talks with the United States, a Canadian government official with knowledge of the discussions said on Wednesday. Reuters reported on Monday that the two countries were working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian[USN:L6N46C11U TEXT:" steel and autos. "] US President Donald Trump's Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in next week's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] and tariffs on Canadian imports have become a for Trump, with Republican candidates in border states calling for an end to the trade war with Canada. The latest talks have focused on tariffs imposed under Section 232 of US trade law, including up to a 50% tariff on Canadian steel and a 25% tariff on autos. The US Commerce Department, which administers the Section 232 tariffs, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump on Sunday predicted the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics. Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday there had been "a slight intensification" in talks.

item.title: UK's Healey raises business rates threshold for small firms
item.description: British finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday he would raise the threshold at which small companies start paying business rates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday he would raise the threshold at which small companies start paying business rates. "I'm increasing the threshold for Small Business Rate Relief for retail hospitality and leisure businesses from £12,000 to £18,000 ($15,900-$23,900)," Healey said in his budget speech to parliament. The figures relate to "rateable value", the estimated annual rental value of a commercial property. Healey said the move will mean 70,000 businesses will not pay any business rates - a property tax charged on commercial properties to fund local services. He said other businesses in the retail, hospitality and leisure sectors would see their rates frozen in real terms. Prime Minister Andy Burnham had said in July he would [USN:L6N43P0CQ TEXT:"lower business rates"] for pubs, clubs and live music venues by 20% from April 2027. ($1 = 0.7527 pounds)

item.title: Britain's finance minister hikes bank tax to 6%, less than lenders feared
item.description: Britain is to double a tax surcharge on banks to 6%, finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday as part of his first budget announcement, resisting intense lobbying pressure from lenders in recent months which had argued any such increase could curb lending.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain is to double a tax surcharge on banks to 6%, finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday as part of his first [USN:L5N46E1W5 TEXT:"budget announcement"], resisting intense lobbying pressure from lenders in recent months which had argued any such increase could curb lending. Shares in HSBC (HSBA.L) , Barclays (BARC.L) , Lloyds Banking Group (LLOY.L) and NatWest <NWG.L rallied on Wednesday after the tax hike was smaller than feared, with Barclays, NatWest and Lloyds up around 4%. The tax hike comes via an increase in the surcharge banks pay on profits above a set threshold from 3% to 6%, partially reversing a cut from 8% three years ago under then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. The hike will be temporary and last for 15 months, Healey said. Big British lenders have reported bumper profits in recent years, fuelled by favourable interest rates. UK Finance, the industry lobby group, has said Britain already taxes banks higher than in other major financial centres. It estimated in a report this month that the UK banking sector paid £25.7 billion in direct taxation in the year to end-March. British trade unions had lobbied for an even bigger tax hike, citing fairness and banks' record profits.

item.title: UK's Healey says minimum wage to rise by 3.9%
item.description: Britain's finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday that the main minimum wage rate would increase by 3.9%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday that the main minimum wage rate would increase by 3.9%. The rate paid to workers aged 21 and over, currently £12.71 an hour, and the rate payable to workers aged 18-20, now £10.85, will both rise by 3.9%. Some analysts and employers had blamed larger jumps in the rate for younger workers for [USN:L8N4250GH TEXT:"increasing youth unemploymen"]t. The increase means the National Living Wage will increase to £13.21 an hour and the 18-20 National Minimum Wage will be £11.27. "For 2.3 million of our lowest-paid workers, I'm increasing both the national minimum wage and the National Living Wage by 3.9%," Healey told lawmakers on Wednesday. In April, Britain's Low Pay Commission – which advises on minimum wage rates – had said the National Living Wage would probably need to increase by around 3.7% in 2027 to £13.18 an hour to keep up with how it expected average pay to rise. Britain's main minimum wage rate has risen by around 50% since 2020 and is one of the highest among advanced economies as a share of median earnings, following efforts by successive governments to lift it to two thirds of median hourly pay. Businesses, especially in lower-paying sectors such as retail and hospitality, have complained about the increased minimum wage and higher social security contributions, though there is no clear evidence that it has cost large numbers of jobs. Between 2024 and 2026, the minimum wage for 18-20 year olds increased significantly faster than that for older workers, and ahead of its 2024 election victory, the Labour Party promised to scrap the lower rate which it called "discriminatory". However, in March, the Labour government tweaked the remit of the Low Pay Commission to give it [USN:L8N4260WD TEXT:"more scope to take labour market conditions into account"] when setting the minimum wage for 18-20 year olds. The most recent official data showed that [USN:L8N46608R TEXT:"average weekly earnings"], excluding bonuses, rose by an annual 3.7% in the three months to August, while [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"consumer price inflation"] hit an 11-month high of 3.5% in September.

item.title: Avalanche aim to regain footing in rematch vs. Devils
item.description: The Colorado Avalanche looked flat last week in their 4-3 loss to the New Jersey Devils.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Colorado Avalanche looked flat last week in their 4-3 loss to the New Jersey Devils. Things have not improved much for Colorado, but it has a chance to turn things around when the Devils come to Denver on Wednesday night. The Avalanche have lost three of their past four games, with all the losses coming on the road. The perennial Stanley Cup contenders acknowledge they have had issues with intensity lately but vowed it will be different going forward. "I think it's us as a group just not being good enough," Colorado captain Gabriel Landeskog said. "There's been games where it's been good, and there's been games where it's been really bad. I think we're also used to winning. But this year, we're not winning. We're finding ways to lose games here and there, and the bad ones have been real bad. "Those are the ones that (the media) and us ... we're trying to find the answers to. But, I have full confidence in this group. We know what we've got to do. We got to dig our way out of it." The one-goal loss in New Jersey on Oct. 20 was deceiving because Colorado scored two goals in the final 3:13 of the contest. Both of those were by Artturi Lehkonen, who has been the hottest goal scorer on the team. Lehkonen's 10 goals lead the team, with six coming in the past five games. Despite the recent struggles, Nathan MacKinnon is off to a strong start with 21 points (seven goals, 14 assists). The Devils come into the game off a 5-1 win in Dallas on Tuesday night in goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's debut with his new team. Jake Allen likely will get the start in net against the Avalanche and has a chance to sweep them this season. Allen had 31 saves in beating Colorado on Oct. 20, a 4-3 win that kickstarted the current four-game winning streak. He is 5-2 with a 2.84 goals-against average in seven starts this season, and with Hellebuyck joining the Devils, they have a formidable goaltending tandem. Logic dictates Hellebuyck, the 2025 Hart Trophy winner, is the No. 1 goaltender for New Jersey, but Allen is not worried about his standing with the team. "Whatever they need, whatever Connor needs," Allen said. "Obviously it's going to take a little bit of time to get going here, but I've never in my career had a set number of games. I can play whenever he needs a night off or things like that. "Like I said earlier in the year, I've held just about every position in the league, from a tandem to the starter to a glorified backup. Nothing is new to me. I'll be ready to go." Captain Nico Hischier comes into Wednesday night's game on a bit of a roll after a slow start to the season. He had two goals in the win at Dallas on Tuesday night, his second two-goal game of the season, and he has four points in his past four games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Russia's Rosatom says it is in advanced talks to supply floating nuclear power plants to African countries
item.description: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom could supply floating nuclear power plants to coastal African countries and is in advanced discussions with at least four nations, senior company executives said on Wednesday at a Russia-Africa Summit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom could supply floating nuclear power plants to coastal African countries and is in advanced discussions with at least four nations, senior company executives said on Wednesday at a Russia-Africa Summit. Vladimir Aptekarev, deputy head of Rosatom's machine-building division, said that 38 of Africa's more than 50 countries have sufficient coastline to host a Russian-made floating power unit. At present, only one floating nuclear power plant is in operation globally, in Russia's remote Chukotka region, dating from 2020. Floating plants use smaller reactors, are contained within a vessel which can be towed to a destination and require less infrastructure on land. They also make it possible to secure a new source of energy quickly and at a lower cost. "As a first step, a floating nuclear power unit can serve as a good entry point, enabling a country both to address its energy needs and to join the nuclear club," said Aptekarev. Rosatom is proposing implementing such projects under a power purchase agreement (PPA) model, with servicing and refuelling cycles carried out in Russia, allowing the unit to operate for up to 60 years. "With this source of electricity, we are effectively addressing all the key issues and challenges facing the African continent," he said. Rosatom is currently building Egypt's first nuclear power plant, El Dabaa, which will become the second nuclear power station on the African continent after South Africa's Koeberg plant, built using French technology in the mid-1980s. The project comprises four 1,200-MW power units with Russian-designed VVER-1200 reactors. Rosatom Chief Executive Alexei Likhachev told reporters the company is in advanced discussions on potential floating nuclear power plant projects with Egypt, Togo, Namibia and Tanzania. The prospect of deploying floating nuclear power plants in Egypt could also gain momentum following a meeting between the presidents of Russia and Egypt scheduled for Wednesday, he said. For international markets, Rosatom is offering floating power units with a capacity of 100 megawatts with RITM-200M reactors adapted for warm climates. Rosatom has already [USN:R4N45T00P TEXT:"reached"] an agreement with Indonesia on what it describes as the world's first export supplies of electricity generated by two floating nuclear power units with a combined capacity of 200 megawatts.

item.title: Bank of America plans new branches in Wisconsin, Alabama, New Orleans
item.description: Bank of America plans to open 19 branches in Wisconsin by 2030, creating 130 jobs, it said on Wednesday, and is on course to open 50 branches a year across the US.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bank of America (BAC.N) plans to open 19 branches in Wisconsin by 2030, creating 130 jobs, it said on Wednesday, and is on course to open 50 branches a year across the US. * BofA also plans to open 10 branches in Birmingham, Alabama, from the first quarter of 2027, and expand in Greater New Orleans in the second half of 2027 * "We continue to strategically enhance and expand our branch network, really trying to reach more of the US population," Holly O'Neill, president of the bank's consumer, retail and preferred banking, told Reuters * "We choose these markets based on their growth dynamics, their population, and our opportunity to grow the business," she said * The bank has 3,500 branches or financial centers that cover 83% of the US population. Since 2016, Bank of America has invested more than $5 billion in branches

item.title: Clippers want full-game performance against high-scoring Lakers
item.description: After finally meeting their match on offense, the Los Angeles Lakers will look to rebound from a high-scoring affair when they travel across town to face the Los Angeles Clippers at Inglewood, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After finally meeting their match on offense, the Los Angeles Lakers will look to rebound from a high-scoring affair when they travel across town to face the Los Angeles Clippers at Inglewood, Calif. One game after he scored 52 points in a victory at Utah, Luka Doncic delivered 41 on Tuesday, although the Lakers fell 136-129 at home against the Portland Trail Blazers. Teammates Austin Reaves added 26 points and Sandro Mamukelashvili contributed 17. After LeBron James bid farewell to the Lakers by signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in July, Los Angeles won its first three games this season with a revamped roster before losing for the first time on Tuesday. "I think sometimes early in the season, these are good learning lessons that we can apply both as coaches and players," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "How can we teach and scheme better? It was an incredible shot-making game. Also factor that in." While the Lakers shot 56.3% from the floor, the Trail Blazers shot 59%, including 57.1% in the fourth quarter to seal the victory. Portland also was 18 of 36 (50%) from 3-point range for the game. Doncic promised high-level efforts when he wrote in a letter to fans before the season began that the team was "going to give you everything we have, every single night. No excuses. No nights off." Doing his best to live up to his word, Doncic has averaged 36 points, 6.8 rebounds and 8.3 assists a game this season. Reaves has averaged 26.5 points. While the offense has delivered, a new physical defense had its flaws against Portland. "We didn't do basic coverages like we were supposed to," Reaves said. "We had a lot of blown assignments, and it was everybody. I made some bad defensive mistakes. You could go around the room." The Lakers already have defeated the Clippers once this season, 125-117 at home on Friday. The Lakers took charge by going on a 14-1 run late in the third quarter. Reaves scored 28 points and Doncic 23. After the Clippers watched last week's game against the Lakers slip away, they were competitive into the closing minutes Sunday on the road against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Clippers trailed 97-96 with three minutes remaining before the Thunder pulled away with a quick 6-0 burst en route to a 108-101 victory. Darius Garland scored 16 points with 11 assists for the Clippers, while Kris Dunn and Brook Lopez each had 15 points in a balanced offensive attack. So what did Clippers coach Tyronn Lue learn about his team in the tough loss? "That we play hard. We can play with any team," he said. "Now we have to figure out how to close games. Taking care of the basketball is one thing. But if we're competing for 48 minutes -- not 34 minutes, not 38 minutes -- then we have a chance to be in any given game." Of primary concern was the Clippers' 26 turnovers that led to 38 points for the Thunder. In the fourth quarter, the Clippers had seven turnovers that yielded 13 points. Against the Lakers on Friday, the Clippers also had 26 turnovers that were turned into 33 points. The Clippers average an NBA-high 23.3 turnovers per game, with no other team averaging more than 19.5 this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Research organization IAVI receives US funding for Ebola vaccine development
item.description: IAVI, a biomedical research organization, said on Wednesday it was awarded $36 million under a US government contract worth up to $99 million to advance development of its single-dose vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: IAVI, a biomedical research organization, said on Wednesday it was awarded $36 million under a US government contract worth up to $99 million to advance development of its single-dose vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo has risen above 10,000, [USN:L2N46D08D TEXT:"government data"] showed on Tuesday, making the Bundibugyo outbreak the country's largest and deadliest. Here are more details: The US Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority award supports manufacturing of vaccine doses for clinical testing and outbreak response, including an early-stage trial It also supports development of an updated candidate targeting the variant behind the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak There are currently no approved vaccines or specific treatments for disease caused by Bundibugyo virus IAVI will partner with Hilleman Laboratories, SK bioscience, and IDT Biologika for development, manufacturing and vaccine production IAVI's one-dose rVSV-based vaccine candidate has demonstrated protective efficacy in animal studies, the organization said Single-dose vaccines may offer practical advantages during outbreaks by allowing rapid vaccination without the logistical requirements of a multidose regimen Drugmaker Regeneron (REGN.O) on Monday [USN:L3N46C0UG TEXT:"said"] it had extended its agreement with the US health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment

item.title: Número de víctimas mortales en accidente ferroviario de España sube a 64, según gobierno regional
item.description: El número de fallecidos confirmados por el accidente del tren de alta velocidad ocurrido el miércoles cerca de Toledo en España subió a 64, informó el miércoles el Gobierno regional de Castilla-La Mancha, mientras los equipos de rescate seguían buscando entre los restos de los vagones
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: UK's Healey increases taxes on gambling companies in budget
item.description: British finance minister John Healey announced an increase in taxes on gambling companies on Wednesday in his annual budget.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey announced an increase in taxes on gambling companies on Wednesday in his annual budget. Healey said in his budget statement the government would raise Machine Games Duty, a tax on the net takings from some slot machines, to 25% from 20%. The new taxes will impact companies such as Ladbrokes owner Entain (ENT.L) and Evoke (EVOK.L) , the owner of William Hill UK and 888. Gambling companies warned ahead of the budget that higher taxes could lead to job losses in a sector already grappling with tax increases announced in last year's budget. Analysis commissioned by the Betting and Gaming Council, an industry lobby group, claimed in recent months that doubling Machine Games Duty could lead to the closure of up to 1,470 betting shops and the loss of 15,900 jobs across the industry.

item.title: US bans imports from three Chinese genomics companies, citing forced labor
item.description: The United States on Wednesday banned imports from three Chinese genomics companies for allegedly working with the government of Xinjiang to enable the forced labor of Uyghur and other ethnic minorities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States on Wednesday banned imports from three Chinese genomics companies for allegedly working with the government of Xinjiang to enable the forced labor of Uyghur and other ethnic minorities. The companies are BGI Genomics Co.. Ltd, (300676.SZ), MGI Tech Co Ltd. (688114.SS) and Shenzhen BGI Technology Co Ltd, which the U.S. says is also known as the BGI Group. The companies were added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List, according to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, which identifies entities that use or facilitate the use of forced labor of Uyghurs and other minorities, or source material from the Xinjiang region. Beijing has regularly dismissed accusations of forced labor and other abuses against Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in the Xinjiang region

item.title: Alemanha não vê motivo para questionar resultado da eleição no Brasil
item.description: O governo alemão não vê motivos para questionar a validade dos resultados eleitorais no Brasil, afirmou porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O governo alemão não vê motivos para questionar a validade dos resultados eleitorais no Brasil, afirmou porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores nesta quarta-feira. "Com base em tudo que sabemos, tudo ocorreu conforme as regras... Esperamos continuar a parceria estratégica com o Brasil", disse porta-voz em coletiva de imprensa. (Reportagem de Ludwig Burger)

item.title: Lucro do Deutsche Bank supera previsões no 3º tri
item.description: O Deutsche Bank divulgou nesta quarta-feira um aumento de 2% no lucro do terceiro trimestre, contrariando as expectativas de queda, já que o bom desempenho dos setores de banco de varejo e corporativo compensou a receita mais fraca do banco de investimentos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) divulgou nesta quarta-feira um aumento de 2% no lucro do terceiro trimestre, contrariando as expectativas de queda, já que o bom desempenho dos setores de banco de varejo e corporativo compensou a receita mais fraca do banco de investimentos. O maior banco da Alemanha registrou lucro líquido atribuível aos acionistas de 1,59 bilhão de euros (US$1,77 bilhão), acima dos 1,56 bilhão de euros do ano anterior e superando a previsão média dos analistas, de 1,44 bilhão de euros. Os resultados se somam aos sinais de fraqueza nos principais bancos de investimento, já que a volatilidade dos mercados de capitais pesou sobre as atividades durante o trimestre. O aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos, as preocupações com a inteligência artificial e os conflitos geopolíticos têm inquietado investidores e conselhos administrativos, restringindo as negociações e pesando sobre a receita da área de banco de investimento. A receita proveniente da negociação de títulos de renda fixa e moedas, um dos maiores negócios do Deutsche Bank, caiu 3% após um desempenho recorde no ano anterior. A queda ficou em linha com as expectativas e foi menos acentuada do que a queda de 5% relatada por concorrentes norte-americanos. Para o banco de investimento como um todo, a receita caiu 2%, em linha com as expectativas. A divisão continuou sendo a maior fonte de receita do Deutsche Bank. O Deutsche Bank adotou um tom mais otimista em relação às perspectivas para o ano inteiro, prevendo receitas do grupo superiores a 33 bilhões de euros, em comparação com a orientação anterior de cerca de 33 bilhões de euros. (Reportagem de Tom Sims e Matthias Inverardi)

item.title: Wall Street's wider weakness keeps AI trade rolling
item.description: AI remains the only game in town for Wall Street, and a lack of attractive alternatives is perpetuating this reliance. That risks making a crash all the more likely and painful when it comes.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: AI remains the only game in town for Wall Street, and a lack of attractive alternatives is perpetuating this reliance. That risks making a crash all the more likely and painful when it comes. The concentration of US equity indices in tech is well known, but less appreciated is how weakness in other sectors is helping drive this phenomenon. Normally, when a market boom starts to seem a bit top-heavy, investors begin trimming exposure. While that has happened to some extent recently, the moves have been modest. Despite the red flags around AI spending, investors are not giving up on the trade. Little wonder: Big Tech's recent track record has been exceptional. A group of 41 AI-related stocks has accounted for 75% of S&P 500 (.SPX) returns, 80% of earnings growth and 90% of capital spending growth since ChatGPT launched in November 2022, according to JPMorgan Private Bank. Technology and communication services, just two of the S&P 500's 11 sectors, are expected to deliver 42% of the entire index's forecast $783 billion in third-quarter earnings, according to LSEG. That share is expected to rise to 45% in the fourth quarter. Investors expect these two sectors to account for half of all earnings growth this year, with six sectors contributing just 10%. Tepid growth in other parts of the economy appears to be keeping a lid on rotation out of tech. THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT? This helps explain why market turbulence driven by AI jitters always seems to be so short-lived. Take the last few days. Last Thursday, the S&P 500 fell 1.2% as worries over the AI investment frenzy slammed chip stocks. That was notable less for the scale of the decline than for its remarkably narrow breadth. While the index fell, 337 of the index's 500 stocks actually rose, according to Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid. Indeed, of the nearly 3,000 days over the past three decades in which more than 300 stocks rose, [USN:L4N46803Y TEXT:"Thursday"] was the index's second worst performance. Curiously, the worst was January 27, 2025, when China's low-cost AI model DeepSeek burst onto the scene, sparking a record 17% crash in Nvidia (NVDA.O) shares. This is yet another reminder – as if investors needed one – of the risk that market concentration can pose. By Friday, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq (.IXIC) had closed at their lowest levels in over a month, pulled down by tech. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) plunged by 20% in a little over two weeks, while Meta (META.O) , which reported earnings last week, saw its shares fall 20% from their recent peak as investors were unnerved by the hyperscaler's plan for a record [USN:L3N46C0RK TEXT:"$97.5 billion equity raise"] to help fund its beefed-up AI spending binge. Not for the first time this year, it looked like we might be seeing the beginning of a deeper, more prolonged AI slide. But both benchmarks are already rebounding. On the surface, the catalyst appears to be Anthropic’s massive initial public offering (IPO) [USN:L4N4690UA TEXT:"filing on Monday"] and a host of other tech fundraising, which have apparently given investors confidence that the AI boom still has legs. Yet that’s puzzling, given that added equity supply would not normally be expected to boost equity prices. Once again, the alternatives for equity investors may simply be limited. NO CORRECTION HOME Of course, this earnings season could deliver a major downside surprise in the tech space that triggers a more durable reversal, even if investors are forced to flee to other asset classes or low-growth defensive stocks. HSBC strategists have turned cautious and, [USN:FWN46C10G TEXT:"on Monday"], cut their maximum overweight equity position to neutral. A decline of 10% or more in the S&P 500 wouldn't seem unreasonable. But it would be a rarity. In the last four years, the benchmark US equity index has only experienced one downturn of more than 10%. That was from February to April last year, when President Donald Trump's [USN:L1N40L0V1 TEXT:"“Liberation Day” tariffs"] spooked markets, culminating in a 20% fall. History shows that markets can continue rising even when alarm bells are loud and clear. Former Federal Reserve Chair Alan Greenspan famously called out the “irrational exuberance” of the US equity market in 1996, years before the dotcom bubble actually burst. The current AI boom could certainly outlast many doomsayers, given the slim opportunities elsewhere. It’s notable that when HSBC changed its equity stance, it also said that any dips in the coming weeks "will likely be a good buying opportunity." But the “there is no alternative” trade can only fuel the “fear of missing out” trade for so long. At some point, this boom loop can become a doom loop. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. item.title: EQT's acquisition of Range underscores race to dominate US natgas market
item.description: EQT's acquisition of rival producer Range Resources this week marks the latest consolidation in the natural gas industry, as producers are scrambling to lock in supply to feed growing demand for liquefied natural gas exports and power demand.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: EQT's (EQT.N) acquisition of rival producer Range Resources (RRC.N) this week marks the latest consolidation in the natural gas industry, as producers are scrambling to lock in supply to feed growing demand for liquefied natural gas exports and power demand. Canonsburg, Pennsylvania-based EQT said on Monday it will [USN:L3N46C0NK TEXT:"buy Fort Worth, Texas-based Range Resources"] (RRC.N) in a $13 billion all-stock deal that will create the nation's biggest gas producer. EQT is the second-largest natural gas producer in the US. "The Range transaction increases our market access to what we believe are the two premium markets in this world - domestically in Appalachia and on the international front with LNG," EQT CEO Toby Rice told Reuters in an interview following the deal. He said it makes the company "the natural choice for gas supply domestically and around the world." The deal underscores how top US gas producers are racing to consolidate ahead of what they expect will be a step-change in domestic demand, driven by new LNG export terminals coming online and a buildout of gas-fired power plants to supply electricity-hungry data centers — even as a near-term glut has depressed prices and [USN:L6N45E0P3 TEXT:"forced operators to curtail output"]. In Appalachia, where EQT and Range produce most of their gas, Rice said the company boosted its demand growth estimates for the region to over 25 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) from a prior forecast of around 20 bcfd. One billion cubic feet is enough gas to supply about five million US homes for a day. Rice said that about half of that demand growth would remain in the basin, supplying things like power plants to feed data centers, and the other half is for pipeline takeaway projects like EQT's [USN:L6N45E0P3 TEXT:"Mountain Valley Boost project"] to move more gas from West Virginia to Virginia and its proposed POWER project to move more gas from Pennsylvania to Ohio. On the international front, EQT has targeted having 15% of its gas sales exposed to international markets. "Increasing our production base with Range is going to give us the ability to increase our LNG capacity, still maintain our 15% strategic target (and) increase our LNG exposure," Rice said, noting that now was "an incredibly attractive opportunity" since gas was currently trading below $4 per million British thermal units in the US but over $30 in Europe and Asia. "Natural gas demand is inflecting in two directions at once (power for data centers and LNG exports) and EQT is the only Appalachian producer contracted into both," Melius Research analysts said in a note. MORE TO COME The EQT-Range merger follows Devon Energy's (DVN.N) merger with Coterra Energy in May 2026 to create the nation's third-biggest gas producer, and the merger of Chesapeake Energy and Southwestern Energy in October 2024 to create Expand Energy (EXE.O) , currently the nation's biggest gas producer. About a third of US gas production comes from the Marcellus and Utica shale basins in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia in Appalachia. "There's a number of logical ... combinations there that would likely occur over the next couple of years up in the Northeast ... I think it's a natural next step in consolidation," said Matthew Bernstein, vice president of North American oil and gas at energy research and consulting firm Rystad Energy. Bernstein said Expand Energy could make a move to bolster its position in the Northeast, noting there were quite a few public players with production in Appalachia, including Antero Resources (AR.N) , CNX Resources (CNX.N) and National Fuel Gas' (NFG.N) Seneca Resources spinoff. Officials at Expand, Antero and National Fuel Gas were not immediately available for comment. Officials at CNX said they do not comment on market speculation regarding mergers and acquisitions. Analysts at Mizuho said in a note that they "continue to see gas-focused US shale assets getting concentrated in fewer hands ... This bodes well for capital discipline, especially as gas demand is expected to inflect starting in 2028 on LNG and AI data center/electrification power demand tailwinds."

item.title: Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028 presentan su lema oficial, "Stars Align"
item.description: Los organizadores de los Juegos Olímpicos y Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028 han presentado "Stars Align" como su eslogan oficial, planteando el lema como el punto de encuentro entre la preparación deportiva de toda una vida y el protagonismo de la capital del entretenimiento.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: Los organizadores de los Juegos Olímpicos y Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028 han presentado "Stars Align" como su eslogan oficial, planteando el lema como el punto de encuentro entre la preparación deportiva de toda una vida y el protagonismo de la capital del entretenimiento. La campaña se estrenó el miércoles con un video promocional de 60 segundos acompañado del éxito de los Red Hot Chili Peppers "Can’t Stop", en el que se muestran lugares emblemáticos del sur de California, como el letrero de Hollywood y el Observatorio Griffith. Aunque el eslogan evoca de forma natural el glamour de Hollywood y las imágenes celestiales, el director de marketing de LA28, Alex Merchan, afirmó que el comité organizador quería que el mensaje redefiniera las percepciones modernas sobre el destino. "Para nosotros, 'Stars Align' no se basa en la suerte. Se fundamenta en el esfuerzo y el compromiso», declaró Merchan a Reuters en una entrevista. "'Stars Align' es cuando la preparación se une a la oportunidad y creamos algo extraordinario". Siguiendo la tradición de los lemas de las ciudades anfitrionas —como "United by Emotion" de Tokio 2020 y "Games Wide Open" de París 2024—, LA28 pretende plasmar tanto el escenario deportivo mundial como la identidad local. Merchan hizo hincapié en que el eslogan va más allá de los aproximadamente 15.000 deportistas que competirán para incluir a la mano de obra local, a los voluntarios y a las pequeñas empresas que participan a través de iniciativas como el programa de proveedores "Local Authentic" de LA28. "Sí, celebraremos a esos atletas, pero no podemos perder de vista que estos Juegos serán posibles gracias a todas las estrellas que participan en su organización", afirmó Merchan, añadiendo que la campaña sirve como invitación para que la comunidad se implique desde el principio. La inauguración de los Juegos Olímpicos está prevista para el 14 de julio de 2028, seguida de los Juegos Paralímpicos el 15 de agosto. La presentación del eslogan supone un hito en una campaña comercial y cultural cada vez más intensa de cara a 2028, que acabará incluyendo el recorrido nacional del relevo de la antorcha por los 50 estados y la presentación de la mascota oficial. "Esto es solo la chispa, nuestro primer paso", afirmó Merchan. "Nos queda mucho más por venir".

item.title: UK's Healey extends freeze in fuel duty until at least July
item.description: Britain's finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday he would maintain a freeze on the level of fuel duty rates, extending a five-pence temporary cut introduced in 2022 until at least July.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday he would maintain a freeze on the level of fuel duty rates, extending a five-pence temporary cut introduced in 2022 until at least July. "Earlier this year, the government extended the 5p cut to Fuel Duty and slashed red diesel to its lowest rate in over 20 years. With the war in the Middle East still driving high fuel prices, I am extending these tax cuts for motorists through the winter and spring to July," Healey said in his budget statement. Duty paid on motor fuels has been frozen since 2011, except for the temporary cut which was introduced in 2022 when oil prices spiked after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The freeze has been extended by successive governments. The conflict in the Middle East has pushed up oil prices this year with the RAC motoring body reporting that the [USN:L8N45O0OV TEXT:"average pump price of diesel in Britain hit record highs"] in recent weeks. Fuel duty is a major revenue-raiser for the government and brings in around £25 billion ($33 billion) a year.

item.title: France Un hommage national sera rendu aux victimes de l'attentat de Trappes
item.description: "Un hommage national sera rendu" en soutien aux victimes de "l'acte terroriste raciste" qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves vendredi à Trappes et La Verrière dans les Yvelines, a annoncé mercredi la porte-parole du gouvernement, Maud Bregeon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: "Un hommage national sera rendu" en soutien aux victimes de "l'acte terroriste raciste" qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves vendredi à Trappes et La Verrière dans les Yvelines, a annoncé mercredi la porte-parole du gouvernement, Maud Bregeon. Le président Emmanuel Macron a "insisté sur le fait que dans cs moments-là, on devait être dans la responsabilité, dans l'unité et dans la dignité", a-t-elle dit à l'issue du conseil des ministres. "Il a insisté aussi sur le fait que la très faible compassion qu'il y a eu dans les heures qui ont suivi était de nature à inquiéter, de même que les tentatives d'instrumentalisation", a-t-elle ajouté. La porte-parole du gouvernement n'a pas donné de précisions sur la date ni le lieu de cet hommage national.

item.title: African Champions League group phase draw
