item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The draw for the group phase of the African Champions League was made in Cairo on Wednesday. Group A: Esperance (Tunisia), Petro Atletico (Angola), FC Nouadhibou (Mauritania), Wiliete (Angola) Group B: Zamalek (Egypt), Young Africans (Tanzania), Mouloudia Alger (Algeria), Club Africain (Tunisia) Group C: Renaissance Berkane (Morocco), Simba (Tanzania), Orlando Pirates (South Africa), Colombe Sportive (Cameroon) Group D: Pyramids (Egypt), Al Hilal (Sudan), Horoya (Guinea), Maghreb Fes (Morocco) The six rounds of group matches will be played between late November and the end of January. The top two teams in each group advances to the quarter-finals in February.

item.title: UK economic growth downgraded to 1% in 2027, Healey says in first budget
item.description: Britain's economy is forecast to grow by 1% next year, finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday, citing the latest projections from the Office for Budget Responsibility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's economy is forecast to grow by 1% next year, finance minister John Healey said on Wednesday, citing the latest projections from the Office for Budget Responsibility. The new figure compared with a growth forecast for 2027 of 1.6% in the OBR's previous outlook published in March and prepared before the start of the Iran war. The OBR expects economic output to expand by 1.6% in 2028, 1.8% in 2029, 1.7% in 2030 and 1.6% in 2031, Healey said as he gave his first budget statement speech to parliament. Those projections compared with the budget watchdog's previous expectations for growth of 1.6% in 2028 and 1.5% in 2029 and in 2030. Growth in 2026 was upgraded slightly to 1.2%, up from the previous forecast of 1.1%.

item.title: Telenor sees AI shoppers testing its premium mobile pitch
item.description: Telenor's efforts to persuade mobile customers to pay more for network quality and security services could face a new test from AI shopping agents expected to focus heavily on price, executives said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka Olenska, Jesus Calero
item.content:encoded: Telenor's (TEL.OL) efforts to persuade mobile customers to pay more for network quality and security services could face a new test from AI shopping agents expected to focus heavily on price, executives said on Wednesday. The Norwegian operator's "more-for-more" strategy adds benefits to subscriptions to encourage higher spending. Its task is to make those extras count when customers compare offers. AI agents would be "to a large degree price driven", CEO Benedicte Schilbred Fasmer told Reuters, saying the benefits beyond connectivity needed to be clear to customers. That would add another dimension to an already competitive market. Telenor lost 22,000 mobile subscriptions in Norway in the third quarter, while mobile revenue per user rose 2.7% year on year. CFO Torbjorn Wist argued in a call with analysts that prices were already transparent and that coverage, capacity and security would remain a "strategic moat". He also saw agents as a possible route to customers, provided Telenor could exchange information with them. The concern extends beyond telecoms. Payments firm Adyen (ADYEN.AS) [USN:L6N44A0IO TEXT:"told Reuters"] in August that merchants feared losing direct customer relationships and repeat business as shoppers increasingly turned to AI chatbots. Fasmer said Nordic identification requirements would keep people involved in subscription changes. Asked about competition in Norway, she remained confident in the existing strategy, although its pace could slow in some markets. "But we don't think we've run out of road on the more-for-more strategy," she said. Telenor is building a more Nordic-focused business, adding services such as security alongside connectivity while reducing its exposure in riskier Asian markets.

item.title: India seeks $220 billion clean energy push to meet 2030 target
item.description: India needs about $220 billion in clean energy investment over the next three years as it races to expand renewable power and grid infrastructure to meet its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, a senior government official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Sethuraman R
item.content:encoded: India needs about $220 billion in clean energy investment over the next three years as it races to expand renewable power and grid infrastructure to meet its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, a senior government official said on Wednesday. Santosh Kumar Sarangi, the top official at the federal clean energy ministry, said the investments will be needed across solar and wind power, battery energy storage, green hydrogen and transmission infrastructure. India currently has about 308 GW of non-fossil fuel-based power generation capacity and is aiming to increase that to 500 GW as part of its broader efforts to reach net-zero emissions by 2070. The country has already developed a market for about 550,000 tonnes of green ammonia demand from overseas buyers, including Japan and South Korea, he said. Between 2024 and 2026, India attracted about $64 billion of private investment into the clean energy sector, including $6.2 billion in foreign investment, while the government invested an additional $6 billion, Sarangi said. Due to an increased clean energy push and a large number of project tenders awarded over recent years, about 40 GW of clean energy projects have yet to find customers. The federal government is working with state governments to encourage them to take on clean power and ramp up battery storage, Sarangi said. India will meet investors next week at a clean energy summit in New Delhi to discuss potential investments from several countries, including pension funds from Canada, he added.

item.title: Melexis CEO says China now beats Europe in new design wins
item.description: Belgian chipmaker Melexis now records more design wins in China than in Europe, CEO Marc Biron said on Wednesday, underscoring the growing importance of the Chinese market for the company despite broader concerns about geopolitical tensions and supply chains.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Belgian chipmaker Melexis (MLXS.BR) now records more design wins in China than in Europe, CEO Marc Biron said on Wednesday, underscoring the growing importance of the Chinese market for the company despite broader concerns about geopolitical tensions and supply chains. "Four years ago we had more design wins in Europe than in China, but since two years we have had more design wins in China than in Europe," Biron said after Melexis reported record quarterly sales in China. Group sales stood at €223.7 million in the quarter, a 4% rise from last year Melexis [USN:L8N44M0AQ TEXT:"signed"] a Master Purchase Agreement with Chinese EV maker BYD (002594.SZ) in August The group also established its first China-based, Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in March, and introduced its first integrated circuit manufactured in the country Order book point to further sales growth in China over the next quarter

item.title: Nouvelle catastrophe ferroviaire en Espagne, le bilan s'alourdit à 67 morts
item.description: Une collision survenue mercredi matin entre deux trains à grande vitesse près d'Urda, dans le centre de l'Espagne, sur la ligne reliant Madrid à l'Andalousie (sud), a fait au moins 67 morts, ont rapporté les autorités locales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une collision survenue mercredi matin entre deux trains à grande vitesse près d'Urda, dans le centre de l'Espagne, sur la ligne reliant Madrid à l'Andalousie (sud), a fait au moins 67 morts, ont rapporté les autorités locales. Il s'agit de la deuxième catastrophe ferroviaire sur cette ligne cette année, après la collision survenue le 18 janvier à hauteur d'Adamuz, dans la province andalouse de Cordoue, qui avait fait 46 morts et plus de 150 blessés. Le drame avait eu un fort retentissement dans le pays, la population dénonçant une gestion défaillante et au rabais du réseau ferré, et le gouvernement avait alors annoncé un plan à grande échelle pour l'entretien des voies. L'accident de mercredi s'est produit près d'Urda, au sud de Tolède, dans la communauté autonome de Castille-La Manche. Un train AVE, opéré par la Renfe, la compagnie ferroviaire espagnole, et un train Iryo, du nom de l'opérateur privé détenu à plus de 50% par Trenitalia, sont entrés en collision peu après 09h00 (08h00 GMT), ce qui a entraîné le déraillement de plusieurs wagons de l'Iryo, a précisé Esther Padilla, porte-parole du gouvernement de Castille-La Manche. Des images aériennes diffusées par la Garde civile montrent au moins deux voitures de l'Iryo, reconnaissables à leur couleur rouge, couchées sur le remblai, des amas de tôle fracassée et des passagers blessés ou indemnes assis dans des champs adjacents au milieu de dizaines de véhicules de secours. Au total, 147 personnes se trouvaient à bord de l'Iryo, et 397 à bord de l'AVE, a-t-elle dit. Selon une source au fait des premiers éléments de l'enquête, le TGV Iryo s'est arrêté sur la voie près de Tolède, en raison d'un défaut de signalisation, à la demande de l'Adif, l'établissement public chargé de la gestion du réseau ferroviaire espagnol. C'est à ce moment qu'il a été percuté par un express de la Renfe. La Renfe et Iryo n'avaient pas répondu aux sollicitations de Reuters dans l'immédiat. "HORRIBLE" "On a entendu un bruit énorme, vraiment énorme, qui a duré une dizaine de secondes, comme si le train allait dérailler. Par la fenêtre, à droite, on a vu un train accidenté. J'imagine que c'est l'autre", a témoigné un passager sur la radio COPE. Le maire d'Urda, ville proche du site de la collision, a déclaré sur la même station que les secours avaient demandé à la municipalité de mettre à leur disposition des lieux d'accueil, notamment un gymnase, pour la prise en charge des blessés et des passagers. Le maire d'une autre localité voisine, Los Yébenes, a évoqué sur la RTVE un tragédie "horrible". "On nous parle de mutilations et de très graves blessures", a-t-il rapporté. La ministre de la Santé, Mónica García, a lancé un appel urgent aux dons de sang sur le réseau X. Les rendez-vous à l'agenda du président du gouvernement espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, ont été annulés. Le chef du gouvernement s'est dit "consterné" dans un message sur X et a exprimé son "affection, sa solidarité et son soutien aux victimes et à leurs familles". Le roi Felipe VI a exprimé son chagrin face à une "tragédie". "Aujourd'hui, l'Europe pleure avec vous", a écrit sur X la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen. Le président Emmanuel Macron a exprimé "la solidarité de la France". Un porte-parole du Parti populaire (droite, opposition) a fait savoir que la formation suspendait sa campagne pour les élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. La Fédération espagnole de football a annoncé dans un communiqué le report des 24 matches du premier tour de la Coupe du Roi qui étaient prévus ce mercredi. L'autorité nationale de sécurité ferroviaire (AESF) a recensé 69 accidents sur le réseau ferré espagnol - environ 4.000 kilomètres de voie - en 2025, contre 57 en 2024 et 45 en 2016.

item.title: Santander-Résultat net sous-jacent en hausse de 19% au T3 mais plombé par le Brésil
item.description: La banque espagnole Santander a affiché mercredi une hausse de 19% de son bénéfice net sous-jacent au troisième trimestre, porté par le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis après de récentes acquisitions sur ces marchés, bien que le Brésil ait partiellement terni ces résultats.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La banque espagnole Santander (SAN.MC) a affiché mercredi une hausse de 19% de son bénéfice net sous-jacent au troisième trimestre, porté par le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis après de récentes acquisitions sur ces marchés, bien que le Brésil ait partiellement terni ces résultats. Le bénéfice net sous-jacent, avant charges de restructuration, a atteint 3,85 milliards d’euros, dépassant les 3,75 milliards d’euros attendus par les analystes interrogés par Reuters. Une hausse de 11% des commissions sous-jacentes et de 12% du chiffre d’affaires ont également contribué à ces résultats. La diversification de Santander lui a permis de se prémunir contre les ralentissements économiques dans certaines régions, mais l’a rendue vulnérable à la volatilité des marchés et aux dépréciations monétaires, en particulier en Amérique latine. La banque a récemment cherché à renforcer sa position sur les marchés développés grâce aux acquisitions de TSB et de Webster, qui devraient, selon elle, contribuer à faire progresser son bénéfice de plus de 40% au cours des trois prochaines années, pour le porter à plus de 20 milliards d’euros. Au Brésil, son deuxième marché en importance, le bénéfice net a reculé de 15% par rapport à l’année précédente, en partie en raison d’une hausse de 23% des provisions. Le coût du risque, qui mesure les pertes potentielles, a augmenté de 11 points de base par rapport au trimestre précédent, pour s’établir à 4,25%. À la suite de la réélection surprise du président Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva au Brésil, l’action Santander a chuté de 3% lundi, après que les marchés boursiers et le real brésiliens ont enregistré leurs plus fortes baisses depuis des années. Santander bénéficie de la baisse des taux d'intérêt au Brésil, car ses coûts de financement sont étroitement liés aux taux de référence. En revanche, le résultat net sous-jacent a progressé de 48% aux États-Unis et de 40% au Royaume-Uni, tandis qu'il a augmenté de 21% au Mexique et de 19% en Espagne. JP Morgan a indiqué que les activités britanniques et américaines avaient dépassé les attentes, tandis que celles du Brésil avaient affiché des résultats inférieurs aux prévisions. Compte tenu des charges de dépréciation et de restructuration de 416 millions d’euros, principalement liées à l’acquisition de Webster, le bénéfice net publié attribuable a reculé de 2% à 3,43 milliards d’euros, tout en dépassant les prévisions de 3,23 milliards d’euros. Vers 10h10 GMT, l'action Santander reculait de 4,69% à 10,75 euros.

item.title: Indian e-commerce player Meesho's quarterly loss shrinks on rising orders
item.description: Indian online marketplace Meesho reported a narrower second-quarter loss on Wednesday, aided by rising orders and higher income from sellers paying to advertise on its platform.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian online marketplace Meesho (MEES.NS) reported a narrower second-quarter loss on Wednesday, aided by rising orders and higher income from sellers paying to advertise on its platform. Here are some details: Consolidated net loss contracted to 1.32 billion rupees ($13.9 million) in the July to September quarter, from 4.11 billion rupees a year earlier The Bengaluru-based company, known for its budget-friendly prices across fashion, home and everyday items, has been expanding its reach in smaller cities and towns while seeking to boost revenue from sellers and lower delivery costs Meesho competes with larger rivals Amazon (AMZN.O) and Walmart (WMT.O) -owned Flipkart The firm reported a 34% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to 41.32 billion rupees Revenue growth was aided by stronger ad revenue from sellers - Meesho Net merchandise value, a key metric for e-commerce platforms, rose 23% to 129.11 billion rupees, while orders placed increased 17% to 819 million Shares of Meesho, which listed in December last year, have gained 26.42% so far this year ($1 = 95.1875 Indian rupees)

item.title: Amazon unveils new lineup of Alexa devices including redesigned Echo Show
item.description: Amazon.com on Wednesday unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices including a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart display and a photo frame with built-in Alexa, as it pushes its latest version of the voice assistant into customers' homes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amazon.com (AMZN.O) on Wednesday unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices including a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart display and a photo frame with built-in Alexa, as it pushes its latest version of the voice assistant into customers' homes. Here are more details: The Echo Show 16, which has a 16-inch screen, built-in Fire TV and Amazon's first Echo Show camera with night vision, is available for pre-order from $499.99 A new Echo Studio speaker with a built-in camera, which lets Alexa recognize objects held up to it and lets users check on a room remotely, costs $249.99 The new Echo Dot, priced at $99.99, includes a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender for the first time Echo Time, a $199.99 bedside clock, uses sleep-sensing technology to wake users during lighter sleep, without a wearable device The Alexa Photo Frame, starting at $199.99, syncs pictures automatically from Amazon Photos Earlier this month, Apple (AAPL.O) [USN:L1N45Z0I8 TEXT:"launched HomeView"], a $299 smart home device with a 7-inch screen and face recognition, and HomePod mini 2, a $149 smart speaker Amazon is rolling out the devices as it faces growing competition from rivals including Apple, as well as AI companies such as OpenAI that have hardware ambitions.

item.title: Healey says UK will have £15 bln of fiscal headroom at end of forecast period
item.description: Britain's government will have a smaller buffer to meet its fiscal targets by the end of the decade, finance minister John Healey said in his first budget speech on Wednesday, citing forecasts from the Office for Budget Responsibility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's government will have a smaller buffer to meet its fiscal targets by the end of the decade, finance minister John Healey said in his first budget speech on Wednesday, citing forecasts from the Office for Budget Responsibility. The government's tax revenues were expected to be £15 billion ($20 billion) higher than day-to-day spending in the 2029/30 fiscal year, Healey said. He said the buffer is expected to rise to £22 billion in 2030/31. He said the government will meet its fiscal targets despite shocks from the Iran war. "That's what a buffer is for. Use it when you need it. Rebuild it when you can," Healey said. "So, despite the global challenges, this Budget puts us on track to eliminate the current budget deficit and get Britain's finances into the black within 3 years." At the time of former finance minister Rachel Reeves' budget update in March, the OBR estimated the government had £24 billion of so-called fiscal headroom. A Reuters poll of bond dealers earlier this month pointed to [USN:L8N4682G5 TEXT:"£15 billion"] of headroom as higher borrowing costs weighed on the government's spending. ($1 = 0.7527 pounds)

item.title: Netanjahus Block bei Israel-Wahl vorn - aber ohne klare Mehrheit
item.description: Nach der Parlamentswahl in Israel zeichnet sich ein klarer Vorsprung für das rechtsgerichtete Lager von Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanjahu ab. Allerdings verliert Netanjahu seine bisherige Koalitionsmehrheit in der Knesset. Nach Auszählung von gut 70 Prozent der Stimmen entfallen nach Hochrechnungen israelischer Medien vom Mittwoch auf Netanjahus Block 54 der 120 Sitze in der Knesset. Das Oppositionsbündnis des früheren Generalstabschefs Gadi Eisenkot kommt demnach auf 47 Mandate. Parteien, die die arabischstämmige Bevölkerung vertreten, erzielen 19 Sitze.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell, Lili Bayer, Tamar Beeri
item.content:encoded: Nach der Parlamentswahl in Israel zeichnet sich ein klarer Vorsprung für das rechtsgerichtete Lager von Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanjahu ab. Allerdings verliert Netanjahu seine bisherige Koalitionsmehrheit in der Knesset. Nach Auszählung von gut 70 Prozent der Stimmen entfallen nach Hochrechnungen israelischer Medien vom Mittwoch auf Netanjahus Block 54 der 120 Sitze in der Knesset. Das Oppositionsbündnis des früheren Generalstabschefs Gadi Eisenkot kommt demnach auf 47 Mandate. Parteien, die die arabischstämmige Bevölkerung vertreten, erzielen 19 Sitze. Damit verfehlt Netanjahu zwar die für eine Regierungsbildung notwendige Mehrheit von 61 Sitzen. Ein Sieg Eisenkots rückt jedoch in weite Ferne, da sein Lager nach den vorliegenden Zahlen deutlich dahinter zurückblieb. Netanjahus Gegner haben kaum Chancen, ihn ohne die Unterstützung arabischer Parteien abzulösen, was viele von ihnen ausgeschlossen haben. Zumindest während möglicher Koalitionsverhandlungen oder bis zu einer möglichen Neuwahl im kommenden Jahr dürfte Netanjahu geschäftsführend im Amt bleiben. TRUMP BEANSPRUCHT ANTEIL AN ERFOLG Netanjahu forderte in der Nacht vor Anhängern in Jerusalem die Bildung einer starken, rechtsgerichteten Regierung. Zudem hob er die jüngsten militärischen Erfolge Israels hervor und stellte eine engere Zusammenarbeit mit US-Präsident Donald Trump gegen den Iran in Aussicht. Israel stehe vor einer einmaligen historischen Chance, gemeinsam mit Trump die existenzielle Bedrohung durch den Iran ein für alle Mal zu beseitigen, sagte der 77-Jährige. Eigeninteressen dürften nicht von dieser Mission ablenken. Trump, der die Israelis aufgerufen hatte, Netanjahu im Amt zu halten, sagte bei einem Wahlkampfauftritt in Texas, dieser habe sehr gut abgeschnitten. Trump führte dies auch auf seine Unterstützung zurück. Eisenkot erklärte dagegen, die Wähler hätten Netanjahu eine Abfuhr erteilt, und rief den langjährigen Regierungschef zum Rückzug aus der Politik auf. Eisenkot warnte Netanjahu davor, die Sicherheit des Landes für politische Zwecke zu missbrauchen. Netanjahu sei ein geschäftsführender Ministerpräsident ohne Mandat oder das Vertrauen des Volkes, erklärte der 66-Jährige. An die Führung der Sicherheitsbehörden und des öffentlichen Dienstes appellierte er: "Widerstehen Sie jedem Versuch, Sie herauszufordern. Sie haben meine uneingeschränkte Unterstützung. Erinnern Sie sich daran, dass Sie nur dem Staat und den Interessen der israelischen Bürger dienen." HISTORISCH HOHE WAHLBETEILIGUNG Die Wahlbeteiligung lag mit 77,7 Prozent so hoch wie seit mehr als zwei Jahrzehnten nicht mehr. Besonders hoch war sie unter den arabischstämmigen Israelis, die mehr als ein Fünftel der Bevölkerung ausmachen. Viele wurden durch das mobilisiert, was sie als offenen Rassismus aus dem Kabinett Netanjahus betrachten. Das Bündnis mehrerer arabischer Parteien reagierte in seiner Zentrale in Nazareth mit Beifall auf die ersten Ergebnisse. "Wir lehnen die Besatzung und den Rassismus ab, und wir werden hier bleiben", sagte Faten Gattas von der Kandidatenliste des Bündnisses. Es war die erste Wahl seit dem Überraschungsangriff der Hamas am 7. Oktober 2023, bei dem 1200 Menschen getötet und 251 als Geiseln genommen wurden. Der Angriff löste einen Krieg Israels im Gazastreifen, mit der libanesischen Hisbollah-Miliz und mit dem Iran aus. Nach Angaben der Gesundheitsbehörden im Gazastreifen wurden bei der israelischen Offensive bislang mehr als 74.000 Palästinenser getötet. Der Krieg hat Israel international zunehmend isoliert. Der fortgesetzte Rückhalt für Netanjahu bei den meisten israelischen Juden verdeutlicht den Rechtsruck in der israelischen Gesellschaft. Die gemäßigte Linke ist zu einer Randerscheinung geworden. Fast alle jüdischen Parteien teilen mittlerweile Netanjahus Ablehnung eines unabhängigen palästinensischen Staates. Netanjahu selbst wird vom Internationalen Strafgerichtshof in Den Haag wegen mutmaßlicher Kriegsverbrechen gesucht und steht in Israel wegen Korruptionsvorwürfen vor Gericht, die er zurückweist.

item.title: HF Sinclair posts record quarterly profit, appoints new CEO
item.description: HF Sinclair on Wednesday reported a record quarterly profit, as elevated refining margins boosted earnings, and named Steve Ledbetter as its next CEO, effective January 1, sending its shares up nearly 5% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: HF Sinclair (DINO.N) on Wednesday reported a record quarterly profit, as elevated refining margins boosted earnings, and named Steve Ledbetter as its next CEO, effective January 1, sending its shares up nearly 5% in premarket trading. The appointment comes months after former CEO Timothy Go [USN:L4N41P16B TEXT:"departed"] under a mutually agreed separation agreement following nearly three months of voluntary leave during an internal review of HF Sinclair's disclosure processes. Board Chair Franklin Myers served as interim CEO and president since Go's departure. HF Sinclair is also preparing to separate its Lubricants & Specialties business into an independent publicly traded company. The Dallas, Texas-based company reported an adjusted profit of $11.75 per share, the highest ever, for the three months ended September 30, compared with analysts' average estimate of $7.65, according to data compiled by LSEG. US refiners have benefited from a surge in fuel exports since the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, which tightened global supplies and pushed refining margins sharply higher. The benchmark 3-2-1 crack spread , a key measure of refining profitability, more than doubled during the July-September quarter from a year earlier. The company's adjusted refinery gross margin per barrel stood at $54.22 in the third quarter, compared with $19.16 a year earlier. Sinclair's refining segment reported a quarterly adjusted core profit of $2.43 billion, compared with $476 million a year earlier.

item.title: UBS raises Brent outlook, sees oil at $110/bbl by end-2026
item.description: UBS on Thursday raised its forecast for Brent crude prices, expecting oil to remain elevated in the coming months as Middle Eastern supply stays vulnerable to disruptions amid geopolitical uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UBS on Thursday raised its forecast for Brent crude prices, expecting oil to remain elevated in the coming months as Middle Eastern supply stays vulnerable to disruptions amid geopolitical uncertainty. The bank now expects Brent crude to trade at $110 a barrel by the end of 2026, up from its previous forecast of $100. UBS raised its Brent forecast for March 2027 to $95 per barrel from $90, for June 2027 to $90 from $85 and for September 2027 to $85 from $80 "Uncertainty around our forecasts remains elevated, reflecting the unpredictable nature of the Middle East conflict, and the pace of recovery in Gulf production and global oil demand," the bank said in a note Middle Eastern crude loadings have recovered substantially from the severe disruption earlier this year, UBS said, but added that Gulf countries' crude and condensate port loadings remain below pre-conflict levels The bank also noted that October saw a record number of reported [USN:L8N4682UH TEXT:"attacks on vessels"] in and around the Strait of Hormuz, raising insurance and shipping costs Elevated shipping costs are supporting Brent prices, UBS said; Middle East-to-China very large crude carrier rates have jumped to $30-$40 a barrel from $1-$3 over the past decade due to longer voyages and tighter tanker availability Oil prices rose more than 1% on Wednesday, with Brent crude climbing above $115 a barrel, after an attack on a Saudi refinery

item.title: Eurovisión 2027 contará con 36 países, mientras Irlanda y Países Bajos se quedan fuera por Israel
item.description: Canadá debutará en Eurovisión junto con al menos otros 35 países en el concurso del próximo año, según informaron el miércoles los organizadores, mientras que Irlanda y Países Bajos lo boicotearán debido a la participación de Israel, y España, Eslovenia e Islandia aún no han confirmado su participación.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Canadá debutará en Eurovisión junto con al menos otros 35 países en el concurso del próximo año, según informaron el miércoles los organizadores, mientras que Irlanda y Países Bajos lo boicotearán debido a la participación de Israel, y España, Eslovenia e Islandia aún no han confirmado su participación. Las 36 cadenas enviarán su representante nacional a la 71.ª edición del concurso, que se celebrará en mayo en la ciudad búlgara de Burgas, un participante más que en 2026, según ha informado la Unión Europea de Radiodifusión (UER). España, Países Bajos, Irlanda, Islandia y Eslovenia boicotearon el concurso de este año —que atrajo a una audiencia mundial de 130 millones de espectadores— tras pedir la expulsión de Israel por su ofensiva militar en Gaza tras el ataque liderado por Hamás contra Israel el 7 de octubre de 2023. Israel afirmó en aquel momento que se estaba llevando a cabo una campaña de desprestigio global en su contra. La cadena israelí KAN confirmó su participación, mientras que Irlanda y Países Bajos han confirmado que volverán a ausentarse del concurso de 2027. RTVE en España y RTVSLO en Eslovenia tienen hasta diciembre para confirmar su participación, según ha indicado la UER. A finales de septiembre, el consejo de administración de la cadena pública islandesa RÚV señaló que era poco probable que participara, pero aún no ha tomado una decisión definitiva. "En un mundo que puede parecer cada vez más dividido, este certamen une a las audiencias a través de la música, más allá de las fronteras, los idiomas y las culturas, y eso es ahora más importante que nunca", dijo Martin Green, director del Festival de la Canción de Eurovisión, en un comunicado. Además de la debutante Canadá, el cartel del concurso incluye a Macedonia del Norte —que vuelve a la competición por primera vez desde 2022—, a la anfitriona Bulgaria, así como a Francia, Reino Unido, Ucrania y Australia.

item.title: US goods trade deficit unexpectedly widens in September
item.description: The US trade deficit in goods unexpectedly widened in September as imports increased, suggesting that trade again subtracted from economic growth in the third quarter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US trade deficit in goods unexpectedly widened in September as imports increased, suggesting that trade again subtracted from economic growth in the third quarter. The goods trade shortfall increased 2.1%, or $2.8 billion to $134.9 billion last month, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the goods deficit at $130.2 billion. Trade has not contributed to gross domestic product growth for three straight quarters as an AI investment boom pulls in imports, mostly capital goods. Goods imports rose $8.1 billion to $344.1 billion last month. Exports of goods climbed $5.3 billion to $209.2 billion. The government is scheduled to publish its advance estimate of third-quarter GDP on Thursday. A Reuters survey of economists forecast GDP increasing at a 3.2% annualized rate, with AI investment and consumer spending expected to be the key drivers. The economy grew at a 2.2% pace in the second quarter.

item.title: Irã vê apenas ideias inaceitáveis na mais recente mediação para encerrar guerra, diz autoridade
item.description: Mediadores do Catar apresentaram ao Irã uma nova proposta de acordo para pôr fim à guerra com EUA e Israel, afirmou uma autoridade a par das negociações, mas uma autoridade iraniana graduada disse que Doha havia apenas apresentado ideias inaceitáveis que não constituíam uma oferta.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills, Parisa Hafezi
item.content:encoded: Mediadores do Catar apresentaram ao Irã uma nova proposta de acordo para pôr fim à guerra com EUA e Israel, afirmou uma autoridade a par das negociações, mas uma autoridade iraniana graduada disse que Doha havia apenas apresentado ideias inaceitáveis que não constituíam uma oferta. A autoridade a par das negociações, que não é do Irã, disse que uma nova proposta de paz para o conflito, que já dura oito meses, foi apresentada no domingo e estava sendo analisada por Teerã, com uma resposta prevista para o final da semana. O Catar, juntamente com o Paquistão, tem liderado a mediação para pôr fim à guerra, que interrompeu o transporte marítimo global e o abastecimento de petróleo e, recentemente, se espalhou para Arábia Saudita e Iêmen. A proposta apresentada pelo Catar estabelece um cronograma de sete dias para abordar as preocupações tanto de Teerã quanto de Washington, definindo medidas diárias de construção de confiança que cada lado deve adotar, disse a autoridade informada sobre as negociações. O cronograma poderia começar no início da próxima semana e vários países atuariam como garantes do acordo, acrescentou a autoridade. Pouco depois, uma alta autoridade iraniana envolvida nas negociações afirmou que o Catar havia apresentado apenas “ideias inaceitáveis e não uma oferta”, e que a política de Teerã de não demonstrar flexibilidade em relação à questão nuclear permanecia inalterada. Washington quer que o programa nuclear iraniano faça parte das negociações para pôr fim à guerra desde o início, enquanto o Irã afirma que suas condições — que incluem o fim do bloqueio dos EUA aos portos iranianos e o levantamento das sanções às exportações de petróleo iraniano — devem ser atendidas primeiro. O Irã rejeita as preocupações ocidentais de que seu programa nuclear seja de natureza militar. No final de setembro, o Irã apresentou outra proposta de sete dias, segundo a qual o ministro das Relações Exteriores, Abbas Araqchi, afirmou que o Estreito de Ormuz, um dos canais de transporte de energia mais importantes do mundo, poderia ser reaberto se determinadas condições fossem atendidas. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, rejeitou a proposta, o que levou a uma nova mediação do Catar. O rascunho discutido em Teerã no domingo era diferente daquela proposta, disse a autoridade informada sobre as negociações, embora os detalhes do plano mais recente não tenham ficado claros imediatamente. A autoridade havia dito anteriormente à Reuters que os mediadores do Catar haviam se coordenado com Washington antes de irem a Teerã.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro segue para Miami após Trump oferecer saída do Brasil
item.description: O avião que supostamente transporta o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) e sua família para os Estados Unidos está programado para chegar na manhã de quarta-feira em Miami, onde eles receberão vistos de entrada do governo dos Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O avião que supostamente transporta o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) e sua família para os Estados Unidos está programado para chegar na manhã de quarta-feira em Miami, onde eles receberão vistos de entrada do governo dos Estados Unidos. Enquanto o mundo inteiro tentava descobrir onde ele estava, Flávio Bolsonaro entrou na Argentina com sua esposa e duas filhas na noite de terça-feira, segundo o departamento de imigração do país. Flávio, que perdeu a eleição presidencial de domingo para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e se recusou a cumprir ordem do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para entregar seus passaportes, cruzou a fronteira com a Argentina pela Ponte Internacional Tancredo Neves, a cerca de 19 horas de viagem de carro de sua casa em Brasília. A determinação de entrega de passaportes do senador se deu no âmbito de um inquérito em que ele é investigado por lavagem de dinheiro e após seu irmão, o ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, afirmar em uma transmissão nas redes sociais que Flávio deveria sair do Brasil caso perdesse a eleição. Na segunda, em vídeo publicado em sua conta no Instagram, Flávio negou ter a intenção de sair do país, disse que entregaria os passaportes à Polícia Federal e que organizaria a oposição ao governo Lula. Flávio e família embarcaram em um avião particular operado pela Baires Fly S.A. com destino à cidade equatoriana de Guayaquil, informou o departamento de imigração argentino. A Presidência da Argentina não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. A Baires Fly também não se pronunciou. Um Gulfstream G400 operado pela Baires Fly, com matrícula LV-JQW, decolou de Puerto Iguazú às 00h22 e pousou em Guayaquil às 03h46, segundo o FlightAware. A aeronave partiu em seguida para o Aeroporto Executivo de Opa-locka, em Miami, onde estava programada para pousar às 9h18 no horário local (10h18 de Brasília). NOVA RUPTURA ENTRE BRASIL E EUA A saída de Flávio Bolsonaro ameaça aprofundar uma ruptura entre as duas nações mais populosas das Américas. Lula acusou Washington de conluio com a família Bolsonaro para ajudá-la a retornar ao poder. Antes da eleição de domingo, a Reuters noticiou uma campanha do Departamento de Estado dos EUA para recolocar os Bolsonaros no poder. Trump disse a repórteres nesta quarta-feira que aprovaria a ida de Flávio aos Estados Unidos, depois que seu Departamento de Estado afirmou que concederia vistos de entrada à família. Trump já havia alegado anteriormente que o pai de Flávio, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, foi vítima de perseguição judicial no Brasil. Jair Bolsonaro também viajou para os Estados Unidos após se recusar a reconhecer a derrota para Lula em 2022, durante a Presidência de Joe Biden. Ele acabou voltando, e mais tarde foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por planejar um golpe de Estado depois que seus apoiadores invadiram e depredaram as sedes dos Três Poderes em Brasília. Flávio, que era o favorito para vencer a eleição presidencial de domingo, perderá sua imunidade parlamentar quando seu mandato no Senado terminar em fevereiro. (Por Gabriel Stargardter; reportagem adicional de Alexandra Valencia, em Quito; Gabriel Araujo, em São Paulo, e Maximilian Heath, em Buenos Aires)

item.title: Frontier Airlines forecasts smaller-than-expected quarterly loss after surprise profit
item.description: Frontier Airlines on Wednesday forecast a smaller-than-expected fourth-quarter loss and reported a surprise profit for the third quarter, as elevated airfares helped soften the hit from sky-high fuel prices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Frontier Airlines (ULCC.O) on Wednesday forecast a smaller-than-expected fourth-quarter loss and reported a surprise profit for the third quarter, as elevated airfares helped soften the hit from sky-high fuel prices. Shares of the company climbed 2.5% in premarket trading. The Denver-based airline expects adjusted earnings per share between a loss of 15 cents and a profit of 5 cents in the October-December quarter. The midpoint, a 5-cent loss, is slightly narrower than the 6-cent loss analysts had expected, per data compiled by LSEG. Frontier, like most airlines, has relied on fare hikes, capacity cuts and additional fees, including charges for checked bags, in a bid to recover higher jet fuel cost. The airline has also worked to cut costs by returning some leased aircraft and looked to boost revenue by introducing first-class seating and Starlink internet, while also improving loyalty income. It reported a third-quarter adjusted profit of 18 cents per share, compared to a year-ago loss of 34 cents. Analysts had expected a loss of 4 cents per share. Quarterly revenue came in at an all-time high of $1.36 billion, led by unit revenue that grew 30%, and was above estimates of $1.29 billion.

item.title: UK budget: Healey accepts smaller fiscal buffer after global shocks hit economy
item.description: British finance minister John Healey on Wednesday started to set out the government's latest tax and spending measures in his first budget, seeking to boost economic growth while maintaining control of the public finances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey on Wednesday started to set out the government's latest tax and spending measures in [USN:L2N46E09X TEXT:"his first budget"], seeking to boost economic growth while maintaining control of the public finances. Below are quotes from Healey: HEALEY'S FIRST WORDS "This is a budget for the working people of Britain, for British businesses, big and small, delivered at a time when global uncertainties and pressures are swirling worldwide and hitting people here at home. A budget built on fiscal discipline, which matches immediate action today, with clear direction for the future." GLOBAL ECONOMIC STORMS "Analysts like to speak of economic headwinds. But what we face today are global economic storms with trade tensions acting as a drag on global growth, and (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's illegal invasion of Ukraine approaching the end of its fifth year." "The OBR sets out that the war in the Middle East is a key driver affecting today's forecasts. And this government continues to work with our allies to end the conflict and restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz." "In the budget today, I have chosen to use some of the headroom established last year to absorb the impact of the Iran war to protect the economy, and to protect family budgets." FISCAL HEADROOM AND BORROWING "The OBR confirms today that headroom against the stability rule is £15 billion in 2029/30, before rising to £22 billion in 2030/31." "That's what a buffer is for. Use it when you need it. Rebuild it when you can. And so, despite the global challenges, this budget puts us on track to eliminate the current budget deficit and get Britain’s finances into the black within 3 years." "In today's forecast, borrowing falls to 4.2% this year, 3.4% next year, 2.9% in 2028/29, 2.1% in 2029/30, and 1.8% in 2030/31 and 2031/32." DEBT "Our debt as a percentage of GDP is 83.2% this year, 83.8% next year and in 2028/29, before falling to 83.1% in 2029/30, 82.3% in 2030/31 and 81.7% in 2031/32." ECONOMIC GROWTH "Three months ago, the Bank of England upgraded their forecasts for growth this year. Two weeks ago, the IMF did the same." "And today, the OBR has upgraded its forecast too – to 1.2% this year. Followed by 1% next year, 1.6% in 2028, 1.8% in 2029, 1.7% in 2030 and 1.6% in 2031." "Yes, there are real challenges ahead, but Britain has beaten the forecasts this year, and with the action I'm taking today, I believe Britain can beat them again." HOUSEHOLD BILLS "We will introduce a new cost control framework to drive down all aspects of energy bills, and I will scrap the upcoming Gas Shipper Obligation – a levy to fund hydrogen projects – and instead back those projects directly from government." "First, on clean power generation, this government will only buy and build new projects when they lower bills and when they can connect to the grid." "Second, we will break the grip of international gas prices on our bills by moving more of our old renewables onto fixed-price contracts." "And third, we will build cheaper, faster grid connections through GB Grid, and reform the complex web of institutions that govern them." "This winter, for 20 million households in council tax bands A-D, I am announcing a £100 'Household Energy Payment'. Paid directly into people's bank accounts to help deal with rising energy bills, a £2.6 billion scheme, to take the pressure off in the coldest months and see people through to the Spring." NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE "For 2.3 million of our lowest paid workers, I am increasing both the National Minimum Wage and the National Living Wage by 3.9%." BANK SURCHARGE "I am looking to our banks to help fund breathing space for British families. And so banks will pay an extra 3% on the Bank Surcharge. This will be time-limited, to pay for immediate support on energy bills, starting in January, ending 15 months later." TAXES "I am raising taxes on gambling – by increasing Machine Games Duty from 20% to 25% for higher stakes machines, while protecting pubs and seaside arcades." "I will carve out adult gaming centres and vape shops from business rate reliefs, and extend the business rates Transitional Relief Supplement for a further two years, and I will strengthen the requirements for online marketplaces so that sellers cannot avoid paying VAT when they sell online." "For those who feel like celebrating tax cuts for our high streets - I'm providing a £10m alcohol duty relief for around 2000 small British brewers and cider makers." REFORM TO TAX SYSTEM "First, I am giving HMRC funding to improve compliance, and stronger powers to collect overdue tax from those who can clearly afford to pay, but ignore repeated contact. And I am reforming the administration of self-assessed income tax from 2029, bringing more of these taxpayers in line with the majority." "Second, I am changing outdated rules so that people taking profits out of their companies are taxed consistently, and I will protect the treatment of genuine commercial transactions and families passing their businesses down to the next generation." "Third, I am modernising the tax treatment of investment by foreign sovereigns." "And fourth, I will resolve the question of VAT for larger taxi companies, ensuring they play by the same rules, no matter where they are located, while still protecting smaller local firms." INVESTMENT "I'm boosting investment through our Public Financial Institutions – a further £20.4 billion for the National Wealth Fund and the British Business Bank over the coming years, supporting 140,000 jobs." "And I will work with pension providers, asset managers and the wider industry to accelerate more private investment into Britain’s innovative, fast-growth firms." DATA CENTRE COVENANT "I am today launching a new British Data Centre Covenant with strict tests that data centres must meet: to invest in local communities, create local jobs and protect local water supplies." "In return, critical data centres will get the grid connections they need, and, where necessary, be allowed to build onsite generation while they wait."

item.title: Spurs gaining momentum, ready for Jazz
item.description: The San Antonio Spurs have hit the .500 mark and are ready to put their shaky season start behind them when they meet the injury-plagued Utah Jazz in Salt Lake City on Wednesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The San Antonio Spurs have hit the .500 mark and are ready to put their shaky season start behind them when they meet the injury-plagued Utah Jazz in Salt Lake City on Wednesday night. After advancing to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs opened the new campaign with back-to-back losses. But on Tuesday, San Antonio rode an 80-point first half and a blistering shooting night from Julian Champagnie to a 130-103 home win over the Sacramento Kings. Victor Wembanyama, who mirrored his team's patchy early form -- averaging a career-low 20 points on 36.5% shooting from the field in the first three games -- was back to his best against Sacramento, compiling a game-high 29 points on a 14-of-21 clip, with 10 rebounds and five blocks in less than 27 minutes. But the real spark came from Champagnie, who scored 24 of his 26 points in the first half. His entire first-half tally came from 3-point makes (eight), tying his own franchise record for most threes in a half. "Sizable," Champagnie said, laughing, when asked how big the basket looked as he drained 8-of-10 3-point attempts in the first two quarters. "My teammates did a really good job of getting me open and finding where I'm at on the court. I always give credit to them. Without them, I'm not making those shots." Spurs coach Mitch Johnson praised his team's ball movement -- San Antonio had 35 assists to 13 turnovers -- which allowed Champagnie to capitalize on a string of open looks against the Kings. "I thought our team did a good job of recognizing where he (Champagnie) was once he got going," Johnson said. "We've had some times in the last few years when I think we've done a poor job of that, and not intentionally. We've grown in that aspect a little bit, and (Tuesday) was an example of that." While the Spurs appear to be hitting their stride, the Jazz were left to count the cost of two key injuries in Monday's 110-105 home defeat to the Memphis Grizzlies. Lauri Markkanen exited the game early in the first quarter with a right wrist injury, and Jaren Jackson Jr. went off with a right knee injury in the second period. That's two of Utah's top three scorers this season. Markkanen and Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) are questionable to face San Antonio. Jackson appeared in three games for the Jazz last season due to an injury to his other knee after being acquired in a trade from Memphis. He is expected to be sidelined for six to eight weeks after scans revealed he suffered a torn MCL vs. Memphis. The other member of Utah's big three -- Keyonte George -- scored 26 points as the Jazz's patched-up lineup fought valiantly against the undefeated Grizzlies. "I thought that was an awesome showing," Utah coach Will Hardy said. "I'm so proud of the group, the way they fought. ... I think the competitiveness of the team, the way they came together, speaks to the character of the group." Center Mo Bamba rose in the Jazz's time of need, hustling his way to 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks off the bench in his first game of the season. "It's just my job," he said. "A wise man in this organization told me to treat every game like Game 7, every possession like Game 7. "We have a lot of talent in this locker room. It (stinks) that our big names are down for however long they're going to be down for. It's just next man up." --Field Level Media

item.title: Europe's bank trading clean-up has further to go
item.description: Shares in investment banking-heavy Barclays and €55 bln Deutsche are lagging peers. Both are seeking to boost profitability or lighten the load of their volatile businesses. And while they are making progress, it’s an uneven and long journey, implying a lingering discount.
item.dc:creator: Neil Unmack
item.content:encoded: Shares in investment banking-heavy Barclays and €55 bln Deutsche are lagging peers. Both are seeking to boost profitability or lighten the load of their volatile businesses. And while they are making progress, it’s an uneven and long journey, implying a lingering discount. Full view will be published shortly. Follow @Unmack1 on X Deutsche Bank on October 28 reported a 4% year-on-year increase in revenue, boosted in particular by a turnaround in its corporate bank. Revenue at the investment bank fell 2% year-on-year to €2.92 billion in the third quarter, while the top line at the corporate bank and private bank rose 9% and 8% respectively. Barclays on October 22 reported a 3% increase in income to £7.4 billion. Income in the investment bank rose 1% year-on-year, despite a 19% decline in fixed-income and currencies markets business. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: RC Lens ban own fans from attending Lille match
item.description: RC Lens have banned their fans from travelling to Lille for Friday's Ligue 1 clash, punishing them for lighting and throwing pyrotechnics during a Champions League match at Club Brugge, the French club said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RC Lens have banned their fans from travelling to Lille for Friday's Ligue 1 clash, punishing them for lighting and throwing pyrotechnics during a Champions League match at Club Brugge, the French club said on Wednesday. "Following the incidents that occurred in Bruges on Matchday 3 of the Champions League, RC Lens informed all supporters' groups on Monday of its decision not to open the away section in Lille," Lens said in a statement. Lens added that the acts committed involved "dangerous and hostile pyrotechnics" and that "a red line has been crossed". UEFA's Appeals body on Tuesday ordered Lens not to sell tickets to their supporters for the next two Champions League matches, against Leipzig and Liverpool. French authorities also banned Lens fans from travelling to Lille for the northern derby.

item.title: Wendy's gets $1.4 billion buyout offer from Peltz's Trian
item.description: Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has offered to take Wendy's private in a deal valuing the burger chain at about $1.4 billion, a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has offered to take Wendy's (WEN.O) private in a deal valuing the burger chain at about $1.4 billion, a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday. Trian, a longtime Wendy's shareholder, is leading a group that has offered $7.35 per share in cash for the fast-food chain. The offer represents a roughly 20% premium to Wendy's closing price on Tuesday, when the company had a market value of about $1.2 billion. The news was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Drones impactan contra otro buque portacontenedores frente a las costas de Bulgaria: ministro
item.description: Unos drones marítimos atacaron el miércoles un buque portacontenedores frente a la costa búlgara del mar Negro, según afirmó el ministro de Defensa, Dimitar Stoyanov, en lo que supone el último de una serie de acciones que han suscitado temores sobre la creciente magnitud de la guerra de Rusia en Ucrania.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Unos drones marítimos atacaron el miércoles un buque portacontenedores frente a la costa búlgara del mar Negro, según afirmó el ministro de Defensa, Dimitar Stoyanov, en lo que supone el último de una serie de acciones que han suscitado temores sobre la creciente magnitud de la guerra de Rusia en Ucrania. No quedó claro quién llevó a cabo el ataque contra un buque portacontenedores griego que navegaba bajo pabellón liberiano en la zona económica exclusiva de Bulgaria. Una fuente de seguridad marítima con conocimiento del asunto afirmó que la tripulación fue evacuada. La radio nacional búlgara informó de que se había enviado un buque cisterna para prestar asistencia a la embarcación dañada, que se dirigía desde el puerto israelí de Haifa a Constanza, en Rumanía. Contships Management, la empresa con sede en Grecia propietaria y gestora del buque, no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. "Un buque portacontenedores fue alcanzado (…) por tres drones navales, aproximadamente a 21 millas al sureste de Shabla", declaró Stoyanov a la prensa en los márgenes de una reunión sobre seguridad regional. Los ataques con drones contra buques mercantes frente a las costas de Bulgaria han causado probablemente la muerte de dos decenas de marineros internacionales en las últimas semanas. Al menos seis buques mercantes han sido atacados. Los ataques, que han suscitado la condena internacional y la preocupación por el creciente alcance de la guerra en Ucrania, han llevado a Bulgaria —miembro de la Unión Europea y de la OTAN— a solicitar la ayuda de sus aliados para reforzar la seguridad marítima en esta región inestable. Ucrania ha achacado los ataques a Rusia, y el primer ministro búlgaro, Rumen Radev, ha afirmado que los ataques parecen beneficiar a Rusia, aunque Moscú ha negado cualquier implicación.

item.title: CVC, Cinven y Puig se interesan por la firma de perfumes de lujo Parfums de Marly, según fuentes
item.description: Las firmas de capital riesgo CVC Capital Partners y Cinven, junto con la empresa española de cosmética Puig , se encuentran entre los interesados en adquirir Parfums de Marly, la marca de fragancias de lujo propiedad de Advent International, han informado a Reuters dos personas con conocimiento del asunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las firmas de capital riesgo CVC Capital Partners (CVC.AS) y Cinven, junto con la empresa española de cosmética Puig (PUIGb.MC) , se encuentran entre los interesados en adquirir Parfums de Marly, la marca de fragancias de lujo propiedad de Advent International, han informado a Reuters dos personas con conocimiento del asunto. Un acuerdo pondría de manifiesto el interés constante por las marcas de fragancias de alta gama, uno de los sectores de más rápido crecimiento del mercado de la belleza. Advent, que adquirió Parfums de Marly en 2023, está barajando ahora una posible venta del negocio, según estas fuentes. Puig se considera actualmente menos activo en el proceso que algunos de sus competidores, añadió una de ellas. Una de las fuentes señaló que la empresa podría valorarse en menos de 2.000 millones de euros (2.230 millones de dólares). Las negociaciones siguen en curso y no hay certeza de que se llegue a un acuerdo. Los portavoces de CVC, Cinven, Puig y Advent se negaron a hacer comentarios. Parfums de Marly no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Fundada en 2009, Parfums de Marly comercializa fragancias inspiradas en la perfumería francesa del siglo XVIII, con aromas como Layton, Delina y Valaya. El precio de los frascos suele rondar los 250 euros o más. (1 dólar = 0,8961 euros)

item.title: Ethiopia says it has taken delivery of 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets
item.description: Ethiopia has taken delivery of 12 Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets and will later receive four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow as part of a drive to bolster its military capabilities, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ethiopia has taken delivery of 12 Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets and will later receive four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow as part of a drive to bolster its military capabilities, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said on Wednesday. Abiy said on X that the deliveries marked a milestone in Ethiopia's efforts to strengthen national security and "pre-emptively deter aggression" He said Russian President Vladimir Putin had helped ensure the fourth-generation Su-35 military planes were delivered a year earlier than scheduled Abiy did not disclose the value of the agreement, when the S-400 systems would be delivered or where the aircraft and air defence batteries would be based Ethiopia faces multiple security challenges, including in the northern Tigray region, where a rebel alliance last month launched [USN:L8N4620IC TEXT:"an offensive"] against the government, rekindling a war that killed hundreds of thousands of people between 2020 and 2022 In the previous conflict, its air power — especially through the widespread deployment of foreign-made drones — [USN:L6N45G0H1 TEXT:"helped turn the tide"] of the fighting The renewed fighting led to the severing of ties between Ethiopia and its neighbour Eritrea, which Addis Ababa accuses of backing the rebels, although Asmara denies that Russian state-owned defence conglomerate Rostec, responsible for Russian arms exports, did not immediately respond to a request for comment

item.title: PetroChina's Q3 net profit up 21.6% on year
item.description: Asia's largest oil and gas producer, PetroChina , reported a 21.6% year-on-year increase third-quarter net profit, driven by higher oil and gas prices, according to a stock filing on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Asia's largest oil and gas producer, PetroChina (601857.SS) , reported a 21.6% year-on-year increase third-quarter net profit, driven by higher oil and gas prices, according to a stock filing on Wednesday. Net income for the July-September period totalled 51.84 billion yuan ($7.78 billion), compared with 42.29 billion yuan a year earlier. Net profit for the first three quarters was up 21.9% year-on-year at 155.78 billion yuan. Revenue grew 7% to 2.32 trillion yuan. In the first nine months, PetroChina produced 698.6 million barrels of crude oil (2.56 million barrels per day), down 2.2% year-on-year, including 590.4 million barrels produced domestically. Refinery throughput during the 9-month period fell 3.7% on year at 1,002.2 million barrels, or 3.67 million bpd. Ethylene output grew 26.4% during the 9-month period at 8.46 million tons. Marketable natural gas output rose 2.3% to 4,069.4 billion cubic feet during the period, including 3,947.2 billion cubic feet produced in China. Domestic natural gas sales rose 1% at 178.7 billion cubic meters Sales of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel combined were down 5.1% on the year at 114.66 million tons. These included 84.52 million tons sold domestically, which was down 5.7%. Domestic diesel sales fell 8.2% and gasoline down 4.3%. Aviation fuel edged up 1.1%. Nine-month capital expenditure totalled 159.4 billion yuan, compared with 177.5 billion yuan a year earlier. ($1 = 6.6666 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: 36 countries to compete in Eurovision 2027 as Ireland, Netherlands stay out over Israel
item.description: Canada will make its Eurovision debut alongside at least 35 other countries at next year's contest, organisers said on Wednesday, with Ireland and the Netherlands boycotting over Israel's participation, and Spain, Slovenia and Iceland still to announce.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Canada will make its Eurovision debut alongside at least 35 other countries at next year's contest, organisers said on Wednesday, with Ireland and the Netherlands boycotting over Israel's participation, and Spain, Slovenia and Iceland still to announce. The 36 broadcasters will send their national entry to the 71st edition of the contest in the Bulgarian city of Burgas in May, one participant more than in 2026, the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) said Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Iceland and Slovenia boycotted this year's contest, which drew a global audience of 130 million, after calling for Israel's expulsion over its military offensive in Gaza following the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023. Israel said at the time there was a global smear campaign against it Israel's KAN broadcaster has confirmed its participation, while [USN:SPN44W013 TEXT:"Ireland"] and [USN:SPN44W013 TEXT:"the Netherlands"] have confirmed they will again skip the 2027 contest RTVE in Spain and RTVSLO in Slovenia have until December to confirm, the EBU said. At the end of September, the board of Iceland's public broadcaster RÚV signalled its participation was unlikely but has not made a final decision "In a world that can feel increasingly divided, it brings audiences together through music, across borders, languages and cultures, and that matters now more than ever," said Martin Green, director of the Eurovision Song Contest, in a statement Apart from [USN:L6N4330SA TEXT:"newcomer Canada"], the contest lineup includes North Macedonia — which returns to the competition for the first time since 2022 — host Bulgaria, and France, Britain, Ukraine and Australia

item.title: Second-half show keeps Kashima perfect in Asian Champions League
item.description: Kashima Antlers scored three second-half goals to beat Pohang Steelers 3-0 defeat in the eastern league phase of the Asian Champions League Elite as the Japanese side maintained their perfect start to the competition.
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Kashima Antlers scored three second-half goals to beat Pohang Steelers 3-0 defeat in the eastern league phase of the Asian Champions League Elite as the Japanese side maintained their perfect start to the competition. Ryuta Koike, Aleksandar Cavric and Matheus Bueno netted in the final 21 minutes for Toru Oniki's side, who joined fellow J-League side Vissel Kobe on nine points from three matches. "Our most important goal as a team was to make it three consecutive wins in the Asian Champions League," Koike said. "Recently, we haven’t been able to win matches at home, and things haven't been going well in the league." Koike broke Pohang's resistance in the 69th minute, redirecting Buenos' centre past goalkeeper Hwang In-jae with an improvised finish off his chest. Cavric doubled the lead when he scored at the second attempt having seen his initial shot hit the post and Bueno completed the scoring from close range two minutes from time. Kashima and Kobe are the only teams with perfect records remaining in the eastern side of the draw after Gamba Osaka were held to a 1-1 draw by Thailand's Buriram United. The visitors took the lead when Eduardo Mancha netted just before the interval and Gamba's Takashi Usami equalised after 66 minutes. "I'm proud of my team, to come to Japan and perform like that was impressive," said Buriram captain Kenny Dougall. "When you take the lead and don't win it's always a bit disappointing but we have another game next week." The top eight finishers in the 16-team leagues in both east and west Asia will advance to the last 16 in March while the quarter-finals, semi-final and final will be played on a centralised basis in Saudi Arabia in April and May.

item.title: La RFEF aplaza 24 partidos de la Copa del Rey tras el accidente ferroviario en España
item.description: La Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) aplazó los 24 partidos de la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey previstos para el miércoles tras una colisión de trenes en la provincia de Toledo que dejó al menos 30 muertos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) aplazó los 24 partidos de la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey previstos para el miércoles tras una [USN:L6N46E0J7 TEXT:"colisión de trenes"] en la provincia de Toledo que dejó al menos 30 muertos. Al menos 30 personas murieron al chocar dos trenes de alta velocidad, en el [USN:L6N46E0R7 TEXT:"segundo accidente"] mortal en menos de un año en la línea que conecta Madrid con Andalucía, en el sur de España. Los partidos se aplazaron "como muestra de respeto y solidaridad con todas las víctimas", dijo la RFEF, que añadió que las nuevas fechas de los encuentros se anunciarán próximamente. El accidente interrumpió los servicios ferroviarios entre Madrid y Andalucía, lo que afectó a los desplazamientos de varios equipos y sus aficionados.

item.title: Iranians cut essentials and put dreams on hold as war-hit economy bites
item.description: Iranian families are cutting back on food, housing and education as the eight-month-old war with the United States fuels one of the country's worst inflation surges in decades, eroding incomes and pushing households to the brink.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Hafezi
item.content:encoded: Iranian families are cutting back on food, housing and education as the eight-month-old war with the United States fuels one of the country's worst inflation surges in decades, eroding incomes and pushing households to the brink. The strain is being felt far beyond the country's major cities. Workers say wages no longer cover basic expenses, while businesses face rising costs and weakening demand as families spend most of their budgets on food, rent and other necessities. The conflict, triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 and followed by Tehran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and a US blockade of Iranian ports in the Gulf, has disrupted oil exports, trade and government revenues. The turmoil has compounded the impact of decades of sanctions and economic mismanagement. Reuters spoke to more than two dozen people across Iran from different social and economic backgrounds who said worsening conditions had left them struggling to afford food, housing, healthcare and education. "We have no money, no future and no hope. We're tired of living in fear, fear of another US attack and fear of not being able to make ends meet at the end of every month," said Mohammadali, a 47-year-old shopkeeper and father of two in the northeastern city of Mashhad. Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh on Tuesday apologised for the mounting cost-of-living pressures facing Iranians, state media reported, saying pensioners, workers and civil servants were bearing the brunt of soaring prices and high inflation. Iran's inflation surge has shown little sign of easing. Consumer prices in September were nearly 90% higher than a year earlier, while annual inflation accelerated to 73.6%, according to official data and figures reported by state media. Food prices have risen even faster. The cost of food and beverages was 121.8% higher than a year ago, forcing many families to cut spending elsewhere. PRICES OUTPACE PAYCHECKS, JOBS DRY UP For Mahmoud, a 44-year-old government employee in the central city of Isfahan, the gap between wages and living costs widens every month. "With my salary of less than $100, you can survive only for 10 days ... My wife and I lie to our daughters all the time when they ask for a toy or new clothes," he said. Official estimates put the minimum monthly cost of living for a three-person working-class family at around $336, more than three times the average monthly wage of roughly $92 at the free-market exchange rate. As wages fail to keep pace with inflation, many families have exhausted savings, cut consumption or borrowed money to cover daily expenses. Government-mandated pay increases have been swiftly overtaken by rising prices. For many Iranians, the challenge is no longer preserving their standard of living but avoiding financial collapse. "We had to move to my parents' house last month because my husband got laid off from a small tile factory in May. We spent all our savings. But my husband is still jobless and we could no longer afford rent," said Hamideh, a 39-year-old mother of two in the northern city of Rasht. Rising housing costs have added to the squeeze on family budgets. Rents in September were 32.8% higher than a year earlier, while housing, utilities and fuel costs were up nearly 38%, according to official data. The pressure extends to the labour market. The official unemployment rate climbed to 9.1% in the spring, up 1.8 percentage points from a year earlier. The economic participation rate fell to 40.7%, indicating fewer working-age Iranians were employed or actively seeking work. Nearly a quarter of young people aged 15 to 24 are unemployed. "I have been looking for work since graduating in advertising, but after months of searching I've started to lose hope. Companies are cutting budgets, not hiring. Most of my classmates are either unemployed or working in fields unrelated to what they studied," said 23-year-old Firouzeh, who lives with her parents in the northwestern city of Urmia. STUDYING ABROAD A DISTANT DREAM The [USN:L1N45P04X TEXT:"weakening rial"] is also closing off opportunities once seen as pathways to upward mobility. Iran's currency has lost more than half its value over the past year, putting overseas education beyond the reach of many families. "Both my parents are government employees. Their dream was to send me abroad to become a medical doctor. But after two years studying in Turkey, I could not pay the tuition for this year and I am returning home," said Shahriyar, 25, in Istanbul. He said several of his friends were in the same situation. Washington's expanded sanctions, announced on August 24 as part of "Operation Economic Outcast" and aimed at cutting Tehran's funding for the war, have added to the economic strain on ordinary Iranians, analysts said. Businesses are under pressure. Sanctions and war-related disruptions have increased the cost of imports and restricted access to foreign currency and raw materials, while retailers and small businesses face higher operating costs just as demand weakens, threatening revenues and jobs. For Iran's rulers, the challenge is maintaining essential imports and public services while financing a costly conflict. Central Bank Governor Abdolnasser Hemmati said in mid-October that US claims Iran's economy was collapsing were "an illusion". The deterioration in living standards also presents a growing political challenge for the authorities, who remain wary that worsening economic conditions could reignite nationwide unrest. Economic grievances have fuelled repeated waves of protests in recent years, leaving officials sensitive to signs that war, inflation and rising unemployment are further eroding public patience. The clerical establishment responded to previous outbreaks of unrest with a sweeping crackdown that, according to Iranian officials and rights groups, [USN:L8N3YK1DJ TEXT:"killed thousands"] in January.

item.title: Geron discontinues late-stage trial of blood cancer drug
item.description: Geron said on Wednesday it would halt a late-stage trial of its treatment for a rare blood cancer, sending the drugmaker's shares down 9% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Geron (GERN.O) said on Wednesday it would halt a late-stage trial of its treatment for a rare blood cancer, sending the drugmaker's shares down 9% in premarket trading. The drug, branded as Rytelo, was being evaluated as a treatment for myelofibrosis, a rare type of blood cancer in which scar tissue gradually builds up in the bone marrow. Geron said it made the decision following an independent data monitoring committee's recommendation that the trial was unlikely to achieve its main goal of overall survival, compared to the best available therapy. Geron said a detailed analysis of the data will be conducted, and study findings will be shared at a future date. The trial enrolled 327 patients with high-risk myelofibrosis whose disease had returned or failed to respond after treatment with a JAK inhibitor, a type of drug used to manage symptoms and reduce spleen enlargement. "As we fully analyze the data from the IMpactMF trial, we remain committed to growing Rytelo demand in the US and broadening access to eligible patients outside the US," CEO Harout Semerjian said. Rytelo received US approval in 2024 for treating transfusion-dependent anemia in patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a group of blood cancers. The drug, Geron's only commercial product, competes with Bristol Myers Squibb's (BMY.N) Reblozyl. In the second quarter, Rytelo brought in $57.5 million in revenue.

Oct 28 : Puerto Rico's seven-division world champion Amanda Serrano will retire after defending her unified featherweight world titles against Australia's Skye Falzon on home soil, in a fight her promoter dubbed "The Last Walk". Most Valuable Promotions said Serrano, who holds a 50–4–1 record with 32 knockouts, will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight world titles on January 9 at Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan. Puerto Rico's only undisputed boxing champion is also gunning for the all-time women's knockout record which the 38-year-old jointly shares with American Christy Martin. "Boxing has been my life and I never could have imagined the journey it would take me and my family on," Serrano said in a statement.

"From the early days when women's boxing was fighting for recognition in small theatre shows, to headlining Madison Square Garden in New York, reaching millions of fans around the world on the biggest shows, and helping open doors for the next generation of female fighters... I always believed and I'm proud of everything we've accomplished." Serrano made history alongside Ireland's Katie Taylor in 2022 when they became the first women boxers to headline New York's Madison Square Garden. The highest-profile rivalry in women's boxing produced a trilogy of fights which Taylor swept via a majority decision in 2025. A Guinness World Record holder for winning titles across seven weight divisions, Serrano also became a leading voice for equality in women's boxing. In 2023, she competed in the first women's unified world championship bout over 12 three-minute rounds, later voluntarily vacating her WBC title rather than abandon her commitment to equal rules. "'The Last Walk' is a celebration of an athlete who changed the sport forever... We're proud to give Amanda the farewell she deserves," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, founders of Most Valuable Promotions. "Saturday, January 9, will mark the end of an extraordinary career inside the ring, but Amanda's legacy will live on through every female fighter who follows in her footsteps." Falzon, who is also 38, holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts.

item.title: Bombardier, UK's BAE explore partnership for future combat aircraft programs
item.description: Canadian business jet maker Bombardier said on Wednesday it had signed a strategic agreement with BAE Systems to explore opportunities to develop industrial and technology capabilities for future combat air programmes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian business jet maker Bombardier (BBDb.TO) said on Wednesday it had signed a strategic agreement with BAE Systems (BAES.L) to explore opportunities to develop industrial and technology capabilities for future combat air programmes. Under the memorandum of understanding, the companies will assess opportunities in research and development, systems integration, workforce and supply-chain development, industrialisation and lifecycle support as Canada deepens its involvement in next-generation combat air initiatives. The agreement underscores Bombardier's push to expand its defence aerospace business. CEO Éric Martel said earlier this year the company saw growing opportunities for its defence unit, which converts business jets into special-mission aircraft, as Canada and Europe boost military spending and seek to diversify away from US defence firms amid geopolitical tensions. Bombardier's agreement with BAE comes months after Canada joined the Global Combat Air Programme, or GCAP, as an observer. Britain, Italy and Japan launched GCAP in 2022 to develop a next-generation stealth fighter by 2035. The programme is led by Britain's BAE Systems, Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (7011.T) and Italy's Leonardo (LDOF.MI) . The Financial Times reported last week that Airbus (AIR.PA) executives were [USN:L6N46B02Z TEXT:"set to meet"] BAE Systems counterparts to discuss the European planemaker's potential participation in GCAP, citing people familiar with the matter.

Oct 28 : Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase is adding Ripple's stablecoin RLUSD to its platform, expanding its slate of dollar-backed crypto tokens.  The move is a boost for blockchain payments company Ripple, which launched RLUSD in December 2024 to facilitate near-instant settlement of cross-border payments. The stablecoin has a market capitalization of more than $2.5 billion, according to data provider CoinGecko.  RLUSD will be available starting Wednesday across Coinbase's retail and institutional platforms, Coinbase said. For years, Circle's USDC was the flagship stablecoin Coinbase offered to its customers, but Coinbase has gradually expanded its stablecoin offerings to include PayPal's PYUSD, as well as Open USD, a stablecoin issued through a joint venture backed by Visa, Mastercard and Coinbase.   "It's a really credentializing moment for RLUSD to not only be listed on Coinbase but to be embraced across the platform," said Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple.  Stablecoins are digital tokens designed to keep a constant value and backed by traditional currencies, most commonly the US dollar. They are used mainly to trade in and out of other cryptocurrencies, such as bitcoin, but proponents say they can also facilitate instant payments and corporate treasury management.
