item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro expected to land in Miami shortly after Trump offers Brazil exit
item.description: The plane believed to be carrying Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family to the United States was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday morning in Miami, where they will be given entry visas by the United States government.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The plane believed to be carrying Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family to the United States was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday morning in Miami, where they will be given entry visas by the United States government. With the whole world [USN:L6N46D0VK TEXT:"trying to work out where he was"], Bolsonaro entered Argentina with his wife and two daughters late on Tuesday evening, according to the country's migration department. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and had refused to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, crossed into Argentina via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, about 19 hours by road from his home in Brasilia. The family then boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly S.A. bound for the Ecuadorean city of Guayaquil, the migration department said. Argentina's presidency did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither did Baires Fly. A Gulfstream G400 operated by Baires Fly, registration LV-JQW, departed Puerto Iguazu at 12:22 a.m. (0322 GMT) and landed in Guayaquil at 3:46 a.m. (0846 GMT), according to FlightAware. The aircraft then departed for Miami's Opa-locka Executive Airport, where it was scheduled to land at 9:18 a.m. local time (1318 GMT). It was unclear how Bolsonaro entered Ecuador. Authorities there did not immediately respond to a request for comment. FRESH BRAZIL-US RIFT Bolsonaro's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power. Ahead of Sunday's election, Reuters reported on a US State Department [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"campaign"] to restore the Bolsonaros to office. Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would approve of Bolsonaro coming to the United States, after his State Department said it would give them entry visas. Trump has previously alleged that Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. Jair Bolsonaro also travelled to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in 2022, during Joe Biden's presidency. He eventually returned but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia. Bolsonaro had been favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result. Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday after the order to hand in his passports that he had no plans to flee. "I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me."

item.title: 日独首脳が会談、戦闘機の共同開発参加にメルツ氏意欲 ＥＶ問題は触れず
item.description:
Tamiyuki Kihara
[東京 ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[東京 ２８日 ロイター] - 高市早苗首相とドイツのメルツ首相は２８日、首相官邸で会談した。人工知能（ＡＩ）や重要鉱物など幅広い分野で戦略的連携を強化することで一致する中、メルツ氏は日英伊３カ国が進める戦闘機共同開発への参画に意欲を示した。日本側が懸念する日本製電気自動車（ＥＶ）が欧州で優遇措置の対象外となる問題には触れなかった。

メルツ氏は会談後の記者発表で、日本との防衛協力を一層強めていくと表明した。その上で、日英伊による次期戦闘機開発計画「グローバル戦闘航空プログラム（ＧＣＡＰ）」に言及。ドイツが参画を検討しているとし、「共同開発が可能かどうか検討したい」と述べた。

並んで記者発表に臨んだ高市氏は、日独を「不可欠な相互補完性を持つプレミアム・パートナー」と位置付けることで合意したと述べた。「相互補完が可能な防衛産業分野」での協力推進を強調し、「厳しさを増す国際情勢の中で、日独の連携はかつてなく重要だ」と語ったものの、ＧＣＡＰには触れなかった。

日本はＧＣＡＰを通じ、航空自衛隊Ｆ２戦闘機の後継機の調達を計画している。日英伊３カ国は２０３５年の初号機配備を目指しているが、新たに参加国が加わると開発が遅れ、Ｆ２の退役に間に合わなくなる恐れがあるとの考えが日本政府や与党内にはある。政府関係者によると、技術的な強みがドイツと似通っていることも、日本が開発分担を確保する上で懸念となっている。

一方、両首脳は戦略分野で産業協力を進めることで一致した。高市氏は重要鉱物や半導体などのサプライチェーン（供給網）強靱化で連携を深めるほか、ＡＩをめぐる課題に共同で取り組むため「日独ＡＩ対話」を立ち上げる意向を示した。首脳共同声明とともに、先端科学技術協力および経済安全保障に関する首脳共同宣言を発出することでも合意した。

ＥＵが欧州製ＥＶの域内普及を促す優遇措置を検討していることには、両首脳とも言及しなかった。日本政府や自動車産業からは日本製が欧州市場から排除されるとの懸念が出ており、赤沢亮正経済産業相はメルツ氏が同席したこの日の日独ハイレベル経済サミットであいさつし、「強く懸念している」と述べた。

また、トヨタ自動車の近健太社長は日独企業代表団の一員として高市、メルツ両首脳を表敬訪問。その後にロイターの取材に応じ、今後も日本政府やＥＵに働きかけをしていく考えを示した。「日本の生産車がＥＵ生産車と同等の扱いをされるような形が顧客にとって、自動車産業にとって、自動車文化にとって一番良いと思っている」とした上で、「そういったことをお伝えする機会があれば、その都度お伝えしたい」と語った。

（鬼原民幸　編集：久保信博）

BERLIN, Oct 28 : Winning the Ballon d'Or will help convince Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane to extend his deal with the German champions, former World Cup winner Lothar Matthaeus said on Wednesday. On Monday Kane became the first Englishman to win the prestigious award - the top individual honour in the sport - since Michael Owen in 2001. The England captain was prolific last season, scoring 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions as the German side completed a domestic league and cup double. He was also a World Cup semi-finalist with England, scoring six goals in the tournament. "We are very happy to have Harry Kane in the Bundesliga. He is an international ambassador of football," Matthaeus, who won the award in 1990 after leading Germany to World Cup victory that year, said in an online media round table.

"Maybe he was dreaming to win the Ballon d'Or.. but you have to play in a big club like Bayern. He found his peace in Munich and the right club with the right teammates." Kane, 33, joined Bayern in 2023 in a €100 million ($111 million) move from boyhood club Tottenham Hotspur, in search of silverware. He has since won the league twice and is in talks with Bayern over a new contract. "I think he gets a bonus (for winning the Ballon d'Or), 36 years ago I got nothing," Matthaeus said. "But it is about more than money. It is a good moment to sign (a new deal) for Bayern. Bayern helped him get this Ballon d'Or. "The relationship between Harry Kane and Bayern Munich is perfect, and with everything that has happened in the last three years, I think Harry will sign his contract for the next two, three years." item.title: Israel’s vote prolongs Middle East instability
item.description: Had the coalition opposing Benjamin Netanyahu received a decisive mandate, it might have helped ease regional tensions. Instead, initial election results imply deadlock. Scope for the PM to linger suggests ongoing escalation risks – and oil prices tangibly above $100 a barrel.
item.dc:creator: George Hay
item.content:encoded: Had the coalition opposing Benjamin Netanyahu received a decisive mandate, it might have helped ease regional tensions. Instead, initial election results imply deadlock. Scope for the PM to linger suggests ongoing escalation risks – and oil prices tangibly above $100 a barrel. Full view will be published shortly. Follow George Hay on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties were forecast to win 54 seats in parliament following Israeli elections on October 27. The opposition bloc led by his rival Gadi Eisenkot was forecast to win 47 seats, according to 70.7% of votes tallied on the morning of October 28. Parties representing Israelis of Arab descent were forecast to win 19. While Netanyahu lost his bloc's majority in the 120-seat Knesset, as expected, opponents were left with no hope of unseating him without some form of backing of Arab parties, which many have ruled out. Even then, he would remain as caretaker during any coalition negotiations, or until a new election in 2027. Netanyahu, addressing his Likud party's faithful after 3 a.m. (0100 GMT) at the party's election headquarters in Jerusalem, called for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government". He also highlighted Israel's military successes and raised the prospect of a renewed joint military action against Iran alongside his ally, US President Donald Trump. "Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he said. Eisenkot acknowledged that Netanyahu was still in office as a caretaker, but said the prime minister had lost public support and urged him to retire from politics. He also issued a warning that Netanyahu might use security for political ends. As of 1100 GMT on October 28, Brent crude prices were trading at $115 a barrel, up 1%. CONTEXT-NEWS

Oct 28 : Former Japan coach Takeshi Okada has resigned as vice-president of the Japan Football Association, citing concerns over developments surrounding FIFA and the World Cup, the JFA said on Wednesday. Okada's resignation came a week after Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa declared support for Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president at the AFC's extraordinary congress in Tokyo. The endorsement marked a sharp shift from the AFC's position three months earlier, when the confederation accused FIFA of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal to sell a stake in FIFA competitions. "Guided by my belief that sports should embody integrity, I have always valued their social significance," Okada said in a statement on the JFA website.

"However, the series of actions surrounding this year's FIFA World Cup represent a significant divergence from my personal convictions. As a sportsman, I cannot accept this, which has led me to make this decision." Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, is seeking re-election in March after apologising for his failed private investment project. Support from Asia, one of FIFA's largest voting blocs, could prove crucial to his bid. "Given the relationship with the Asian Football Confederation and the impact on Japanese soccer, I understand that there are practical reasons for aligning with the AFC's stance," Okada said. Okada coached Japan at the 1998 and 2010 World Cups, leading the team to the last 16 in South Africa.

item.title: ブラジル最高裁、ボルソナロ上院議員への捜索報道を否定
item.description: [ブラジリア ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ブラジリア ２８日 ロイター] - ブラジル最高裁は２８日、フラビオ・ボルソナロ上院議員を対象とする警察の捜査活動は実施されておらず、捜索・差し押さえ令状も発付されていないと発表した。

これに先立ち、ニュースサイトＧ１は同日、連邦警察が首都ブラジリアにある同議員の自宅で捜索・差し押さえ令状を執行したと報じていた。

最高裁は声明で「フラビオ・ボルソナロ上院議員または同議員の住所地を対象とする捜索・差し押さえ令状が存在する、あるいは執行されたという情報が出回っているが、これは虚偽だ」と表明した。

関係者によると、２５日のブラジル大統領選の決選投票で現職のルラ大統領に敗れたボルソナロ氏は米国に向けて出国した。

ボルソナロ氏は敗北を認めておらず、旅券の提出を命じた最高裁の命令に従わずに出国した。この命令は資金洗浄疑惑の捜査に関連するもので、ボルソナロ氏は不正を否定している。

item.title: Nigeria agrees transport allowance for federal government workers ahead of Tinubu re-election bid
item.description: Nigeria's government agreed on Wednesday to pay federal government workers a 70,000 naira ($52) monthly transport allowance for six months as part of a deal with the main labour union, the Nigeria Labour Congress, to ease soaring living costs, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nigeria's government agreed on Wednesday to pay federal government workers a 70,000 naira ($52) monthly transport allowance for six months as part of a deal with the main labour union, the Nigeria Labour Congress, to ease soaring living costs, officials said. The deal highlights the political sensitivity of rising prices ahead of President Bola Tinubu's [USN:L8N4441DC TEXT:"re-election bid"] in January. His reforms have been credited with improving public finances but have left millions of Nigerians reeling from the worst [USN:L8N44200K TEXT:"cost-of-living crisis"] in a generation. Ministry of Labour spokesperson Annah Daniel said federal government workers would receive the payout from next month The government also pledged to clear outstanding worker benefits, including arrears of a special allowance dating back to May 2026, which it will pay in three monthly instalments starting in November The agreement revives talks on a new national minimum wage, with both sides agreeing to immediately set up a wage negotiation committee, though they remain divided over when any increase should take effect Health workers will receive 19 months of unpaid allowance arrears, with the government pledging to clear the backlog within three months from December 2026, meeting a long-standing union demand Additional measures, including tax relief for workers, will be referred to the National Economic Council for consideration, while proposed hazard allowances for agricultural workers are undergoing verification and cost assessments Both sides agreed to reconvene in a month to review progress on implementing the measures, Daniel said ($1 = 1,338.6400 naira)

item.title: ノルウェー首相、プーチン氏との電話会談擁護 「欧州の見解伝達」
item.description: [オスロ ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[オスロ ２８日 ロイター] - ノルウェーのストーレ首相は２８日、ロシアのプーチン大統領、フィンランドのストゥブ大統領との３者電話会談について、プーチン氏に米国だけでなく欧州の見解も確実に伝えることが目的だったと述べ、会談を擁護した。

２７日の電話会談は、ロシア政府との直接接触を避けてきた西欧諸国の首脳の長年の慣行を破るもので、デンマークのフレデリクセン首相など同盟国の指導者から批判を受けた。

会談は９０分間にわたった。ウクライナとロシアの当局者は１１月にアブダビで、２月以来初めてとなる対面協議を行う見通しで、今回の電話会談はこれに先立って行われた。

ストーレ氏は公共放送ＮＲＫに「われわれ（ストゥブ氏と私）は今後に目を向け、この戦争が何カ月も際限なく続き、人々が命を落とし、解決が一段と難しくなる事態を避けるには何が必要かに焦点を当てた」と語った。

「（プーチン氏が）考えを変えるとは思わないが、われわれの立場を極めて明確に聞くことにはなる。米国側が同氏と話す際、こうしたメッセージの一部が伝わっていないのではないかと懸念している」と述べた。

また、ノルウェーは、ロシアとウクライナのエネルギーインフラへの攻撃停止、ウクライナ産穀物を輸出する船舶への攻撃停止、捕虜交換の実施といった緊張緩和措置の導入を望んでいると説明した。

ウクライナが領土を割譲せずに和平を実現できるかとの質問には「現在、ロシアは（ウクライナ領土の）２０％近くを支配している。ウクライナは領土を失ったと認める合意には決して署名しないだろう。ただ、現在の前線を現実として受け止め、出発点にできるかどうかは別の問題だ」と答えた。

「そして大きな問題は、和平合意後に（ウクライナに）どのような安全の保証を提供できるかだ。プーチン氏も、これが大きな問題であることを認識している」と述べた。

ロシアのラブロフ外相は、２７日の電話会談でウクライナ紛争について新たな提案はなく、欧州諸国は単に交渉過程での役割を求めているだけだと述べている。

item.title: 米国防長官、インド太平洋への関与強調 ＡＳＥＡＮと協力推進へ
item.description:
Mikhail Flores Karen Lema
[セブ（フィリピン） ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Mikhail Flores　Karen Lema

[セブ（フィリピン） ２８日 ロイター] - ヘグセス米国防長官は２８日、東南アジア各国の国防担当閣僚らに対し、インド太平洋地域への米国の関与は揺るがないと訴え、米国と同盟国・パートナー国の利益を守ると約束した。

ヘグセス氏はフィリピンのセブで２日間にわたり開かれる東南アジア諸国連合（ＡＳＥＡＮ）国防相会議と関連会合に参加している。海洋状況把握の強化や、海軍間の相互運用性と協力の拡大などの実務的な協力を通じてこの関与を裏付けると述べた。

「これらは象徴的な取り組みではない。真剣なパートナーが何をするかを具体的に示すものだ」とし「真剣なパートナーは共に訓練し、学び、計画を立て、紛争を防ぐために必要な信頼と能力を築く」と語った。

今回はイラン戦争で米軍の資源が逼迫し、米国内の政治的圧力も高まる中での訪問となった。東南アジアをはじめアジア各国の政府は、米国がアジア太平洋に引き続き注力できるのかを見極めようとしている。

ヘグセス氏は「われわれは自国の利益と同盟国・パートナー国の利益を守る。それこそが『力による平和』だ」と強調した。

また米国とＡＳＥＡＮが来年、正式な関係樹立から半世紀を迎えることを踏まえ、「極めて重要な今後数年間」の関係の指針となる防衛協力の枠組みを策定するよう提案した。

item.title: Unitree's quarterly revenue surges 70% in test for China's robotics sector
item.description: Unitree said on Wednesday third-quarter revenue rose 70% from a year earlier but net profit fell in its first earnings result since listing, as China's best-known humanoid maker faces its first market test amid a tech sector rout.
item.dc:creator: Laurie Chen
item.content:encoded: Unitree (688836.SS) said on Wednesday third-quarter revenue rose 70% from a year earlier but net profit fell in its first earnings result [USN:L1N44G01S TEXT:"since listing"], as China's best-known humanoid maker faces its first market test amid a tech [USN:L4N4601U6 TEXT:"sector rout"]. It generated 665 million yuan ($100 million) in revenue while net profit attributable to shareholders fell 17.4% to 112.7 million yuan, below analysts' 224 million yuan forecast, as the company more than doubled research and development expenses. For the first nine months of the year, revenue climbed 55.7% to 1.82 billion yuan and net profit rose 270.5% to 386.7 million yuan, Unitree said in a Shanghai Stock Exchange filing. The company attributed the January-September profit surge to higher gross profit and to a large one-time share-based payment expense booked in the prior-year period. It is one of the few profitable domestic robot firms as the sector searches for viable commercial applications of the technology. Research and development spending jumped 249.6% in the third quarter to 127.0 million yuan, or 19.1% of revenue, as the company invested more in embodied-intelligence large models, computing capacity and its R&D team. Investors are closely watching the company's performance as a bellwether for future listings of Chinese humanoid robot makers, whose technology has not yet proved commercial viability. Reuters reported last month that Chinese regulators are [USN:L8N458174 TEXT:"slowing down"] IPOs for humanoid robot firms amid tech stock volatility, as they scrutinise whether soaring valuations and revenue tied to state-backed projects reflect real commercial demand. TECH MARKET ROUT Unitree's shares have surged over 65% in the past two weeks after slumping almost 55% from their August debut. The company issued an abnormal trading announcement on October 21, warning investors of significant valuation risks. But US investment bank JPMorgan hiked its stock rating on Monday and the company last week released a demo video of its new H2-X "Kung Fu Legend Guardian" humanoid robot showing off combat moves, spurring the latest rally. Unitree's results come amid a broader market rout led by Chinese AI and technology shares. The STAR50 index (.STAR50) of Shanghai-listed chip and AI leaders has tumbled 40% since July, wiping out around $480 billion in market value, while the blue-chip CSI300 (.CSI300) has fallen about 20% from June highs. Unitree, which competes with Tesla (TSLA.O) and Hyundai Motor Group-owned Boston Dynamics, has drawn global attention for its robots that run, dance and perform martial arts. One of the world's biggest producers of humanoid and quadruped robots, it is backed by influential Chinese companies including Alibaba Group (9988.HK) and Tencent (0700.HK) .

item.title: イスラエル総選挙、ネタニヤフ首相続投へ ユダヤ系から予想以上の支持
item.description:
Steven Scheer Rami Ayyub Lina Obeid
[エルサレム ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Steven Scheer　Rami Ayyub　Lina Obeid

[エルサレム ２８日 ロイター] - イスラエルで２７日に実施された国会（定数１２０）の総選挙で、ネタニヤフ首相（７７）の陣営はユダヤ系国民から事前の予想を上回る支持を獲得し、ネタニヤフ氏は少なくとも暫定首相として続投することがほぼ確実となった。

イスラエルのメディアによると、同国の歴史的な転換点と位置付けられた今回の選挙では、２８日午前の開票率約７０．７％の段階で、右派、極右、ユダヤ教超正統派の各党で構成するネタニヤフ氏の陣営が５４議席を獲得し、アイゼンコット元軍参謀総長（６６）率いる野党陣営の４７議席を大きく上回る見通しとなった。また、アラブ系政党は１９議席を獲得する見込み。

開票は続いており、結果はなお変わる可能性がある。ただ、中道左派から強硬右派までの反ネタニヤフ勢力を集めたアイゼンコット氏の陣営は、接戦を予測していた選挙前の世論調査を下回る結果となっており、同氏の勝利は一段と遠のいている。

ネタニヤフ氏の陣営は予想通り国会で過半数を失ったものの、野党勢力が同氏を退陣に追い込むには、アラブ系政党から何らかの支持を得ることが不可欠となった。多くの野党勢力はそうした協力を否定している。仮に協力が実現しても、連立交渉の間、あるいは２０２７年に再選挙が行われるまで、同氏は暫定首相にとどまる。

FAST

LOS ANGELES, Oct 28 : Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks on Wednesday, abandoning a long-held aversion to the technology as it caps a burst of product launches ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. Apple is holding an event in Los Angeles after launching a folding iPhone, Duo, at its Silicon Valley headquarters in September and a smart home hub in New York earlier this month. While those products will test new markets for Apple, the Los Angeles event could rekindle an old question: should Apple put the touchscreens that it made mainstream in iPhones and iPads in its oldest product line? Apple executives long resisted the idea, with Steve Jobs saying in 2010 that touchscreens on laptops were "ergonomically terrible" and then-CEO Tim Cook saying in 2012 that such devices would be as pleasing to users as converging a toaster and a refrigerator. Before becoming Apple's current CEO, John Ternus argued that Apple already made a touchscreen computer with its iPad lineup. But touchscreens have been widely available for more than a decade on Windows devices, and with the iPhone nearing its two-decade anniversary, a new generation of buyers expects screens to respond to touch.

"I believe they were always wrong on pushing back on touch, and this is the long arm of reality setting in," said Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. "Some things are purely inevitable." A key question for Apple is how customers will respond. The company has seen an uptick in Mac sales, but much of that growth has been among technology enthusiasts and businesses buying the machines to handle AI tasks on-device. While Apple this week announced an upgraded base model of its MacBook Pro with a new M6 chip, Bloomberg News has reported that it plans to ship touchscreen models with its existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips that already come in MacBook Pro models, meaning the new machines would not gain a significant performance boost over existing ones. "The only thing people want is more memory and better processors for local models!" prominent tech commentator Jason Calacanis, the host of the All-In Podcast, wrote on X.

item.title: Phillips 66 posts record quarterly profit on refining strength
item.description: Phillips 66 on Wednesday reported a record quarterly profit, topping Wall Street estimates, powered by higher refining margins on fuel supply disruptions due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Phillips 66 (PSX.N) on Wednesday reported a record quarterly profit, topping Wall Street estimates, powered by higher refining margins on fuel supply disruptions due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Peers [USN:L4N4680YK TEXT:"Valero"] Energy (VLO.N) and [USN:L3N46E13O TEXT:"HF"] Sinclair (DINO.N) also posted record third-quarter profits as US refiners emerged as key beneficiaries of the disruptions that tightened global supplies, while refinery utilization remained at multi-year highs. US fuel exports, particularly diesel, used in manufacturing and agriculture, have hit record levels. Phillips 66's refining segment reported a sharp jump in adjusted earnings to $6.06 billion in the quarter from $430 million a year earlier, while realized margin more than tripled to a record $38 per barrel from $12.15 per barrel last year. US refinery margins, measured by the benchmark 3-2-1 crack spread , were up more than 150% on average during the July-September quarter from a year earlier. Shares of the company rose 1.3% in premarket trading. Phillips 66's net income rose to $5.62 billion from $133 million a year earlier, marking its highest quarterly profit on record. Adjusted earnings at its renewable fuel segment rose to $191 million during the quarter, compared to a loss of $43 million a year earlier. After years of margin pressure, US refiners are seeing improving returns from renewable fuels as higher biofuel blending requirements and rising diesel prices boost profitability. Phillips 66 said its Coastal Bend expansion project remains on track, with initial volumes expected in the fourth quarter and full ramp-up to 350,000 barrels per day in early 2027, improving transportation between Permian and Eagle Ford output and NGL processing plants in Corpus Christi and Sweeny in Texas. In August, the company, Kinder Morgan (KMI.N) and HF Sinclair said they would [USN:L4N4480QA TEXT:"proceed"] with the proposed $5 billion Western Gateway Pipeline system and had finalized a joint venture agreement. Houston-based Phillips 66 reported an adjusted profit of $14.08 per share for the three months ended September 30, compared with analysts' average estimate of $11.73, according to data compiled by LSEG.

FAST

LONDON/HONG KONG, Oct 28 : With jet fuel prices at roughly double their levels before the Iran war, airlines are growing increasingly reluctant to lock in future fuel costs through new hedges, warning instead of steep fare increases to offset higher fuel bills. Hedging allows airlines to lock in future fuel prices, helping shield them from increases and providing greater certainty over costs. But some programmes require premiums, collateral or other costs, while airlines that hedge at current elevated prices risk being locked into expensive fuel if geopolitical tensions ease and prices retreat. As the conflict in the Middle East enters its ninth month, the strategy shift means fliers globally will likely pay far higher air fares as carriers lose their hedging protection, testing consumer willingness to shell out more for travel. "Most hedging is finishing," AirAsia CEO Tony Fernandes told Reuters this month, adding the Malaysian airline was budgeting for 12 months of high oil prices and had "given up trying to predict" how geopolitical tensions would evolve.

He said the firm was not even modelling a scenario where oil prices fall. "So everyone's going to be exposed. There's only one way or two ways of dealing with that: cut costs or raise fares." Finland's Finnair, which said this month that high fuel costs had fed through to ticket prices, has stopped adding new hedges as fuel costs surged this year. It has an average hedging ratio of 34 per cent for 2027. "With such high prices, how do you then lock in low prices again?" finance chief Pia Aaltonen-Forsell said on Tuesday. "If we add right now, it's more expensive." NO EUROPEAN AIRLINE WELL HEDGED THROUGH 2027, RYANAIR SAYS Jet fuel accounts for between 30 per cent and 40 per cent of airlines' costs, with European and Asian carriers historically hedging more of their fuel needs than US rivals, which largely abandoned the practice after costly bets on oil prices backfired. "You have stability of cost when you hedge," said Jeffrey Goh, managing director at Alton Aviation, adding it remained a bet on prices rising — and could backfire. "You have to look at the forward curve and predict how fast it might go down." The pressure could intensify in 2027 as hedges put in place before the war expire, exposing airlines more fully to current fuel prices. "None of the European airlines, including Ryanair, are well-hedged until summer of 2027, so I think you're going to have to see air fares rise by 15 per cent to 20 per cent," Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary told reporters earlier this month. Ryanair said in September it had stopped hedging. Europe's largest airline has hedged about 80 per cent of its jet fuel needs for the year ending March 2027. In a sign of challenges airlines may face pushing higher fares, budget carrier Norwegian Air Shuttle said on Wednesday it had been forced to undo some post-Iran war price hikes because customers "were not willing to pay". FUEL HEDGING NOT A 'COMPLETE SOLUTION' Globally, airline hedging policies remain fragmented, with some carriers expanding programmes since the war began and others dialling them back. Carriers with weak balance sheets also often have less flexibility to absorb the costs associated with hedging and can be fully exposed to fuel-price movements, contributing to a flurry of recent bankruptcy and insolvency filings. US airlines have largely shown little appetite to return to hedging despite this year's fuel shock. Analysts say US consumers tend to be less price sensitive than travellers in other regions and the most willing to absorb higher fares. Air fares in the European Union rose 5.8 per cent year-on-year in September, the latest official data show. US air fares, meanwhile, were up more than 20 per cent year-on-year in the month. American, United, Delta, JetBlue and Allegiant have no material fuel hedges, while Frontier has no active hedging position. Southwest ended its long-running programme last year, while Alaska and Hawaiian also closed out remaining positions. The reluctance of some European and Asian airlines to add new hedges could signal a broader shift in industry attitudes towards fuel hedging, although this year's fuel-price spike has also highlighted the risks of remaining exposed to fuel markets. Delta, United and Southwest all cut profit targets or disappointed investors with their earnings outlooks this month as fuel expenses climbed. Despite hedging more than 70 per cent of their jet fuel needs for this year, Ryanair and Lufthansa cut capacity on some routes to limit the impact of unhedged fuel costs. "Fuel remains the single largest area of uncertainty in the outlook," said Air New Zealand Chief Financial Officer Kris Cudmore. "Our hedging program provides some nearer term protection, but it is far from a complete solution."

(Additional reporting by Phil Blenkinsop in Brussels, Rajesh Kumar Singh in Chicago and Julie Zhu in Hong Kong and Essi Lehto in Helsinki; Editing by Adam Jourdan and Mark Potter)

Source: Reuters

item.title: South Korea media commission fines Google and Apple over app payment systems
item.description: South Korea's Media and Communications Commission has fined Google and Apple for limiting users to specific app payment systems and ordered corrective measures, the regulator said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's Media and Communications Commission has fined Google (GOOGL.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) for limiting users to specific app payment systems and ordered corrective measures, the regulator said on Wednesday. Google was fined 42.9 billion won ($32.35 million) and Apple 20.8 billion won, the commission said in a statement. Apple said it disagreed with the decision and was evaluating options in accordance with South Korean laws. It said it has worked with outside developers to enable innovation through its App Store. Google did not immediately have comment when contacted by Reuters. ($1 = 1,326.0900 won)

item.title: Renshaw, Green guide Australia to 191-4
item.description: Matt Renshaw (74) and Cameron Green (65) scored half centuries but were dismissed just before tea as Australia went to the interval on 191 for four on the second day of the decisive third test against South Africa at Newlands on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Matt Renshaw (74) and Cameron Green (65) scored half centuries but were dismissed just before tea as Australia went to the interval on 191 for four on the second day of the decisive third test against South Africa at Newlands on Wednesday. • Australia trail South Africa’s first-innings total of 329 by 138 runs with six wickets in hand. • Josh Inglis (5 not out) and Alex Carey (1 not out) will resume in the evening session. • Renshaw and Travis Head (41) put on 58 for the first wicket before spinner Simon Harmer (2-43) removed the latter with his first ball of the match. Head chopped the ball on to his stumps playing off the back foot. • Marnus Labuschagne's poor run in tests continued when he fell for a duck, caught by Aiden Markram at slip off Harmer. • Renshaw and Green added 126 for the third wicket before they also fell in quick succession, this time to fast bowler Marco Jansen (2-28). Renshaw was caught by wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton and Green edged to Harmer at slip. • The series is level at 1-1 after Australia won the first test by 214 runs in Durban and South Africa responded with a victory by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha. • The team who win the match will occupy the number one position in the test world rankings, which is currently held by Australia.

FAST

Oct 28 : The US dollar held onto gains on Wednesday after reaching a two-week high ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, while sterling investors awaited the Andy Burnham government's first budget, hoping it would avoid a heavy reliance on borrowing. The week is packed with monetary policy decisions by central banks globally as policymakers weigh the path ahead for interest rates against the backdrop of price pressures due to the Middle East conflict and ballooning sovereign debt costs. Traders broadly expect no change in Fed monetary policy after a series of Fed officials in recent weeks signalled the need to wait and watch for more signs of persistent price pressures. However, they see a 78 per cent chance that the central bank could lift interest rates by at least 25 basis points in December, the CME Group's FedWatch tool showed. The euro was flat at $1.1126, trading just above the May 2025 low it hit earlier this month, while against the yen, the dollar was steady at 157.89 yen.

"A hold would likely be accompanied by a statement similar to the statement in September when the FOMC hiked, underlining the fact that the economy remains resilient," Derek Halpenny, head of research, global markets EMEA & international securities at MUFG, said in a note. "There is a risk that there could be some dissents and that would certainly be one signal of the leaning and would strengthen the market’s conviction of a hike in December." The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six other currencies, was trading at a two-week high of 102.37. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note was up 1 basis point at 5.0 per cent. UK BUDGET EYED The spotlight was on the British government's budget plans, with finance minister John Healey expected to detail fiscal spending for the coming year at 1230 GMT. The pound slipped 0.1 per cent to $1.328 and was about 0.2 per cent lower versus the euro, but sterling was close to the 17-month high versus the euro hit in the previous session. Investors will be keen to see how the government expects to raise revenue, with analysts expecting taxes on banks, gambling firms and online marketplaces. "The expectation is that the UK is maybe a little bit more fiscally constrained than many of its European peers. So if the government doesn't do anything too negative, there's room for the market to be somewhat pleasantly surprised in this," said Michael Leithead, head of fixed income at EFG Asset Management. However, given the recent scrutiny around government debt, any significant reliance on borrowing could spark a selloff in the currency and gilts.  CANADIAN RATE HIKE AWAITED; KIWI FALLS Later in the day, the Canadian central bank is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by at least 25 basis points in a preemptive move to stop energy-led inflation from spreading into the rest of the economy.  The Canadian dollar inched up 0.1 per cent to C$1.403 per US dollar.  The European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan are also expected to deliver monetary policy verdicts on Thursday and Friday, respectively, with both central banks expected to leave policy rates unchanged.    The New Zealand dollar sank as much as 1.3 per cent to $0.5609 after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand held interest rates at 2.75 per cent, surprising a large majority of economists who had expected a rate hike. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was 0.7 per cent higher at $81,292.46, while ether climbed 0.9 per cent to $2,362.49.

Source: Reuters

At least 30 people killed in Spain when two high-speed trains collide

FAST

MADRID: At least 30 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday (Oct 28), the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said. Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha television showed a derailed train with several carriages remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line. Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident. "We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train," he said.

A person briefed on the disaster said an express operated by Spanish train operator Iryo stopped near Toledo due to a signal fault, on orders from infrastructure manager ADIF, when it was struck by another high-speed train on. A train operated by Renfe then struck the stationary train at high speed, causing several carriages of both trains to derail, the person said. There was no immediate response to a Reuters request for comment from Iryo or Renfe.

The scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Oct 28, 2026. (Photo: Juanma Jimenez/Europa Press via AP)

PASSENGER DESCRIBES SEEING FATALITIES Castilla-La Mancha regional government said the death toll had risen to 30 from 10 after earlier warning it could rise. Jesús Pérez Martín, mayor of the nearby town of Los Yébenes, said the situation was "horrific" and pointed to a severe tragedy. "They are telling me about mutilations and very serious injuries," he told RTVE. Health Minister Mónica García urged people in a post on X to donate blood. Eduarda, a passenger on the Iryo train, told Cadena SER radio she felt a strong impact that threw her forward, initially making her think the train had made an emergency stop. She only realised the seriousness of the accident after seeing injured people and being told to evacuate. After climbing down an embankment to safety, she saw what she described as a catastrophic scene, with part of the train hanging down the slope and a fire in one carriage. Emergency responders, including a helicopter, police and ambulances, arrived within about 20 minutes, she said. "I saw dead people," she said.

SECOND FATAL ACCIDENT ON LINE IN A YEAR Castilla-La Mancha region spokesperson Esther Padilla said 147 people had been travelling on the Iryo train and 397 on the Renfe train. The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line that killed 46 people. That crash in January, which occurred after a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province, triggered a debate about the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.

Related:

Passengers tell of terror, screams and darkness after Spain train crash

Railway safety questioned as Spain reels from twin train disasters

ELECTION DUE NEXT MONTH The Renfe and Iryo trains crashed just after 9am, causing two Iryo wagons to derail, a spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha region said, adding that the cause was not yet clear. Renfe said it had activated a special line for families of victims and expressed its condolences. Iryo said it had activated emergency protocols. The latest accident comes as Spain gears up for an election on Nov 29. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's agenda, published on the Spanish government's website, had been cleared for the day. The opposition People's Party also cancelled all campaign events, a spokesperson said. "Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families," Sanchez said on X. Manuel Galan, the mayor of the nearby town of Urda, told Cadena SER that emergency services had asked the town council to prepare emergency facilities, including a sports hall, to accommodate passengers and the injured.

Civil Guards stand amongst the wreckage of a train collision between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on Oct 28, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Javier Soriano)

RAIL SAFETY RECORD Accidents, including derailments and collisions, increased from 45 in 2016 to 57 in 2024 and 69 last year, according to Spain's railway safety authority. In the same period, problems such as deterioration and breaks in the rails went from 494 and 667, a level below the 716 registered in 2024. Some 25 million passengers used a high-speed train in Spain in the first half of the year, a decline of roughly 14 per cent compared with the same period last year, according to a Reuters analysis of data from Spain's competition authority. European Commission data shows Spain's maintenance investment in its roughly 4,000km of high-speed lines has lagged large European peers, despite an unmatched drive to expand the network. Spain spent an average of about €1.5 billion a year from 2018 to 2022 on its high-speed network, more than any other country. However, the vast majority went to new infrastructure with only some 16 per cent earmarked for maintenance, renewal and upgrades. Spain had registered among the lowest fatality rates in the EU from train incidents before this year's accidents, with just one or fewer fatalities per thousand kilometres of railway tracks, according to the latest available Eurostat data from 2024. Over 90 per cent of Spain's train network is equipped with the highest level of safety control systems in the European Union, according to the EU railway agency. Alongside Belgium and Switzerland, its networks have the largest amount of rail equipped with a Europe-wide signalling standard.

Source: Reuters/ec

Kepler Cheuvreux analyst Torsten Sauer pointed instead to profit-taking. The computer mouse and keyboard maker reported non-GAAP operating income of $231 million for the three months ended September, beating the $204 million consensus compiled by Visible Alpha and its own guidance of $185 million to $210 million. AlphaValue analyst Maximilien Pascaud said the market reaction appeared excessive given that the incident at one of Logitech’s semiconductor suppliers at the end of June was now largely contained. "However, the market's focus has quickly shifted to profitability headwinds: gross margins will face meaningful pressure from component inflation and rising freight rates, while elevated marketing and R&D spend continues to weigh on operational leverage," Pascaud said. item.title: Russell Brand says friends abandoned him after 'devastating' sex crime allegations
item.description: British comedian and actor Russell Brand said on Wednesday that friends and colleagues turned against him after allegations of sex crimes were made against him, before telling a jury in a London court that consent was fundamental.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden
item.content:encoded: British comedian and actor Russell Brand said on Wednesday that friends and colleagues turned against him after allegations of sex crimes were made against him, before telling a jury in a London court that consent was fundamental. Brand, once a regular figure on British television and star of a number of Hollywood movies, is on trial accused of [USN:L1N4650H6 TEXT:"three counts of rape"], three of sexual assault and an attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. The 51-year-old former husband of US singer Katy Perry denies all the allegations. Appearing in the witness box in the third week of his trial at London's Southwark Crown Court, Brand said "no" loudly and clearly when his lawyer asked him if he had committed any of the alleged crimes. The jury has previously been told how all the complainants came forward to detectives after a documentary was broadcast in 2023 along with a number of newspaper articles in which anonymous allegations were made by other women who are not involved in the trial. Brand, wearing a black suit with an open-neck white shirt and a loose black tie, said the impact had been "devastating" as friends turned their backs on him and not a single person would give evidence on his behalf. Asked by his lawyer Ian Winter if they would "touch you with a bargepole", he replied: "No." 'CONSENT IS FUNDAMENTAL', BRAND SAYS As Brand described how his public image had grown over time, he said his marriage with Katy Perry in 2010 had brought him "staggering fame". The couple split up 14 months later. Prosecutors, who completed their case against him earlier on Wednesday, have described Brand as a sexual predator. They said [USN:L1N4610E0 TEXT:"Brand raped a woman"] after meeting her at a fringe event at the Labour Party conference in 1999, forced a woman [USN:L1N4650H6 TEXT:"to give him oral sex"] in toilets at a London bar in 2004, and had molested another woman at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. He is also accused of trying [USN:L8N46211H TEXT:"to pull a woman"] into the male toilets at MTV Europe, in London, where she was working in 2001, and that in 2009 he [USN:L8N4661S4 TEXT:"anally raped a woman"] who had agreed to consensual sex at his home. The final allegation is that he assaulted a woman who was working at the Channel 4 TV station where they were involved in a recording project. Describing the impact of the allegations against him, Brand said that he had been barred from the hospital where his son was receiving open heart surgery after the documentary was broadcast. "My entire life has been consumed by these events, these allegations, these accusations, the impact of these allegations and accusations," he said. "I have devoted myself to these matters." Brand said the first complainant had willingly had sex with him. "Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed more important than sex itself," he said. The trial continues.

Norway’s premier says call with Putin was effort to present European views

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

OSLO, Oct 28 (Reuters) – Norway’s prime minister defended on Wednesday a three-way call with Vladimir Putin and Finland’s president, saying it was intended to ensure the Russian leader heard European as well as US views.

Tuesday’s call between Russia’s Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian premier Jonas Gahr Stoere broke a longstanding practice among Western European leaders of shunning direct contact with the Kremlin, and was criticised by allies including Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen.

The 90-minute call came ahead of what are expected to be the first face-to-face talks since February between Ukrainian and Russian officials, in Abu Dhabi next month.

Show Full Article

“We (Stubb and I) were focused on looking forward, what must happen for this war to not continue endlessly for months, with people dying … and it is even more difficult to find a solution,” Stoere told public broadcaster NRK.

“I don’t think (Putin) will change his mind, but he gets to hear our position very clearly. I am worried that some of these messages do not reach him when the Americans talk to him,” he said.

Norway, said Stoere, was keen to introduce de-escalation steps such as stopping attacks on energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine, halting strikes on ships exporting Ukrainian grain and conducting prisoner-of-war exchanges.

Asked whether there could be peace without Ukraine ceding territory, Stoere said: “Today Russia controls nearly 20% (of Ukrainian territory). Ukraine will never sign a deal that recognises that they have lost territory, but whether they can take the current frontline as a reality and as a starting point, that is a different question.”

“And the big question is what kind of security guarantees can there be for the country (Ukraine) after a peace deal? Putin recognises that this is the big question.”

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said Tuesday’s call offered nothing new on the Ukraine conflict, and that European countries were simply seeking a role in the negotiation process.

(Reporting by Gwladys Fouche in Oslo; Editing by Terje Solsvik, Louise Rasmussen, Aidan Lewis)

At least 10 people dead in Spain after two high-speed trains collide

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MADRID, Oct 28 (Reuters) – At least 10 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said.

Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train with at least one carriage remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line.

Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident.

Show Full Article

“We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been the other one,” he said.

DEATH TOLL LIKELY TO RISE

Castilla-La Mancha region spokesperson Esther Padilla said the number of casualties was likely to rise.

“The latest confirmed figure is 10 dead, but we know it is going to increase. Very likely we will be talking about a higher number,” Padilla said, adding that several carriages had plunged down an embankment.

She said 147 people had been travelling on the Iryo train and 397 on the Renfe train.

The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line that killed 46 people.

That crash in January, which occurred after a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province, triggered a debate about the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s agenda, published on the Spanish government’s website, had been cleared for the day. The opposition People’s Party also cancelled all campaign events ahead of a snap election on November 29, a spokesperson said.

“Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families,” Sanchez said on X.

The Renfe and Iryo trains crashed just after 9 a.m. (0800 GMT), causing two Iryo wagons to derail, a spokesperson for the Castilla La Mancha region said, adding that the cause was not yet clear.

Rail operator Adif said the incident occurred on the line from Madrid to Seville.

Manuel Galan, the mayor of the nearby town of Urda, told Cadena SER that emergency services had asked the town council to prepare emergency facilities, including a sports hall, to accommodate passengers and the injured.

(Reporting by David Latona, Emma Pinedo, Mireia Merino, Corina Pons, Victoria Waldersee, Benjamin Mejias and Joan Faus; Writing by Charlie Devereux; Editing by Toby Chopra and Alison Williams)

Indonesian students protest over forest fires, Prabowo policies

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Stanley Widianto JAKARTA, Oct 28 (Reuters) – Hundreds of Indonesian students and civil society groups staged protests on Wednesday in cities including the capital Jakarta against President Prabowo Subianto’s policies, including the handling of ongoing forest fires.

Worsened by the El Niño weather pattern that leaves peatland vulnerable to fires, Indonesia has been faced with its worst forest fires, and resulting haze, in 11 years, increasing respiratory illnesses and polluting the air of neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore.

Protesters crowded a Jakarta landmark roundabout, with some wearing gas masks, holding up signs protesting over forest fires and demanding the government designate the blazes as a national disaster.

Show Full Article

Some carried signs that said “If we burn, you burn with us,” and held up the three-finger sign of protest – references to the The Hunger Games movie that has been adopted as a symbol by many youth protest movements globally.

Anggi Aurien, 28, had been wearing a gas mask for three hours at the landmark, protesting about the forest fires that have killed wildlife.

“Animals don’t have a mind of their own. If we kill them, what’s the difference between us and them?” she said.

Other signs included photos of the orangutan, which bears the brunt of the fires, and a cardboard cutout of Prabowo.

Other students, including from the University of Indonesia, were blocked by dozens of police and military personnel, leading to some scuffles.

“Revolution! Revolution!” protesters chanted.

Ezra Al Barra, a student from the University of Padjadjaran, said the fires were “our collective anger,” adding students came from other regions outside Jakarta.

Students also rallied in Makassar, in South Sulawesi, and Bandung, in West Java, with similar demands. Dozens of them on motorbikes filled the main roads.

Protesters called for the the government halt spending on populist programmes such as Prabowo’s free meals scheme, among other demands.

Syahganda Nainggolan, chief of the government’s communications office, urged calm but said the government welcomed the protests and was open to input.

PRABOWO’S POPULARITY

The protests, the second in a week, came as Prabowo’s approval ratings had fallen steadily since late last year, according to surveys by Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting, two years into his presidency.

Indonesia has prosecuted companies allegedly linked to the fires and tried methods of modifying the weather to induce rain.

Indonesia’s last major protest took place in August, when hundreds were detained.

In 2025, weeks-long nationwide protests broke out in Indonesia after the police killing of a motorcycle taxi driver, with several more people killed during the unrest.

(Reporting by Stanley Widianto, Johan Purnomo, Heru Asprihanto and Ananda Teresia; Editing by David Stanway and Alex Richardson)

How teachers are remaking classrooms for the AI age

FILE PHOTO: A young student watches Dr. Seuss during a zoom class in Los Angeles, California, U.S., March 2, 2021. REUTERS/Mike Blake/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: A young student's school computer sits waiting for attention in Los Angeles, California, U.S., March 2, 2021. REUTERS/Mike Blake/File Photo

28 Oct 2026 06:18PM (Updated: 28 Oct 2026 06:29PM)

Bookmark

FAST

Oct 28 : In the AI capital of the world, sixth-grade humanities teacher Tristen Chang is designing her classroom so students can’t rely on chatbots. Starting last year, Chang did away with take-home essays and began using oral exams to test students at her San Francisco school. She asks students 15 questions about character, plot, theme and metaphor, which they can answer in as little as five minutes. "There’s been a long march of technology changing teaching, but AI is the most drastic," Chang said. "Everything’s out the window.” As generative AI becomes ubiquitous, US middle and high school teachers are rethinking how they assess learning. Educators are assigning less take-home work, increasing in-class writing and discussion, and redesigning assignments to measure students' thinking rather than simply their answers, according to Reuters interviews with a dozen teachers and education experts across the country.

School systems remain divided over AI, leaving many teachers to navigate the transition largely on their own. Some want AI integrated into classrooms; others want it restricted. Many occupy a middle ground. “Where many adults are using these tools for various kinds of purposes to help them in work-based settings, we haven't really figured out what that means for education,” said Antero Garcia, an education professor at Stanford University and president of the National Council of Teachers of English. A FIXTURE IN EDUCATION As students gain access to AI chatbots on their phones and laptops, teachers are moving more learning back into the classroom. They are increasingly relying on in-class writing, instruction and face-to-face assessment.  Rusty Shabe, who teaches middle school English in San Francisco, said students often turn to AI at home when they feel overwhelmed. He is trying to combat that impulse by devoting more classroom time to writing, taking a month, for example, to work on an essay with seventh-graders.  Bobson Wong, a high school math teacher in New York, now assigns fewer homework questions and more in-class practice so he can better monitor how his students are working. “AI has definitely changed not just how students do math, but how I teach it,” Wong said.  AI's effect on learning is up for debate. A 2025 Harvard randomized trial found that a custom AI tutor improved learning gains and student engagement, while a small 2025 MIT Media Lab study found that people who used ChatGPT to write essays did the work faster, but appeared to do less thinking. Even so, AI is becoming a fixture in education: a 2025 RAND survey found that the majority of US students and English, math and science teachers reported using AI for schoolwork. Last spring, Meghan Hyland, a high school English teacher in a New York City suburb, realized some students were heading to the bathroom to access AI on their phones. Although phones were already banned in her class, she began requiring students to leave them behind when they left.  She has also made classwork a bigger component of students' grades and stopped relying on homework as practice.   “My main ability to understand whether they know how to do critical thinking has to be done in school,” Hyland said. For some educators, the best way to beat AI is to avoid predictable questions. Because AI is adept at answering conventional questions about character and plot, some teachers have begun asking students for interpretations that depart from mainstream thinking.  “I try very hard to create prompts that, at the moment at least, AI is imperfect at responding to,” said Pian Rockfeld, a high school English teacher in the Bronx.  Among her other strategies: assigning essays that require students to read scholarly articles that typically sit behind a paywall, protected from AI chatbots.  ‘YOU CAN’T HIDE WHEN THE LAPTOPS ARE AWAY’ For some teachers, AI is accelerating a broader backlash against classroom technology, motivating them to move away from screens and toward notebooks, pen-and-paper writing and physical projects. Rex Ovalle, a high school English teacher in a Chicago suburb, tells students to retrieve a composition notebook from a box at the start of class. He limits Chromebook use to roughly 10 per cent of school days. “I have seen a lot of engagement because you can’t hide when the laptops are away,” Ovalle said. While Chromebooks and other technology became pervasive during the COVID-19 pandemic, many school districts are now re-evaluating their technology use amid concerns about excessive screen time. In Hyland’s English classes, students write by hand except when they require special accommodations. She has developed new ways to assess their comprehension of a book, such as assigning a cooking demonstration to show how they understand “A Tale of Two Cities." A black-and-white cookie, for example, represented the book's famous opening line about the best of times and worst of times. Hyland said she looks for lessons that involve “something done live so that in real time they are showing creative thinking.” Even as they worry about misuse, some teachers are embracing AI as a classroom tool. They said it can help them find articles on a specific topic, design classroom signage and develop graphics for slide presentations, for example. Michael Zagari, a high school social studies teacher in a New York City suburb, uses AI to change the vocabulary in historical documents for students at different reading levels and to condense articles so he can cover them in class. He encourages students to use AI to get started on research projects and thinks they develop critical thinking skills by learning how to effectively prompt AI. “AI is not going away,” Zagari said. “We need to teach civic responsibility of how to use AI just like we taught responsible use of the Internet.”

Source: Reuters
