item.title: US regulator proposes new rules to speed up LNG projects
item.description: A US regulator proposed new rules on Wednesday to hasten liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity as part of the Trump administration's larger push to speed up energy infrastructure development and cut costs for consumers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A US regulator proposed new rules on Wednesday to hasten liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity as part of the Trump administration's larger push to speed up energy infrastructure development and cut costs for consumers. The US is the world's largest LNG exporter and expected to add another 100 million metric tons to its production by the end of the decade. LNG has been at the center of US President Donald Trump's energy dominance agenda since his return to office. He ordered the resumption of LNG export approvals - something former President Joe Biden had paused - and also started to streamline the environmental approval process that previously slowed projects. The latest rule, proposed by the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), will help operators adopt new technologies to save costs and boost safety, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. Leveraging the technologies will generate $100 million in savings annually, he added. LNG buyers globally have been seeking more diverse supply sourcing ever since the US-Israeli war against Iran cut off Gulf shipments, while Trump has championed the project as a way to boost national security and trade with partners. The proposed rulemaking updates PHMSA’s safety framework for LNG facilities by incorporating National Fire Protection Association standards for the siting, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of LNG facilities. "By overhauling these basic rules to embrace modern technologies, we can safely unleash America’s energy dominance, lower costs, and generate millions in economic opportunity for the men and women powering our energy sector,” Duffy said. The Trump administration's pro-energy stance has led to public announcements from the largest LNG exporters, including Cheniere (LNG.N) and Venture Global LNG (VG.N) , that they will move forward with permitting as much LNG capacity as they think they can [USN:L1N3Z10UO TEXT:"build"] because of permitting certainty under the Trump administration. In the almost two years since the Trump administration took office there has been a wave of LNG projects in the US that announced a final investment decision, amounting to more than 50 million metric tons per annum. One of those is Delfin LNG, which is set to become the first US [USN:L4N42A1LT TEXT:"floating"] LNG export facility, but has not been publicly given the all-clear by PHMSA to operate the pipeline to take natural gas to the floating facility after an explosion earlier this year. Even with the rule change, LNG project developers will still have to go through the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission permitting process, face constant legal challenges and get environmental approvals.

item.title: Meta and Snap face major US legal test of youth social media addiction claims
item.description: Two teenage plaintiffs who say social media caused them to develop serious mental health problems will take Meta Platforms and Snap to trial in Los Angeles on Wednesday in the latest test of claims raised in thousands of US lawsuits over social media's impact on young people.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Two teenage plaintiffs who say social media caused them to develop serious mental health problems will take Meta Platforms (META.O) and Snap (SNAP.N) to trial in Los Angeles on Wednesday in the latest test of claims raised in thousands of US lawsuits over social media's impact on young people. The case is only the second to go to trial involving individual plaintiffs who allege that social media companies deliberately designed their platforms to be addictive. Social media companies lost the first such trial to the tune of [USN:L6N40615P TEXT:"$6 million in damages"] in March. Plaintiffs referred to in court papers as S.J., a 16-year-old girl from Illinois, and K.D.B., an 18-year-old woman from Mississippi, have said they began using YouTube as early as age 3 or 4 and other platforms around age 9. They have alleged that autoplay, infinite scroll and other features drove them to compulsive use, and they developed depression, anxiety and eating disorders as a result. The trial, which begins with the jury selection process on Wednesday, is expected to run for several weeks. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram head Adam Mosseri and Snap CEO Evan Spiegel are expected to testify. The two plaintiffs initially sued TikTok and Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) YouTube, in addition to Meta and Snap. Both [USN:L1N44012V TEXT:"reached settlements"] with TikTok and YouTube ahead of trial, and the Illinois plaintiff also settled with Meta. Wednesday's trial covers claims by both plaintiffs against Snap, and the Mississippi plaintiff's claims against Meta. Meta and Snap have asked Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Carolyn Kuhl, presiding over the proceedings, to split the cases into separate trials, arguing that trying them together would unfairly mix up the evidence for jurors. The judge has not yet ruled on that request. 'A YOUNG PERSON'S MENTAL HEALTH' A Meta spokesperson said the company disagrees with the claims made against it and has built protections into its platforms for a decade. Meta owns Instagram and Facebook. "A young person's mental health is shaped by many factors, as the evidence in this trial will show," the spokesperson said in a statement. "The plaintiff used TikTok far more than Instagram or Facebook, and her personal circumstances were a substantial factor in her struggles." A Snap spokesperson said its Snapchat platform is different from traditional social media because it does not open to a feed or a ranking of what other people post. The company has built safeguards into its platform, the spokesperson said. "We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent their experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed," the spokesperson said. Emily Jeffcott, an attorney representing the Mississippi plaintiff, said in a statement ahead of the trial that "we look forward to educating the jury about the dangers of features like endless feeds, autoplay and streaks and how Meta – and allegedly Snap as well – have implemented and emphasized these features." A TEST CASE Plaintiffs S.J. and K.D.B. sued in 2023. Both described staying awake for hours scrolling social media, losing focus in class and engaging in self-harm using methods shown in social media videos. They are seeking unspecified compensatory and punitive damages. Their cases are among more than 3,000 lawsuits brought by individuals and others that have been consolidated in Los Angeles Superior Court. Their lawsuits have been selected as bellwethers, or test cases, meaning the verdict could influence how the companies and plaintiffs resolve the remaining cases. Social media companies have denied that their platforms were designed to addict young people, and have said they have taken action to make the apps safe for young users. They also have argued that they are [USN:L6N40D1C3 TEXT:"shielded from the claims"] by Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, a 1996 federal law that generally protects online platforms from liability over user-generated content. The trial judge disagreed that Section 230 bars claims over how the sites are designed, and allowed the suits by the two plaintiffs to go to trial. In the case decided in March, a Los Angeles jury found that Meta and YouTube were negligent, siding with a young woman referred to in court papers as Kaley G.M. There have been multiple cases scheduled for trial since then, but the companies have [USN:L6N43O148 TEXT:"settled the claims"] or, in some cases, the plaintiffs have [USN:L6N44H178 TEXT:"chosen to drop"] them. SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND STATES SUE [USN:L6N46C17C TEXT:"More than 3,800 lawsuits"] brought by states, school districts and individuals over similar claims are pending in federal court in California, court records showed. In August, Meta reached [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"settlements worth up to $18 billion"] to resolve claims made by nearly every US state and territory over the impact of its platforms on teen mental health. The company agreed as part of that deal to change how teens can access Instagram and Facebook. Members of Meta's senior legal team told reporters after that settlement that the company views the individual and school district cases as harder to prove at trial than cases brought by states because they require plaintiffs to directly link specific problems to its social media platforms. Meta is appealing the verdict in the case decided in March, arguing that Section 230 should have barred the claims by plaintiff Kaley G.M. A ruling in Meta's favor [USN:L6N40D1C3 TEXT:"on the issue"] could derail thousands of lawsuits over youth mental health and shield it from billions of dollars in potential liability that the company has said poses a serious threat to its future, according to experts.

item.title: Fed likely to go into wait-and-see mode on rates
item.description: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, less than a week ahead of critical US midterm elections centered on the cost of living, as central bank policymakers wait to see if inflation moderates or stays strong enough to warrant more hikes in borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, less than a week ahead of critical US midterm elections centered on the cost of living, as central bank policymakers wait to see if inflation moderates or stays strong enough to warrant more hikes in borrowing costs. Fed officials ahead of this week's two-day policy meeting had signaled the central bank could be patient after [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raising rates"] by a quarter of a percentage point last month. Maintaining the Fed's benchmark interest rate in the current 3.75%-4.00% range also would move the discussion beyond the November 3 midterm elections that will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republican Party retains control of Congress over the final two years of his term or cedes one or both legislative chambers to the Democrats. There is about a 90% probability that the Fed will hold rates steady when it issues its policy decision at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT), according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. Financial markets' focus, instead, has shifted to the likely pace and extent of future rate increases that investors see as inevitable given the [USN:L1N4610KT TEXT:"strength of inflation."] Economists and many Fed policymakers now see prices driven higher not just by the lingering energy cost shock from Trump's decision to attack Iran and the holdover effects of his tariffs, but by strong demand from the artificial intelligence industry and healthy consumer spending. Fed officials see demand-driven inflation as being more under their control, and concerns that price increases are broadening across the economy could lead some policymakers to dissent in favor of a rate hike that they feel is needed to keep inflation from accelerating. "Today, the question is not so much about whether the Fed will hike again, but about how many more hikes are to follow," Dario Perkins, TS Lombard's managing director for global macro, wrote in an analysis that suggested the Fed may be forced into a series of hikes "if the AI bubble doesn't burst." Given Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's promise in an August 28 speech to return inflation to 2% "at sufficient speed," Perkins said the central bank "will need to keep hiking until its target is in sight." Right now it is not, a fact Warsh will need to reconcile with any decision to hold rates steady. While the central bank's policy statement, which has shrunk considerably since the new Fed chief took over in late May, is not expected to provide much of an explanation, Warsh is likely to face questions about why such a pause was considered appropriate when he participates in a press conference scheduled to start at 2:30 p.m. EDT. PERSISTENT INFLATION The Fed's 2% inflation target is measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index. Initial estimates show the headline reading for that index, as well as related measures stripping out some volatile commodity and non-market prices, rose in September and remain lodged at 3% or higher on an annualized basis — with little progress seen in recent months. The PCE report for September will be released on Thursday, a day after the policy meeting concludes, but enough of the component data is in hand for policymakers to have a firm estimate of the numbers. Since Warsh took the helm at the Fed, some of the dynamics policymakers said might help lower inflation — like an end to the US-Israeli war with Iran and productivity improvements stemming from AI — have yet to materialize. After a summer lull that helped lower month-to-month inflation in June and July, the global benchmark oil price has since surged to around $114 a barrel, rising about 20% since the start of September. Prices for diesel fuel — a critical input for numerous industries including agriculture, construction and transportation — are near [USN:L6N46C131 TEXT:"record highs"] and have been a force behind the widening of inflation. The AI boom, meanwhile, has come to be seen across the Fed as a short-term driver of inflation regardless of its potential to make the economy more productive over the medium or long term. The breadth and persistence of inflation will be central as Fed officials debate the course of policy, even if they agree to leave rates on hold for now, Derek Tang, an economist at Monetary Policy Analytics, wrote ahead of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee's meeting this week. Tang's firm now sees the Fed approving three more quarter-percentage-point rate increases in its coming meetings, in line with market expectations of quarterly hikes from now through June 2027. To avoid seeming dovish after a pause in the wake of stronger inflation data, "Warsh will likely seek to couch the October skip against a wide backdrop of an FOMC still set on proving its mettle" in fighting inflation, Tang wrote. "Stopping the spread of inflation from idiosyncratic supply shocks to demand more broadly is top of mind for even the center of the Committee," which has grown more anxious that demand inflation is taking on a life of its own, he said.

item.title: Fed officials not aligned on weight of financial conditions
item.description: One issue dividing Federal Reserve officials over whether more interest rate hikes are needed as soon as this week is just how much weight to put on the loose financial conditions that many outside the US central bank see as a key driver of inflation in an accelerating economy.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: One issue dividing Federal Reserve officials over whether more interest rate hikes are needed [USN:L6N46D0VW TEXT:"as soon as this week"] is just how much weight to put on the loose financial conditions that many outside the US central bank see as a key driver of inflation in an accelerating economy. Financial conditions — denoted by things like short- and long-term borrowing costs and stock prices — are a key variable because the changes the Fed makes to the cost of short-term credit rely on markets to translate them to broader borrowing costs. On balance, a central bank that is on a rate-hike path to combat half a decade of above-target inflation would likely boost interest rates at the two-day meeting that is scheduled to conclude on Wednesday. But guidance from key officials suggests a majority of Fed policymakers will support leaving the central bank's benchmark interest rate [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"unchanged"] after unanimously agreeing to lift it by a quarter of a percentage point to the [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"3.75%-4.00%"] range in September. Investors expect a rate hike at the December 8-9 policy meeting. "Some people on the Fed have a financial conditions framework and some people don't," said William Dudley, who led the New York Fed from 2009 to 2018. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh "seems to think that financial conditions are important," but that sense is "not really ingrained" in terms of how "the Fed thinks about monetary policy" as an institution, Dudley said. Officials flagged by Dudley as sensitive to market conditions are those many believe are likely to dissent in favor of higher rates, including the Cleveland and Dallas Fed presidents and potentially the head of the Minneapolis Fed. Those three policymakers [USN:L6N43X0VQ TEXT:"dissented"] over the decision to leave rates unchanged in July, which was the second meeting of the Warsh-led era. Meanwhile, officials such as New York Fed President John Williams are more focused on economic data. Williams was one of the [USN:L6N45N16X TEXT:"key voices"] who boosted markets' bets that the Fed would hold rates steady this week. 'GOING FULL STEAM AHEAD' Understanding financial conditions is "part of my framework. It's something that I look at because I think it's really hard to know what neutral is" when it comes to setting central bank rate policy, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said earlier this month. Even with real-world borrowing costs having gone up, "most of what I'm hearing in my district is that they're going full steam ahead" and "when I look at financial conditions broadly, to me they don't seem restrictive" and they likely need to be to help the Fed get inflation back to its 2% target, Hammack said. Dudley agrees with the financial focus. "The US economy doesn't run on short rates; it runs on long rates, it runs on the stock market valuation, and it affects the household wealth," he said. "If you just focus on short-term rates and don't care about how that's influencing all these other factors, you're going to misjudge the stance of monetary policy." Private-sector economists generally agree that financial conditions are not in a place to help bring down price pressures. Goldman Sachs' closely watched financial conditions index for the US has tightened a bit since the Fed hiked rates on September 16, but is still close to where it was at the start of the year despite the more hawkish monetary policy path. Meanwhile, a survey of investors by Deutsche Bank showed 42% of respondents deemed financial conditions as "moderately accommodative," with only 15% saying they were restrictive. Analysts at Piper Sandler think monetary policy is likely misaligned with what the central bank wants from price pressures. "The Fed is still accommodative," the firm said, noting that an effective 3.9% federal funds rate was supporting growth and cushioning the economy from 5% bond yields, as reflected in banks' easing lending standards. Former Philadelphia Fed President Patrick Harker, now a professor at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, said getting to the bottom of financial conditions is a "complicated story" in which investment in the tech sector is very strong but not so elsewhere. As a result, he views the overall state of financial conditions as closer to neutral. Evercore ISI analysts said it would be better if the Fed had more clarity over financial conditions. "Warsh's focus on financial conditions without a well-defined FCI (Financial Conditions Index) framework is a vulnerability," they said in a note on Monday. In terms of Warsh's approach at the post-meeting press conference on Wednesday, "we think he will suggest somewhat tighter FCI could help extend the AI boom, though that could sound more persuasive to economists than investors," the Evercore ISI team said.

item.title: Michigan Senate race a test of attacks on Muslim candidate, progressive agenda
item.description: Michigan's tight race for an open US Senate seat will help determine control of the chamber while testing two broader questions: whether identity-based attacks on a Muslim candidate can succeed in a battleground state, and how willing Democratic voters are to embrace the party's progressive wing.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne
item.content:encoded: Michigan's tight race for an open US Senate seat will help determine control of the chamber while testing two broader questions: whether identity-based attacks on a Muslim candidate can succeed in a battleground state, and how willing Democratic voters are to embrace the party's progressive wing. Republican Mike Rogers has sought to portray Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who would be the nation's first Muslim senator if he wins the November 3 election , as sympathetic to Islamist extremism, which El-Sayed denies and supporters say is Islamophobic. Rogers has also argued that El-Sayed's support for universal healthcare and other progressive policies places him outside the political mainstream. El-Sayed, a former public health official, has focused his campaign on lowering costs for working-class Americans while seeking to tie Rogers to President Donald Trump , even as Rogers has [USN:L1N45T0KO TEXT:"broken with the president"] on some issues in the campaign's closing weeks. Trump has falsely accused El-Sayed of being a Muslim extremist, while Rogers has tried to tie him to the Muslim Brotherhood. Branches of the Brotherhood, one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist movements, were [USN:L1N3YE0QK TEXT:"designated as terrorist organizations"] by the Trump administration this year. El-Sayed has disavowed the group and denied any connection with it. [USN:L6N4661FE TEXT:"Pollsters and political strategists"] say the attacks are aimed at dissuading Jewish and Black voters in the Detroit area who backed his primary opponent, Representative Haley Stevens, from voting for him. "He's a Muslim-American and so Rogers is attempting to do his best to portray El-Sayed as an outsider who's dangerous," said Jonathan Hanson, a political scientist and public policy lecturer at the University of Michigan. Michigan's Senate seat is critical to both parties' efforts to control the chamber. Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority heading into Tuesday's election. Independent analysts rate the race a toss-up. The RealClearPolling average shows El-Sayed ahead by 2.5 percentage points in a state Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024. El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Cole Wozniak accused Rogers of resorting to "desperate, bad faith attacks" and said the Democrat was focused on "his plans to bring down costs and stand up to the chaos and corruption in Washington." Abby Ronson, a spokesperson for the Rogers campaign, pointed to Rogers' appearance on Sunday on NBC News' "Meet the Press," where he said he was not criticizing Islam but what he described as El-Sayed's adherence to a "radical Islamic agenda." IDENTITY ATTACKS Advocating policies to curb corporate influence and expand the social safety net, El-Sayed, 41, has emerged as one of the Democratic Party's most prominent progressives. He describes himself as a capitalist and rejects the socialist label, but a victory on Tuesday would likely be seen as a boost for the party's left wing as it seeks greater influence ahead of the 2028 presidential election. But the margin of any victory will matter, said Michigan State University political scientist Matt Grossmann. "If El-Sayed wins by a couple of points but trails Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson by a wide margin, that won't be a very convincing argument," Grossmann said. "And if El-Sayed were to lose, then it would be a mark against that faction of the party." Rogers, 63, has cast himself as a pragmatic conservative focused on lowering costs, boosting manufacturing and strengthening border security. With [USN:L6N46C17B TEXT:"Trump's popularity"] sagging, he recently called for an end to the war in Iran and the trade dispute with Canada, while avoiding direct criticism of the president. But portraying El-Sayed as a national security threat has also become a central feature of Rogers' closing message. Rogers has based that claim in part on a 2012 group letter signed by El-Sayed and other Egyptian Americans in support of then-newly elected Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood. The letter called on Morsi to purge the media and security services of holdovers from the dictatorship toppled during the Arab Spring. The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to a query about the letter. Earlier this month Rogers agreed with a social media post calling El-Sayed a terrorist. He also appeared with [USN:L1N469003 TEXT:"Trump at a rally"] on Sunday where the president likened El-Sayed to the September 11 attackers and said his goal was to keep a "jihadist" out of the Senate. The rhetoric prompted a rare rebuke from the NAACP, the nonpartisan civil rights organization, which does not typically intervene in political races. "The blatantly racist attacks surrounding the Michigan Senate race are unacceptable and disgusting," NAACP President Derrick Johnson said in a statement. "It’s the same ugly, divisive tactics we’ve seen used during the darkest chapters of the South’s history." A poll by Michigan State University's Institute for Public Policy and Social Research found that 38% of Michigan voters were less likely to support a Muslim candidate. John Clark, a political science professor at Western Michigan University, said the attacks on El-Sayed were aimed in part at depressing Democratic turnout but could work against Rogers by angering and boosting turnout among Michigan's sizable Arab American communities in Dearborn and elsewhere. "Maybe this helps with some voters, but it has the potential of backfiring with others," Clark said.

item.title: Nevada unions, politicians caught between AI job creation and destruction
item.description: On more than 100,000 acres of Nevada desert east of Reno, one of the world's largest concentrations of data centers is taking shape, providing years of work for thousands of electricians, pipefitters and other union tradespeople who are building it.
item.dc:creator: Valerie Volcovici
item.content:encoded: On more than 100,000 acres of Nevada desert east of Reno, one of the world's largest concentrations of data centers is taking shape, providing years of work for thousands of electricians, pipefitters and other union tradespeople who are building it. About 400 miles southeast, along the iconic Las Vegas Strip, the AI technology powered by such data centers is taking a toll: Self-driving Zoox and Waymos are replacing human-driven taxis and valets; casino floor bartenders are being replaced by robots; and MGM's (MGM.N) massive call center is slashing hundreds of jobs. That split screen is challenging the Nevada Teamsters, a politically powerful network of local labor unions representing 30,000 workers across the construction, transportation and hospitality industries, many of whom will be voting in the Nov. 3 elections. Some want to see new data-center construction halted or slowed. Others view the boom as a gift. "My job is to represent all of our unions," said Ross Kinson, the Nevada Teamsters’ political director, adding the group had launched a process in April to find a unified stance ahead of the November polls. "This is a very, very important issue to the building trades, and it's providing a lot of jobs and creating good opportunities for a lot of people." But, he said, he has been encouraging members to consider the flip side: "What is it doing to our jobs?" Nevada unions’ soul-searching reflects the national debate underway over whether regulation should slow down AI development amid conflicting projections of job destruction and creation – and whether AI will ultimately lift humanity or harm it. It’s likely to affect Nevada's voting on Nov. 3. The Nevada Teamsters interviewed more than 180 political candidates from both parties ahead of the election, Kinson said. Those who didn’t support strong worker protections, or those looking for an outright ban on new data-center construction, were unlikely to win the union's backing. "It's a political minefield for politicians to tiptoe through," said Kinson. Nevada will also play a significant role in the 2028 presidential elections as the second state in the Democratic primary schedule behind South Carolina. ROBOT BARTENDERS On a suburban street just off the Las Vegas Strip, 63-year-old Larry Goldfinger and a group of fellow Teamsters he jokingly calls "the walking dead" trudge through the desert heat, clipboards in hand. They’re knocking on doors to promote candidates they believe will protect the city’s workers from AI-driven job losses. Goldfinger has spent nearly three decades as a valet at some of the Strip's most iconic casinos, and another decade in Vegas hospitality jobs – work he now fears will dry up as AI automation takes over everything from concierge services to bartending. "I raised my family, and I have had a good life doing it, and I feel like these guys that are 30ish aren't going to be able to do that," he said, wearing a Teamsters baseball cap to shield his head from the Nevada sun. By 2035, AI and automation could put up to 92,000 Southern Nevada hospitality jobs at risk, or roughly one-third of that workforce, according to an analysis by RCG Economics. Teamsters Local 986 has already been losing call-center workers at casinos to AI automation, while taxi drivers and valets face pressure from the expansion of autonomous-vehicle fleets operated by Waymo and Zoox. Robot bartenders and touchscreen hotel check-ins have also become increasingly common. MGM Resorts laid off around 200 call-center workers last year, Kinson said. On a recent investor call, MGM International CFO Jonathan Halkyard said about 80% of guest interactions "now take place via AI/digital platforms." MGM declined to comment for this story but directed Reuters to a labor contract it had reached with culinary union members in 2023. It promised advanced notice of AI-driven job losses along with health care and severance pay for those affected. The Las Vegas economy is no stranger to booms, busts and technological change. But how it navigates the AI-era will have huge consequences, said John Restrepo, principal of RCG Economics. "If they use those tools to just do massive job displacement, that's not going to be good," he said. Goldfinger said he worries the rise of AI in Las Vegas will not only cost the city lots of jobs, but also ultimately hurt business by making it less welcoming to tourists accustomed to interacting with well-trained hospitality staff. "We are not against the changes," he said. "We just want to make sure we are involved in how it's changing." NEW GOLD RUSH Every morning, Christopher Williams joins the traffic along the USA Parkway in northern Nevada's high desert on his way to an expanding cluster of data centers owned by Google (GOOGL.O) , Switch, Tract and others in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center. The historic mining region was the site of a 19th-century gold rush, briefly earning Storey County the label of "the richest place on earth." Williams, a 20-year-old with curly black hair and glasses, is part of the new rush, this time for high-paying data-center jobs. He moved from northern California to Reno last year after struggling to get enough hours as a line cook earning $18.50 an hour. Now he’s making more than $22 an hour and works 45 to 60 hours a week. "I might not fully agree with data centers being built everywhere, but they are helping a lot of people," he said. "If I don't take the job, somebody else will, and it's a lot of money left on the table." For local officials, the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center has been a lifeline after a prolonged economic slump. "We're finding that our economy is more stable than it used to be as a primarily gaming and tourism economy, and it's providing opportunities, especially for young people that want to stay," said County Commissioner Clay Mitchell. According to the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center has generated 850,000 work hours per month in 2026 – up from about the same number during all of 2022. BABY AND THE BATHWATER The Nevada Teamsters’ internal discussions have led it to endorse Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford for governor, Kinson said. Ford, who is seeking to unseat Republican incumbent Governor Joe Lombardo, has proposed halting new data-center tax abatements and requiring developers to shield residents from higher energy costs, and also wants strong regulation protecting jobs from AI - the right balance to appeal to the spectrum of Teamsters unions, Kinson said. Ford had consulted with the Teamsters before launching his data-center platform this summer and hosted his first town hall about the issue at the Teamsters Local 14. Lombardo has championed data centers as a major economic driver, calling the industry a "new gold rush", but had been slower to embrace checks and balances on the industry, according to Kinson. In September, Lombardo imposed new restrictions on some of the generous tax incentives that lured the industry to the state. Lombardo did not respond to requests for comment. The union’s influence tends to be significant. In 2025, union members accounted for about 13% of wage and salary workers in Nevada, compared to 10% nationwide, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. In other parts of the United States, the data-center issue has also been key to union endorsement decisions. In Kansas, for example, Republican gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson won backing from the state's largest transit and railroad union, as well as from a local chapter of the IBEW electrical workers union, after Democratic rival Cindy Holscher called for a moratorium on data-center development. It marked the first time in more than 50 years that the Kansas transit union backed a Republican candidate for governor. Sean McGarvey, president of North America's Building Trades Unions, said – just like in Nevada – there is a division in the wider labor community around AI and data centers. But banning new data centers, he said, will never get their support. "We don't throw the baby out with the bathwater," he said. "This is one of those once-in-a-lifetime opportunities to reindustrialize the country."

item.title: ＶＷ、中国開発技術を海外展開 南米・南アで競争力強化へ
item.description: [合肥（中国） ２８日 ロイター] - ドイツ自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）は、中国で開発した技術を南米や南アフリ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＶＷ、中国開発技術を海外展開　南米・南アで競争力強化へ 19:00 配信

2月、中国安徽省合肥にあるフォルクスワーゲン工場で撮影。 REUTERS/Florence Lo（ロイター） [合肥（中国） ２８日 ロイター] - ドイツ自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）は、中国で開発した技術を南米や南アフリカなどの海外市場に展開する。中国を重要な技術革新拠点として活用し、世界市場での競争力強化を目指す。

ＶＷは２８日、中国東部の合肥市にある研究開発拠点が中国企業と共同開発した電子制御基盤「チャイナ・エレクトロニック・アーキテクチャー（ＣＥＡ）」を備える車台「コンパクト・メイン・プラットフォーム」を、グローバルサウス市場向けの次世代モデルに採用すると発表した。２０２０年代末までに南米で展開を開始する。

ＶＷグループのオリバー・ブルーメ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は声明で「中国はＶＷグループの技術革新を支える重要な原動力であり、世界市場に向けた製品・技術の拠点としても重要性を増している」と表明。「われわれはこれを『中国で、中国を超えて』と呼んでいる」と明らかにした。

今回の動きは、従来の「中国で、中国のために」という現地化戦略からの転換を示す。ＶＷは中国販売の立て直しや、小鵬汽車（シャオペン）、地平線機器人（ホライズン・ロボティクス）など現地パートナーとの技術提携を商業的な成功につなげることに苦戦している。

ＶＷは創業以来８９年の歴史で最大の事業再編を進める中、中国事業をかつての利益の源泉から、コスト効率の高い開発・輸出拠点へと転換することを目指している。今後数年間で、中国製のＶＷブランド車とジェッタブランド車の南米・アフリカ向け輸出を増やす計画も発表した。

ゼネラル・モーターズ（ＧＭ）や現代自動車、ルノーなど既存の自動車メーカーも、国際市場で中国勢と競う中、中国で開発した技術を世界に展開する同様の戦略を採用する動きを加速させている。

ＶＷは技術面の進展の一環として、８５０ボルトの急速充電に対応し、自動運転「レベル３」に対応する準備を整えた技術パッケージ「ＶＥＧＡ」も披露した。２０２７年の導入を予定している。

＜縮小する市場シェア＞

今回の戦略更新は、ＶＷが中国での市場シェア低下に直面する中で行われた。中国では比亜迪（ＢＹＤ）や吉利汽車などの国内勢が、電気自動車（ＥＶ）やソフトウエア、価格競争で外資勢をしのいでいる。

ＶＷがこれまで対応策として進めてきたのが「中国で、中国のために」という現地化戦略だった。同グループによると、開発の現地化により開発期間を最大３０％短縮できる。また、小鵬と共同開発したＣＥＡは、複数の車台や駆動方式にわたって、ソフトウエアで機能を制御・更新する車両を支えることを目指している。

ＶＷは現在の中国での新車投入攻勢を、同市場で「主導権を取り戻す」取り組みの一環と位置付けている。

中国で開発したモデルの投入先候補として東南アジア、中南米、アフリカを挙げる一方、欧州と北米は当面対象から外している。

こうした方針は、中国自動車メーカーの動きと重なる。中国勢は国内競争の激化や生産能力の拡大を背景に、自国市場での成長維持が難しくなる中、輸出を一段と積極化している。

ＶＷの中国事業トップ、ラルフ・ブランドシュテッター氏は、中国の乗用車市場が２０２６年に２０％、台数にして約４５０万台縮小すると予想している。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず コラム：「カメ」の米国株が「ウサギ」の中国を追い抜く時 10/28(水) 19:00 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: 伊インテーザのモンテ・デイ・パスキ買収、ＥＣＢが承認
item.description:
Valentina Za
[ミラノ ２７日 ロイター] - イタリア最大の銀行インテーザ・サンパオロは２７日、モンテ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
伊インテーザのモンテ・デイ・パスキ買収、ＥＣＢが承認 18:58 配信

イタリア中部シエナのモンテ・デイ・パスキ銀行に入る男性。２０１６年１月撮影。 REUTERS/Max Rossi（ロイター） Valentina Za

[ミラノ ２７日 ロイター] - イタリア最大の銀行インテーザ・サンパオロは２７日、モンテ・デイ・パスキ・ディ・シエナ（ＭＰＳ）の経営権取得について、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の承認を得たと発表した。総額３２０億ユーロ（３６０億ドル）の買収提案の実施に向け大きく前進した。

今後はイタリアの市場規制当局、国家証券委員会（ＣＯＮＳＯＢ）の判断に焦点が移る。ＣＯＮＳＯＢは１１月上旬に公開買い付けに関する書類を承認する見通しで、その後、独禁当局が１１月後半に判断を下すとみられる。

インテーザはＣＯＮＳＯＢの承認を得れば、独禁当局の判断を待たずに公開買い付けを開始できる。買い付け期間は数週間に及ぶため、投資家は期間終了までに独禁当局の判断を検討する時間を確保できる。

ＥＣＢはまた、インテーザによるメディオバンカの間接的な経営権取得も承認した。ＭＰＳは昨年メディオバンカを買収した。

item.title: EQT, Bain $5 billion Kakaku showdown heralds contested Japan buyout era
item.description: TOKYO, Oct 28 : A battle between private equity firms EQT and Bain to acquire a $5 billion Japanese internet company illustrates how takeovers in Japan are becoming increasingly contested, with the participation of strategic buyers helping push up prices.EQT bid for Kakaku.com in May, only for Bain to team up
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

EQT, Bain $5 billion Kakaku showdown heralds contested Japan buyout era

FILE PHOTO: A view shows EQT AB's logo at the company's office in Tokyo, Japan May 13, 2025. REUTERS/Miho Uranaka/File Photo

28 Oct 2026 05:57PM

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 28 : A battle between private equity firms EQT and Bain to acquire a $5 billion Japanese internet company illustrates how takeovers in Japan are becoming increasingly contested, with the participation of strategic buyers helping push up prices. EQT bid for Kakaku.com in May, only for Bain to team up with SoftBank Group subsidiary LY Corp and submit a rival offer. That sparked a six-month bidding war in which EQT has hiked its offer price seven times to try to secure the support of Kakaku shareholders. It is the highest-profile takeover battle since KKR fended off Bain last year to buy Fuji Soft in a deal valuing the software firm at $4.1 billion, as private equity firms face off in a country relatively unused to contentious takeover battles. As more funds are taking more companies private, prospective buyers are factoring in the risk of battles and rising prices, dealmakers said. The trend of private equity firms working with non-financial firms, like Bain and LY, is also pushing up prices, they said.

Financial sponsor-backed M&A deals in Japan totalled $24 billion in January-September, just shy of a year earlier but almost double the $13 billion in the same period of 2024, LSEG data showed. Other contested deals include CVC and KKR's bid for cosmetics firm Mandom, and on Tuesday the Nikkei reported that Advantage Partners has countered Integral with a bid for Kadoya Sesame Mills. In the battle for Kakaku, EQT extended its offer period for the 10th time on Wednesday, with the deadline for shareholders to tender at the latest price of 3,683 yen ($23) a share on November 12. Bain and LY raised their offer to 3,700 yen on Monday, rising to 3,720 if they secure the support of Kakaku's third-largest shareholder KDDI. Kakaku's shares ended trading at 3,747 yen on Wednesday, indicating that market participants think further price hikes are possible. STRATEGIC COMPANIES SEE SYNERGY  Companies operating in the same sector as buyout targets may see more growth potential in the targets than funds acting alone so the idea of bidding together is gaining traction, said Yusuke Watanabe, a partner at private equity firm Carlyle. This trend is likely to push up the price of final bids, he said. LY, which operates the Line messaging app and Yahoo Japan internet portal, considered bidding for Kakaku in recent years, a person familiar with the matter said. When the media reported EQT's interest in April, LY decided to join Bain and make a counteroffer, the person said, declining to be identified as deliberations were private. LY has said it sees synergies between its internet businesses and Kakaku's price comparison website Kakaku.com and restaurant review website Tabelog.com. Such synergies include referring customers to LY's online services and integrating them into the payments ecosystem of SoftBank's digital wallet PayPay. In a similar case last month, telecommunications firm Hikari Tsushin joined forces with private equity firm MBK Partners and NEC Capital Solutions to buy Leopalace21, aiming to provide internet, gas and electricity to Leopalace's managed rental properties. Bringing in a strategic buyer also offers an exit option when funds struggle to offload investments, said Gregory Salathé, a partner at Freshfields law firm. EXPECTING MULTIPLE BIDDERS Such is the expectation for multiple bidders that a target is likely to consider auctioning itself rather than negotiating with a suitor, as was previously the norm, said Akihiko Manaka, co-head of investment banking and co-head of M&A in Japan at Bank of America. "If it's a good asset, the sort of company everyone wants, competition is naturally fierce, making it difficult to buy cheaply," Manaka said. "The buyers really have to work for it." ($1 = 157.4700 yen)

Source: Reuters

item.title: 仏レミー・コアントロー、7─9月期売上高が予想上回る 株価は下落
item.description: [２８日 ロイター] - フランスの酒造大手レミー・コアントローは２８日、第２・四半期（７─９月）の売上高がオーガニ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
仏レミー・コアントロー、7─9月期売上高が予想上回る　株価は下落 18:57 配信

2019年2月、仏フランスのアンジェ近郊にあるコアントロー蒸留所で撮影。 REUTERS/Stephane Mahe（ロイター） [２８日 ロイター] - フランスの酒造大手レミー・コアントローは２８日、第２・四半期（７─９月）の売上高がオーガニックベースで４．２％増加したと発表した。中秋節を控え中国向けコニャック出荷が加速したことで予想を上回ったものの、投資家が回復見通しに懸念を示したことから、株価は５％下落した。

同グループは米国の販売代理店による在庫削減や中国での需要低迷によって引き起こされた長期にわたる不振を受け、成長の回復を目指している。

• 第２・四半期のオーガニック売上高は４．２％増の２億８０１０万ユーロ（３億１１４７万ドル）となり、会社がまとめたコンセンサス予想の平均値である３．６％増を上回った。

• コニャックのオーガニック売上高は１２．４％増の１億８９９０万ユーロとなり、アナリスト予想の１億８６４０万ユーロを上回った。

• 同グループは通期業績見通しを確認した。

• TP ICAP Midcapのアナリストらは、同グループの回復はすでに株価に反映されているとし、最近の株価上昇を受けてリスク・リターン比の魅力が低下したと指摘した。

item.title: スペインで高速列車衝突、30人死亡 9カ月前にも同路線で事故
item.description:
Emma Pinedo Victoria Waldersee
[マドリード ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Emma Pinedo　Victoria Waldersee

[マドリード ２８日 ロイター] - スペインで２８日、マドリードと南部アンダルシア地方のセビリアを結ぶ路線で高速列車同士が衝突し、地元当局によると少なくとも３０人が死亡した。

９カ月前にも同路線で同じ運営会社の高速列車同士が衝突する事故があり、４６人が死亡していた。

カスティーリャ・ラマンチャ・テレビの映像には、脱線した列車の少なくとも１両が高架区間に残り、線路下の斜面にねじ曲がった金属や壊れたパネルなどが散乱する様子が映っていた。

カスティーリャ・ラマンチャ州政府報道官は、午前９時（日本時間午後５時）過ぎに「レンフェ」と「イリョ」の列車が衝突し、イリョの車両２両が脱線したと述べた。死者が３０人となった。

事故の状況について説明を受けた関係者によると、民間高速鉄道会社イリョが運行する列車が信号の不具合により、国有鉄道インフラ管理会社（ＡＤＩＦ）の指示でトレド近郊に停車していたところ、スペイン国鉄（レンフェ）が運行する列車が衝突、双方の複数の車両が脱線した。

州政府報道官によると、イリョの列車には１４７人、レンフェの列車には３９７人が乗っていた。

１月の事故では、コルドバ近郊のアダムスで列車が脱線し、対向列車に衝突。近年の鉄道保守への投資水準を巡る議論を引き起こした。

スペイン政府のウェブサイトに掲載されていたサンチェス首相の当日の予定は全て取り消された。野党の国民党も全ての選挙イベントを中止した。

＜鉄道の安全＞

スペインの鉄道安全当局によると、脱線や衝突などの事故は２０１６年の４５件から２４年に５７件、２５年には６９件に増加した。同期間にレールの劣化や破断などの問題は４９４件から６６７件に増えたが、２４年の７１６件は下回った。

ロイターによるスペイン当局データの分析によると、２６年上半期の高速鉄道利用客は約２５００万人で、前年同期から約１４％減少した。

欧州委員会のデータによると、スペインは高速鉄道網の拡大を他に類を見ない勢いで進め、総延長は４０００キロ程度及んでいるが、保守への投資は欧州主要国に後れを取っている。

スペインは２０１８─２２年に高速鉄道網に年間平均約１５億ユーロを支出し、他のどの国よりも多かった。ただ、その大半は新たなインフラに向けられ、保守や取替・改良に充てられたのは約１６％にとどまった。

欧州連合（ＥＵ）統計局の入手可能な最新の２４年のデータによると、スペインの鉄道事故による死亡率は域内で最も低い水準にあった。線路１０００キロ当たりの死者は１人以下だった。

ＥＵ鉄道機関によると、スペインの鉄道網の９０％以上にＥＵで最高水準の安全制御システムが導入されている。欧州共通の信号規格を導入した路線はベルギー、スイスに並んで最も長いという。

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for higher open as SK Hynix lifts chips; Fed in focus
item.description: US stocks were on track to open higher on Wednesday as memory-chip firms climbed after SK Hynix's bumper results, while investors looked to upcoming key corporate earnings as the next test of AI trade, alongside the Federal Reserve's rate decision.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Chauhan, Utkarsh Hathi
item.content:encoded: US stocks were on track to open higher on Wednesday as memory-chip firms climbed after SK Hynix's bumper results, while investors looked to upcoming key corporate earnings as the next test of AI trade, alongside the Federal Reserve's rate decision. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU.O) gained 3.6% in premarket trading after South Korean rival SK Hynix (000660.KS) reported a more than sevenfold jump in [USN:L2N46D1DE TEXT:"quarterly profit"]. SK Hynix's US-listed shares jumped 7.5%. Data storage firms Sandisk (SNDK.O) and Western Digital (WDC.O) rose 4.1% and 1.4%, respectively, while Seagate Technology (STX.O) was an outlier, down 2.5%, after [USN:L2N46D14B TEXT:"reporting"] its first-quarter results. The broader semiconductor segment was also trading higher, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) up 0.9%, while AMD (AMD.O) and Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) each added 1.5%. Alphabet (GOOGL.O) advanced 1.3% following a [USN:L6N46E00G TEXT:"media report"] that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips. At 08:16 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 36 points, or 0.07%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 16.25 points, or 0.21%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 123.5 points, or 0.41%. The Nasdaq (.IXIC) has gained around 2% so far this week, following a bruising first half of the month, as sentiment toward AI improved after Anthropic revealed its US [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"IPO filing"] on Monday. The focus now shifts to quarterly results from hyperscalers Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Alphabet, due after markets close on Wednesday, with both companies [USN:L3N46D1FP TEXT:"expected"] to report accelerating cloud growth. Investors will closely scrutinize their capital expenditure plans for signs that massive AI investments are generating returns, as concerns over the viability of debt-funded spending amid rising borrowing costs continue to weigh on the sector. "Demand remains strong, but with capex still accelerating, the market is increasingly focused on what all that spending ultimately produces," said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion. "The more skeptical the market gets about AI returns, the harder it becomes to justify today's pace of spending." Amazon.com (AMZN.O) and chipmaker Intel (INTC.O) are among major technology companies that are expected to report later this week. On the day, Vertiv (VRT.N) jumped 17% after the digital infrastructure provider [USN:L2N46E0EI TEXT:"raised"] full-year profit and revenue forecasts, while also topping third-quarter expectations. Robinhood Markets (HOOD.O) dropped 6.5% after the trading platform [USN:L3N46D1Y4 TEXT:"missed"] Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit, while payment processing giant Visa (V.N) dipped 1.6% following its [USN:L3N46D1XW TEXT:"fourth-quarter results"]. Looking ahead, the US Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision is due at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday, with the market consensus [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"widely tilted"] toward a pause following last month's hike. Market expectations, however, remain hawkish as traders see at least three 25-basis-point increases by late 2027, according to LSEG data, as persistently high inflation due to rising energy costs tied to the Middle East conflict bolster the case for tighter monetary policy. September's Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, could test those bets on Thursday. Third-quarter GDP, which is expected to show 3.2% growth, is also due this week.

item.title: Indian miner Vedanta on track to eliminate net debt by December-end, CEO says
item.description: India's Vedanta is on track to eliminate net debt by the end of the third quarter, its CEO told Reuters on Wednesday, after the metals-to-oil conglomerate posted a rise in quarterly profit on firm base metal prices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Vedanta (VDAN.NS) is on track to eliminate net debt by the end of the third quarter, its CEO told Reuters on Wednesday, after the metals-to-oil conglomerate posted a rise in quarterly profit on firm base metal prices. Here are the details: The Mumbai-based miner's net debt stood at 532.54 billion Indian rupees ($5.59 billion) at the end of fiscal 2026. The company is on track to eliminate that debt by the end of the third quarter, CEO Arun Misra told Reuters in an interview. Consolidated net profit more than doubled to 36.50 billion rupees ($383.45 million) for the quarter ended September 30. Overall revenue jumped 57% to 258.12 billion rupees Higher average zinc prices in the July-September quarter had been expected to boost revenue growth at Vedanta's India zinc business, Emkay Global analysts said Spot zinc prices climbed 35% on-year, according to Jefferies data, on tight supply conditions Copper rose 44%, benefiting from supply constraints and demand linked to electrification and energy-transition projects, Jefferies data showed Lead prices dropped 6% due to weak growth in demand, while the demand-supply equation remained more or less balanced Higher commodity prices typically support selling prices and margins for mining companies Vedanta's net profit margins expanded to 24% from 13% a year earlier Revenue from the company's combined India zinc and lead segment rose 59.5% The firm's cost of raw materials climbed 42.5%, pushing total expenses higher by nearly 34% to 184.76 billion rupees Last week, Vedanta group company Hindustan Zinc (HZNC.NS) posted a more than [USN:L4N4650QO TEXT:"twofold jump"] in quarterly profit, helped by higher metal prices, and cut its annual zinc production cost forecast amid rising output and stronger by-product realisations ($1 = 95.1875 Indian rupees) (This story has been corrected to say that profit more than doubled, not rose 9.1%, in bullet 3.)

item.title: Hegseth Pledges Stronger U.S.-ASEAN Defense Ties as China Tensions Persist
item.description: By Mikhail Flores and Karen Lema U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth sought to reassure Southeast Asian counterparts on Wednesday of Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific, pledging that Washington would defend its interests and those of its allies and partners. Hegseth, who is participating in the …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Mikhail Flores and Karen Lema

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth sought to reassure Southeast Asian counterparts on Wednesday of Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific, pledging that Washington would defend its interests and those of its allies and partners.

Hegseth, who is participating in the two-day ASEAN defense ministers and related meetings in Cebu, Philippines, said the U.S. would back that commitment with practical cooperation, including stronger maritime domain awareness, greater interoperability and cooperation among navies.

“These are not symbolic things. They are concrete demonstrations of what serious partners do,” he said. “Serious partners train together, learn together, plan together and build confidence and competence necessary to prevent conflict.”

Hegseth is visiting the region as governments in Southeast Asia and the wider Asian region weigh Washington’s ability to stay focused on the Asia Pacific as the Iran war strains U.S. military resources and creates political pressure at home.

The defense secretary described the U.S. approach as “strong, quiet and clear,” saying it would be “strong enough to deter coercion and aggression,” quiet enough to avoid “needless escalation or public theatrics,” and clear enough that friends and potential adversaries understood Washington’s position.

“We will defend our interests and the interests of our allies and partners. That is, by definition, peace through strength,” Hegseth said.

Hegseth also proposed developing a U.S.-ASEAN framework for defense cooperation to guide ties during what he said would be the “critically important next several years,” as the two sides mark half a century of formal relations next year.

Economies Grappling With Iran War Impact

Southeast Asia is grappling with the effects of the Iran war, while tension between the Philippines and Beijing has added another source of friction to a forum meant to promote dialogue and practical cooperation on security.

The Iran war, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on February 28, has disrupted global shipping and oil markets, exposing Southeast Asia’s vulnerability to imported-fuel shocks and pushing energy security further up ASEAN’s agenda.

Greg Poling, director of the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, which tracks developments in the South China Sea, said Hegseth would get an opportunity at the gathering to tackle aspects regarding China, the South China Sea and Washington’s commitments to its treaty allies.

The topic is critical for the Philippines, a U.S. treaty ally whose ties with Beijing have soured amid repeated confrontations in the disputed South China Sea, Chinese sanctions and, more recently, a summoning of the Chinese ambassador.

China claims almost the entire South China Sea while other countries in Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia, claim parts of it.

China’s defense attaché in the Philippines will attend the meeting, its defense ministry said on Tuesday.

Days before the meeting, the Philippine military said it monitored and shadowed China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier group as it passed through waters off the southern Philippines toward the Celebes Sea.

Stronger signals were more likely to figure in talks among like-minded partners, added Poling.

Such partners include the “Squad”, an informal grouping of the United States, Japan, Australia and the Philippines, whose defense chiefs are set to meet on October 28. Hegseth will also join an expanded defense ministers’ meeting on October 29, bringing together ASEAN’s 11 members and eight partners, including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea and Russia.

Eventual Chairman’s Statement Seen as Restrained

The eventual chairman’s statement was likely to be more restrained than talks behind closed doors and would employ familiar ASEAN language, said Collin Koh, a security scholar at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies.

Manila’s position as ASEAN chair while embroiled in a dispute with China was “particularly sensitive”, he added.

Poling said the Philippines had to balance “aspirational cooperation” on issues such as energy connectivity, the digital economy and coast guard cooperation against rising tension with China and stalled progress on a South China Sea code of conduct.

“For the Philippines, the whole ASEAN chair year has been a difficult balance,” added Poling, who is also a fellow with the Southeast Asia Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“I’d expect tactical cooperation on the ADMM workstreams … but no strategic alignment on the South China Sea or other thorny issues,” he said, referring to the bloc’s effort to tackle issues such as maritime security and counterterrorism.

item.title: ＪＡＬ、予約情報9万件超に不正アクセス 一部パスポート番号も
item.description: ［東京 ２８日 ロイター］ - 日本航空（ＪＡＬ）は２８日、旅客サービスシステムの委託先への不正アクセスにより約９...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＪＡＬ、予約情報9万件超に不正アクセス　一部パスポート番号も 18:31 配信

ＪＡＬのロゴ。2020年10月、羽田空港で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato（ロイター） ［東京　２８日　ロイター］ - 日本航空（ＪＡＬ）は２８日、旅客サービスシステムの委託先への不正アクセスにより約９万２０００件の予約情報が外部から参照されていたと発表した。

対象は２３年８月１０日から２６年９月２３日の間に委託先システム上に存在していた予約記録の一部で、９万人の予約番号や氏名、搭乗日、搭乗区間など。加えて２０００人分については連絡先、パスポート番号、国籍などにもアクセスがあった可能性がある。

クレジットカード番号やパスワードの漏えいはないという。

対象となる顧客には個別に連絡するなど、必要な対応を行うとしている。

item.title: コメディアン襲撃関与巡る台湾の非難、中国「でっち上げ」と一蹴
item.description: [北京 ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２８日 ロイター] - 中国政府を風刺する公演で知られる台湾のコメディアンに対する襲撃を計画したとして、台湾の検察が５人を起訴したことを受け、中国政府の報道官は２８日、台湾が「対立をあおり」、反中感情をかき立てていると非難した。

台湾政府は、中国の習近平国家主席を風刺したコメディアンの黄逸豪氏が９月に襲撃された事件の背後に中国がいたと主張している。

台湾事務弁公室の陳斌華報道官は北京での定例記者会見で事件について問われ、台湾側の非難は与党・民進党のでっち上げだと一蹴した。

１１月の台湾の地方選挙を念頭に「いわゆる『国境を越えた弾圧』という言説は、本質的には台湾独立を推進し、２国家論を広めるためのもので、台湾で選挙があるたびに持ち出される」と発言した。

「民進党は何の根拠もなくあらゆる口実をでっち上げ、悪意を持って中国を中傷し、反中感情をかき立て、中台間の対立をあおっている。いずれも台湾の人々を欺いて権力を握ろうとするものだ」と述べた。これは毎年繰り返される「使い古された手口」だとも語った。

台湾の頼清徳総統は同日、民進党の週例会議で、「国境を越えた弾圧」は、台湾の民主制度に対する人々の信頼を損なうために中国が使い得る手段だと述べた。「中国が台湾の選挙に介入する狙いは、投票結果を直接変えようとすることだけではない。偽情報を広め、社会の分断を深め、集団間の憎悪をあおることも含まれる」と語った。

item.title: ステランティス、第3四半期増益 キャッシュアウト40億ユーロ
item.description:
Giulio Piovaccari Gilles Guillaume
[ミラノ ２８日 ロイター] - 欧米自動車大手...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ステランティス、第3四半期増益　キャッシュアウト40億ユーロ 18:19 配信

5月、パリ近郊のあるステランティスのオフィスビル。 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier（ロイター） Giulio Piovaccari　Gilles Guillaume

[ミラノ ２８日 ロイター] - 欧米自動車大手ステランティスが２８日発表した第３・四半期決算は、調整後ＥＢＩＴ（利払い・税引き前利益）が２億５６００万ユーロになった。前年同期の９０００万ユーロから増加したほか、アナリスト予想の１億９１００万ユーロを上回った。

ステランティスは緩やかな事業再建プロセスを進めており、同四半期においても依然として４０億ユーロ（４４億５０００万ドル）の事業活動によるキャッシュアウトが発生。２月に電気自動車（ＥＶ）関連で２２０億ユーロを超える減損を発表した同社が、持続的な回復軌道に乗っていることを投資家に納得させるにはまだ道半ばだ。

第３・四半期の売上高は３７６億ユーロとほぼ横ばいだった。欧州と南米ではわずかに増加した一方、ステランティスにとって歴史的に最も収益性の高い市場である北米では３％の減少となった。

２０２６年の業績見通しと、２７年のキャッシュフロー黒字化回帰目標を確認。これはアントニオ・フィロサ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が今年開始したグループ全体のコスト削減計画による効果が計上されるため。

フィロサ氏は発表文で「当社の『バリュー・クリエーション・プログラム』は急速に軌道に乗り、当四半期にはプラスの貢献が認められた。また、年間６０億ユーロに上る効率化目標の少なくとも４０％を今年末までに達成する見通しだ」と述べた。

第４・四半期には「数億ユーロ台半ば」、つまり約５億ユーロのコスト削減が見込まれており、これは第３・四半期実績額の約２倍に相当するという。

また、ステランティスは、業績不振に陥っている高級車ブランド「マセラティ」について、１２月１０日に新たな事業計画を示すと発表した。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：欧州の中銀関係者、米国との協調維持に不安　市場介入に懸念 アングル：欧州の猛暑、経済損失は過去最大規模の恐れ　観光の変化で南欧に大打撃 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント アングル：欧州、熱波で気候変動への無防備さ露呈　「適応」対策が急務 10/28(水) 18:19 最終更新 ロイター

Oct 28 : Robinhood's shares fell 8 per cent in premarket trading on Wednesday after a prolonged chill in crypto markets dragged the trading platform's third-quarter profit below Wall Street expectations. Crypto markets have been under pressure this year due to shifting expectations for US interest rates, outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded funds and bouts of risk aversion that have unsettled investors and sparked waves of selling. Here are more details: • Robinhood's cryptocurrencies revenue fell 55 per cent in the third quarter to $120 million

item.title: 独首相、先端技術の協力拡大呼び掛け 経産相は日本製ＥＶで懸念表明
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２８日 ロイター] - ドイツのメルツ首相の来日に合わせて２８日、都内で日独ハイレベル経済サミットが開催され、メルツ氏は「世界が根本的に変化する中で、日独のパートナーシップがますます重要になっている」と述べ、半導体やロボット技術、ＡＩ（人工知能）、量子技術、バイオテクノロジー、核融合、最新の製造技術といった先端技術分野での協力拡大を呼び掛けた。防衛や重要鉱物調達を巡る協力にも期待を示した。

赤沢亮正経済産業相は「ドイツはわが国にとって欧州最大のパートナーだ」とし、フィジカルＡＩ分野での協力に期待を表明した。一方、欧州連合（ＥＵ）が検討する欧州製電気自動車（ＥＶ）の優遇措置案に関し、日本製ＥＶが欧州市場から排除されるなどの悪影響を「強く懸念している」とも述べ、メルツ首相に直接、懸念を伝えた。赤沢氏は「これまで日独の産業界は大変良好な関係を構築してきた」と指摘。日本がドイツに自動車生産に必要な磁石を供給するなど、補完的なサプライチェーン（供給網）を構築しているとし「特定国による過剰生産に対し本来、同志国として一致して対処すべきパートナーが日独だ」と訴えた。

メルツ氏は講演で、「重要鉱物がなければ、電池も先端半導体も高性能の電動モーターも、日独両国が今後必要とする数多くの技術も実現できない」と強調。「原材料の採掘、加工が少数の国に集中すると、私たちは大きなリスクを抱える」とし、調達先の多角化やリサイクル強化などでより密接に協力すべきだと述べた。「日独両国の防衛産業の協力も深めていくべきだ」とし、「産業界のパートナーと共に新たな市場を開拓し、輸出機会をさらに広げたい」と語った。

経団連の筒井義信会長は「今日、過剰生産がわれわれの産業に少なからず影響を及ぼしており、公平な競争条件を確保するためのルールづくりに両国が主導的な役割を果たすことが求められている」と述べた。経済安全保障の確保にも触れ「重要物資の輸出制限といった経済的威圧が横行する中では、信頼できるパートナーである日独間の協力が肝要だ」と訴えた。筒井氏もＥＶの優遇措置案に触れ「日独を含めた日・ＥＵ間の協力を阻害することがないように要望する」とくぎを刺した。

サミットに先立ち、経済産業省はドイツの重電大手シーメンス・エナジーと浮体式洋上風力発電事業での協力に関する覚書の署名式を行った。産業基盤強化に向けたサプライチェーン（供給網）の発展などに向け協力する。シーメンスはアジア初となる戦略的なオペレーション・メンテナンス拠点を北海道に設置する。

item.title: Volkswagen plant's new recycling hub does little to ease closure fears
item.description: Volkswagen's all-electric car plant in Zwickau unveiled a new recycling facility for components on Wednesday, highlighting a potential future business line even as the site faces possible closure from the early 2030s under the group's restructuring.
item.dc:creator: Rachel More
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen's all-electric car plant in Zwickau unveiled a new recycling facility for components on Wednesday, highlighting a potential future business line even as the site faces possible closure from the early 2030s under the group's restructuring. Hit by the loss of its decades-long dominance in China and mounting competition from [USN:L8N45Z0KG TEXT:"Chinese competitors"] in Europe, Volkswagen is pressing ahead with [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"deep cost cuts"], including plans for 100,000 job reductions and the possible closure of four German plants. Zwickau is among the sites under threat, with no vehicle production currently planned beyond 2031, casting a shadow over Wednesday's launch of Volkswagen's first "Circular Economy Hub" at the factory in the eastern state of Saxony. Volkswagen said 100 workers had been retrained and would begin dismantling 4,100 vehicles a year at the site from 2027. "For us, dismantling and recycling doesn't mean a junkyard — it means creating value," said Thomas Schaefer, the CEO of Volkswagen's volume brands. A 'PILOT PROJECT' FOR NOW The project was awarded to Zwickau in a bid to secure up to 1,000 jobs over the longer term. Volkswagen plans to invest up to €90 million ($100 million), while the regional government has pledged €10.7 million. But the initiative offers only limited relief for a site where around 8,000 jobs are at risk under Volkswagen's overhaul announced in July. Production shifts are also expected to create excess capacity from mid-2026. With support for the far-right opposition running high, Saxony's government is [USN:L8N44P0QE TEXT:"under pressure"] to protect an auto industry linked to one in four jobs in the state. State Economy Minister Dirk Panter said the new facility showed Volkswagen was working with employees and the region to find durable solutions for the sector's future. "The circular economy for automotive components opens up new business opportunities, creates additional value and offers long-term employment prospects," Panter said in a statement. However, company sources and industry observers said the recycling venture alone would not secure the plant's future. Henning Wilts, a circular economy researcher at Germany's Wuppertal Institute, said the Zwickau hub remained an experiment whose commercial viability had yet to be proven. "This is a pilot project that you launch to see if it's scalable and if it's really an investment that will pay off quickly enough," Wilts said, adding: "It is certainly not the answer to all the questions in the European auto industry." ($1 = 0.8981 euros)

Oct 28 : Swiss banking software firm Temenos' CEO Takis Spiliopoulos said sovereign AI and cloud initiatives in Europe were not yet mature enough for major banks to adopt, as the region seeks greater technological autonomy from US providers. The European Union is seeking to strengthen its technological sovereignty through proposals, including the Cloud and AI Development Act, aimed at reducing dependence on US hyperscalers amid concerns over data access under US legislation and the dominance of Amazon, Microsoft and Google in cloud computing. • Spiliopoulos told Reuters that while many countries had pushed US cloud providers to establish local data centres, concerns remained over where data could ultimately be accessed. • "Sovereign data or sovereign AI ... it's not yet at a maturity level that they would really entertain this," Spiliopoulos said, referring to banks.

item.title: ボルソナロ氏、米国へ出国 国務省はビザ発給へ＝関係筋
item.description:
Ricardo Brito Gram Slattery Luciana Magalhaes
[サンパウロ ２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Ricardo Brito　Gram Slattery　Luciana Magalhaes

[サンパウロ ２８日 ロイター] - ブラジルのフラビオ・ボルソナロ上院議員が、２５日の大統領選で敗れた後、米国に向けて出国した。関係者３人が明らかにした。米国務省は同氏と家族に入国ビザを発給する予定だ。

ボルソナロ氏は敗北を認めておらず、旅券の提出を命じた最高裁の命令に従わずに出国した。この命令は資金洗浄疑惑の捜査に関連するもので、ボルソナロ氏は不正を否定している。

アルゼンチンの入国管理当局は２８日、ボルソナロ氏と家族が２７日夜、有効な渡航書類を使って陸路で同国のミシオネス州に一時入国し、現地時間午後１１時半（日本時間２８日午前１１時３０分）にエクアドルのグアヤキル行きのプライベート機に搭乗したと発表した。目的地について、チャーター会社バイレス・フライが運航する同機の飛行計画に基づく情報だと説明した。

ボルソナロ氏と妻、娘２人の現在の居場所は確認できていない。

ボルソナロ氏の選対責任者のマリーニョ上院議員は記者団に「この知らせには驚いている。ボルソナロ氏が６０００万票を得たことを踏まえ、野党指導者としての役割を担う必要があると話し合ったばかりだった」と述べた。

item.title: Al menos 30 personas mueren en España tras la colisión de dos trenes de alta velocidad
item.description: Al menos 30 personas murieron el miércoles tras el choque de dos trenes de alta velocidad en España, el segundo accidente mortal en menos de un año en la línea que une Madrid con la región meridional de Andalucía, según las autoridades regionales.
item.dc:creator: Emma Pinedo, Victoria Waldersee
item.content:encoded: Al menos 30 personas murieron el miércoles tras el choque de dos trenes de alta velocidad en España, el segundo accidente mortal en menos de un año en la línea que une Madrid con la región meridional de Andalucía, según las autoridades regionales. Las imágenes de la cadena regional Castilla-La Mancha Televisión mostraban un tren descarrilado con al menos un vagón aún sobre un tramo elevado de la vía, mientras que se podían ver restos de metal retorcido, paneles rotos y escombros esparcidos por el terraplén situado debajo de la línea. Miguel, un pasajero que viajaba con varios compañeros en el vagón trasero de uno de los trenes, describió a la emisora COPE el momento del accidente. "De repente, hemos escuchado un estruendo gigantesco, un golpetazo enorme, que además ha sido continuo durante 10 segundos, como si el tren fuera a descarrilar. Justo al lado, en la ventana derecha, se ve un tren destrozado, que imagino que sería el otro", dijo. Una persona informada sobre el siniestro explicó que un tren de alta velocidad operado por la empresa ferroviaria española Iryo se detuvo por orden del gestor de infraestructuras ADIF cerca de Toledo debido a un fallo en la señalización, antes de ser embestido por otro tren de alta velocidad. Un tren operado por Renfe chocó a gran velocidad contra el tren parado, lo que provocó el descarrilamiento de varios vagones de ambos trenes, según esta persona. Ni Iryo ni Renfe respondieron de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios de Reuters. UN PASAJERO DESCRIBE HABER VISTO VÍCTIMAS MORTALES El gobierno regional de Castilla-La Mancha afirmó que el número de fallecidos había aumentado de 10 a 30, tras haber advertido anteriormente de que podría aumentar. Jesús Pérez Martín, alcalde de la localidad cercana de Los Yébenes, calificó la situación de "horrorosa" y señaló que se trataba de una grave tragedia. "Me hablan de alguna mutilación y de cosas muy graves", declaró a RTVE. La ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García, instó a la población en una publicación en la red social X a donar sangre. Eduarda, una pasajera del tren Iryo, contó a la Cadena SER que sintió un fuerte impacto que la lanzó hacia delante, lo que en un primer momento le hizo pensar que el tren había realizado una parada de emergencia. Solo se dio cuenta de la gravedad del accidente tras ver a personas heridas y que le indicaran que evacuara el tren. Tras bajar por un terraplén hasta un lugar seguro, se encontró con lo que describió como una escena catastrófica: parte del tren colgaba de la pendiente y había un incendio en uno de los vagones. Los servicios de emergencia, entre los que se encontraban un helicóptero, policía y ambulancias, llegaron en unos 20 minutos, según explicó. "He visto a gente muerta", afirmó. SEGUNDO ACCIDENTE MORTAL EN ESTA LÍNEA EN MENOS DE UN AÑO La portavoz de la Junta de Castilla-La Mancha, Esther Padilla, indicó que 147 personas viajaban en el tren de Iryo y 397 en el de Renfe. La colisión se produce nueve meses después de un accidente entre trenes de alta velocidad pertenecientes a los mismos operadores en la misma línea, en el que fallecieron 46 personas. Aquel accidente, ocurrido en enero tras el descarrilamiento de un tren que chocó contra otro que circulaba en sentido contrario cerca de Adamuz, en la provincia de Córdoba, desencadenó un debate sobre el nivel de inversión en el mantenimiento ferroviario en los últimos años. ELECCIONES EL PRÓXIMO MES Los trenes de Renfe e Iryo chocaron poco después de las 9 de la mañana (0800 GMT), lo que provocó el descarrilamiento de dos vagones de Iryo, informó un portavoz del Gobierno en la región de Castilla-La Mancha, quien añadió que aún se estaban determinando las causas. Renfe informó que había puesto en marcha una línea especial para los familiares de las víctimas y expresó sus condolencias. Iryo indicó que había activado los protocolos de emergencia. Este nuevo accidente se produce mientras España se prepara para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. La agenda del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, publicada en la página web del Gobierno español, quedó anulada para el día. El opositor Partido Popular también canceló todos los actos de campaña de cara a las elecciones anticipadas del 29 de noviembre, según un portavoz. "Consternado ante el grave accidente de trenes en Toledo. (...) Mi cariño, solidaridad y apoyo a todas las víctimas y sus familias", dijo Sánchez en la red social X. Manuel Galán, alcalde de la localidad cercana de Urda, dijo a la Cadena SER que los servicios de emergencia le habían pedido que preparara instalaciones de emergencia, entre ellas un pabellón deportivo para acoger a los heridos. HISTORIAL DE SEGURIDAD FERROVIARIA Los accidentes, incluidos descarrilamientos y colisiones, aumentaron de 45 en 2016 a 57 en 2024 y a 69 el año pasado, según la autoridad española de seguridad ferroviaria. En el mismo periodo, problemas como el deterioro y las roturas de las vías pasaron de 494 a 667, una cifra inferior a los 716 registrados en 2024. Unos 25 millones de pasajeros utilizaron el tren de alta velocidad en España durante el primer semestre del año, lo que supone un descenso de aproximadamente un 14% en comparación con el mismo periodo del año anterior, según un análisis de Reuters basado en datos de la Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia. Los datos de la Comisión Europea muestran que la inversión española en mantenimiento de sus aproximadamente 4.000 kilómetros de líneas de alta velocidad ha quedado rezagada respecto a la de los grandes países europeos, a pesar de un esfuerzo sin igual por ampliar la red. España destinó una media de unos 1.500 millones de euros al año entre 2018 y 2022 a su red de alta velocidad, más que cualquier otro país. Sin embargo, la gran mayoría se destinó a nuevas infraestructuras, y solo alrededor del 16% se destinó al mantenimiento, la renovación y las mejoras. España figuraba entre los países de la UE con las tasas de mortalidad más bajas por accidentes ferroviarios antes de los sucesos de este año, con solo una o menos víctimas mortales por cada mil kilómetros de vía férrea, según los últimos datos disponibles de Eurostat correspondientes a 2024. Más del 90% de la red ferroviaria española está equipada con sistemas de control de seguridad del nivel más alto de la Unión Europea, según la agencia ferroviaria de la UE. Junto con Bélgica y Suiza, sus redes cuentan con la mayor extensión de vías equipadas con un estándar de señalización a escala europea.

item.title: At least 64 people killed in Spain as two high-speed trains collide
item.description: Rescue workers in Spain on Wednesday were scouring the wreckage for more bodies at the crash scene where at least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided, in the second deadly railway accident in the country this year.
item.dc:creator: David Latona, Guillermo Martinez, Michael Gore
item.content:encoded: Rescue workers in Spain on Wednesday were scouring the wreckage for more bodies at the crash scene where at least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided , in the second deadly railway accident in the country this year. Evacuated passengers streamed along a road near the scene, some splattered with blood or with their wounds bandaged, others wheeling suitcases and being given water by volunteers who said it had been donated from neighbouring towns. Hundreds of ambulances, funeral home vans and helicopters were parked next to a train with several carriages sitting on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line where at least three carriages had plunged. Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident. "We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train," he said. A person briefed on the disaster said a train operated by private consortium Iryo stopped near Toledo on orders from infrastructure manager ADIF due to a signal fault. A train operated by Renfe then struck the stationary train at high speed, causing several carriages of both trains to derail, the person said. Renfe said in a statement that after a being authorised to continue its journey, its train had crashed into the Iryo train that had remained stationary "for reasons we don't know". "The Renfe train continued on its way as instructed, and a collision occurred. The exact sequence of events, the traffic conditions and the circumstances of the impact will have to be established by the investigation," Renfe said. There was no immediate response to a Reuters request for comment from Iryo or Adif.

item.title: Gulf equities mixed as Ras Tanura strike unnerves investors
item.description: Gulf stocks ended mixed on Wednesday as an attack on a refinery in top crude exporter Saudi Arabia rattled investors and renewed concerns that conflict in the Middle East could escalate.
item.dc:creator: Ateeq Shariff
item.content:encoded: Gulf stocks ended mixed on Wednesday as an attack on a refinery in top crude exporter [USN:L6N46D0XG TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] rattled investors and renewed concerns that conflict in the Middle East could escalate. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had struck the 550,000-barrel-per-day facility, the kingdom's biggest refinery, with a ballistic missile. Saudi authorities have not immediately confirmed the strike. Saudi Arabia's benchmark stock index (.TASI) reversed early losses to finish 0.4% higher, helped by a 0.7% increase in the country's biggest lender Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) . National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia (4030.SE) advanced 1.6% after reporting a steep rise in quarterly profit. However, Mobile Telecommunications Company Saudi Arabia (7030.SE) retreated 1.5% after a drop in third-quarter profit. Oil major Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) was down 0.3%. Brent crude futures rose $1.31, or 1.2%, to $115.19 a barrel as of 1115 GMT, underpinned by renewed concerns about supply in the Middle East. Dubai's main share index (.DFMGI) fell 0.3%, with top lender Emirates NBD (ENBD.DU) losing 1.1%. GCC markets were under pressure as geopolitical risks weighed on sentiment. Trump's remarks on possible post-midterm military action and ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruptions hampered risk appetite, with focus now on regional mediation efforts for signs of stability, said Ahmed Kamal, CEO at ICM MENA. On Monday, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan [USN:S8N4320AV TEXT:"met Iranian officials in Tehran"] to try to reduce regional tensions. In Abu Dhabi, the benchmark stock index (.FTFADGI) declined 1.6%, dragged down by a 5% plunge in Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank (ADIB.AD) . In the previous session, the sharia-compliant lender reported a marginal rise in third-quarter profit. The Qatari benchmark (.QSI) rose 0.7%, with Qatar Islamic Bank (QISB.QA) gaining 2.5%. Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) slid 1.6%, as most of its constituents were in positive territory including Commercial International Bank (COMI.CA) , which was down 2.4%. A Reuters poll [USN:L6N46D0YD TEXT:"showed"] Egypt's central bank is likely to keep interest rates unchanged on Thursday for a sixth consecutive meeting, as a record-low pound, high energy costs and rising regional tensions outweigh easing inflation. item.title: カタール、イランに戦争終結へ新合意案提示 週末までに回答へ
item.description: [２８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２８日 ロイター] - 仲介役のカタールは２５日、米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争の終結に向けた新たな合意案をイラン側に提示した。イランは案を検討しており、週末までに回答する見通し。交渉について説明を受けた当局者が２８日、明らかにした。

同当局者によると、新たな合意案はイランと米国双方の懸念に対処する７日間の工程を定め、双方が信頼醸成に向けて毎日取るべき措置を示している。

工程は早ければ来週初めに開始される可能性があり、複数の国が合意の履行を保証する役割を担うという。

カタールはパキスタンと共に、米国とイスラエルが２月に始めた対イラン戦争の終結に向けた仲介を主導してきた。紛争は世界の海運と石油供給に混乱をもたらし、中東の他の地域にも波及している。

同当局者によると、２５日にテヘランで行われた会合を前に、総選挙で続投を目指すイスラエルのネタニヤフ首相がイランへの攻撃を今週再開する可能性があるとの懸念が出ていた。

トランプ米大統領は２３日、イランを再攻撃すると改めて威嚇した。一方、イランの治安当局者らはロイターに対し、米国とイスラエルが攻撃を再開した場合に備え、湾岸の海底ケーブルを攻撃する詳細な計画を策定したと明らかにした。

item.title: Hegseth proposes 'ambitious' US-ASEAN defence framework at Philippine summit
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth urged the formation of a new US-ASEAN defence cooperation framework and for strengthened maritime awareness and advanced naval coordination in the region.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Hegseth proposes 'ambitious' US-ASEAN defence framework at Philippine summit

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth urged the formation of a new US-ASEAN defence cooperation framework and for strengthened maritime awareness and advanced naval coordination in the region.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth leaves after attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers' Meeting in Cebu on Oct 28, 2026. (Photo: Aaron Favila/POOL/AFP)

FAST

CEBU: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth proposed the creation of an "ambitious" new US-ASEAN defence framework on Wednesday (Oct 28), telling the bloc's leaders it could help them navigate "critically important" years ahead. The United States has been seeking to boost its regional defence partnerships in recent years, citing the need to uphold what it terms a "free and open Indo-Pacific" as China has increasingly flexed its muscles in the region. Hegseth, speaking before a meeting with defence chiefs from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Cebu, praised what he called the region's "pragmatism" and "proud nationalism". "We're not going to agree on everything, nor do we need to," he said, calling for cooperation where shared interests overlap.
