item.title: ＡＩ投資でプライベートクレジット市場拡大、借り換えリスク浮上＝ムーディーズ
item.description: ［２７日 ロイター］ - 米格付け会社ムーディーズ・レーティングスは２７日、人工知能（ＡＩ）インフラ整備を支えるための借...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＡＩ投資でプライベートクレジット市場拡大、借り換えリスク浮上＝ムーディーズ 14:20 配信

写真のイラストは10月19日撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） ［２７日　ロイター］ - 米格付け会社ムーディーズ・レーティングスは２７日、人工知能（ＡＩ）インフラ整備を支えるための借り入れ増大により、プライベートクレジット市場が従来の企業向け融資の枠を超えて広がっている一方、今後数年で返済期限を迎える融資が集中し、財務基盤の弱い借り手が借り換えに苦戦する可能性があるとの見方を示した。

・ムーディーズによると、ＡＩ関連の資金需要はデータセンター建設にとどまらず、用地取得や電力設備、半導体、ＧＰＵ（画像処理半導体）、ＴＰＵ（テンソル処理ユニット）に拡大している。

・同社は、米国の主要ハイパースケーラー５社とＡＩクラウドサービス企業コアウィーブの設備投資額が２０２７年に累計で約１兆ドルに達すると予測。資金は営業キャッシュフローのほか、負債調達や合弁事業、特別目的会社（ＳＰＶ）などの仕組みを通じて賄われるとしている。

・だが２７年から２９年にかけて多額の融資が返済期限を迎える見通しで、金利上昇局面において信用力の低い借り手の借り換え能力が試されると指摘した。

・ムーディーズが追跡する６０７社の借り手のうち約１７％は、現金での利払いを先送りできるＰＩＫ（ペイメント・イン・カインド）金利を利用している。利払い負担を繰り延べできる半面、債務残高の増加につながる仕組みだ。

・ロイターが今年実施した分析では、米国のビジネス・デベロップメント・カンパニー（ＢＤＣ）が保有するローンの満期到来は２８年と２９年にピークを迎える。

・最近のコアウィーブの債務を巡る市場の動揺は、高いレバレッジを抱えるＡＩ関連企業に対する投資家の警戒感の高まりを浮き彫りにした。

・ムーディーズは、テクノロジー企業や半導体メーカー、ＡＩ開発企業が相互に出資や融資、製品購入を行うケースが増えていることから「循環型」の資金調達リスクにも警鐘を鳴らした。景気後退時にはこうした相関性の高いエクスポージャーが同時に悪化する恐れがあるという。

item.title: ＮＹＳＥ、株バイナリーオプション開始へ 業績指標連動型も申請
item.description:
Laura Matthews
［ニューヨーク ２７日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）は、株式や上場...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹＳＥ、株バイナリーオプション開始へ　業績指標連動型も申請 14:05 配信

写真はＮＹＳＥの建物。2021年1月、米ニューヨーク市で撮影。 REUTERS/Mike Segar（ロイター） Laura Matthews

［ニューヨーク　２７日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）は、株式や上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）の満期日終値があらかじめ設定した価格を上回るか下回るかに対して、投資家が「オール・オア・ナッシング」の賭けを行える新たなオプション契約（バイナリー・リターン・オプション）の取引開始を準備している。

オプションやイベント連動型契約の取引が急増する中で、もっとピンポイントの予想をしたり、リスク管理をより精緻に行ったりしたい個人・機関投資家の需要を取り込むため、取引所各社が新商品開発を進めている事情がうかがえる。

ＮＹＳＥはまた、企業業績指標に連動する第２の新商品、バイナリー型の主要業績評価指標（ＫＰＩ）オプションについても承認を申請しており、イベントドリブン取引への旺盛な需要を取り込む動きを強めている。この商品は、企業が公表する業績指標が設定水準を上回るか下回るかに応じて投資家に利益を支払う仕組み。従来の株価連動型オプションとは異なり、ＫＰＩオプションでは売上高や１株利益、クラウド事業売上高、自動車生産台数などの指標そのものを対象に取引できる。

バイナリー・リターン・オプションは数日以内に取引が開始される見通し。対象となる原資産は１２銘柄で、アップル、エヌビディア、テスラ、ＳＰＤＲ・Ｓ＆Ｐ５００・ＥＴＦトラストなどが含まれる。対象銘柄は順次追加される予定だ。

ＮＹＳＥのケビン・タイレル最高プロダクト責任者は「ここ数年、米国のオプション市場は驚異的な成長を遂げている。取引量の増加を詳しく見ると、新しい取引手法や新商品に対する関心が高まっていることが分かる」と述べた。

これらの契約は現金決済型で、満期時にのみ権利行使できる欧州型を採用。対象指標が満期時に権利行使価格で定めた水準を満たした場合は１ドルを支払い、満たさなかった場合は、支払いは行われない。

item.title: Boosting Western supply of refined critical metals means de-risking investment. But how?
item.description: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure. The question is how to translate initial successes into a long-term, economically viable supply chain that bypasses the world's dominant producer. It was this question that dominated the International Mining and Resources Conference (IMARC) this week in Sydney, which brought together miners, governments and financiers to discuss how to turn the resource endowments of countries like [USN:L5N46D0DY TEXT:"Australia"] into refined metals. Unlike China, which can sustain forms of subsidies for state-controlled enterprises for years until economies of scale are achieved, Western nations are shaped more by finance and profitability. But it is also apparent that in a world where China dominates the production of refined metals and prices are often viewed as opaque, the previous model of mine development and downstream processing will not work. The United States is further ahead than the European Union in recognising that if critical minerals and metals are to be obtained in sufficient quantities and via relatively secure supply chains, then government intervention and support are going to be key. The traditional model of junior miners exploring and proving up a resource, then trying to raise capital to build a mine and eventually moving into production simply will not deliver the needed ore when compared with China's subsidy-driven rivals. And even if ore can be successfully mined, refining is often more challenging, especially in countries like Australia, with its high labour and energy costs and stringent environmental approvals. The main question at IMARC was how to significantly move the needle toward more secure supply for Western economies in a world where China controls 99% of the world's refined gallium, 74% of antimony, 81% of molybdenum, 91% of rare earths, 70% of lithium and 44% of copper, showed data from Visual Capitalist. And that is to name just a few of the vital metals. The answers were varied and reflected that no one tactic or policy is likely to deliver the necessary results. But there was some consensus on what measures are likely to bring the greatest chance of more rapid development of mineral resources. DE-RISKING The biggest factor is how to de-risk projects. Under the traditional model financing was only available if the developer could show that the cost of producing the minerals and metals would be less than the expected future price, or that offtake agreements were in place that guaranteed revenue. It was on this basis that Australia was able to approve massive resource expansion, such as Japanese investment into coal and iron ore mines, and both Japanese and Chinese support for liquefied natural gas projects. Australia also jumped in the past decade to become the world's largest lithium producer, but this was achieved largely with Chinese money and the vast majority of the country's mined lithium ore is processed in China for use by Chinese vehicle and battery manufacturers. For more minor metals with opaque pricing the situation is more complex. There are three main tactics to try and speed up development. The first is to set a floor price for the commodity, as the United States has done for the rare earth compound neodymium-praseodymium, which is used to make magnets. The minimum price of $110 per kilogram gives producers certainty and may end up costing US taxpayers nothing as the price of the compound has risen to trade above the floor. The second is to guarantee offtake, giving producers confidence that buyers will be available for the product at prices that will ensure viability, even if those prices are higher than what is charged by Chinese-controlled suppliers. The third is to directly invest in mines and downstream processing and be prepared to subsidise losses until economic viability can be achieved. The trick is in working out which tactic will deliver the best outcome, and this is likely to vary from project to project. For metals where the government is the main buyer, such as those used by defence industries, owning stakes may be the answer. For industries vital to technology and the energy transition, setting minimum prices and ensuring offtake agreements are likely the better solution. What is lacking so far is a comprehensive strategy across the developed Western economies, and at IMARC it was also clear that the United States and the European Union are showing signs of competing with each other, rather than working together. The risk is that the Western response to China's dominance of refined critical metals remains fragmented and uncoordinated. Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI) , your essential new source for global financial commentary. ROI delivers thought-provoking, data-driven analysis of everything from swap rates to soybeans. Markets are moving faster than ever. ROI can help you keep up. Follow ROI on LinkedIn and X . The views expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.

item.title: 松井証、ゆうちょ銀と出資協議を含め提携について検討
item.description: ［東京 ２８日 ロイター］ - 松井証券は２８日、ゆうちょ銀行が松井証の創業家系企業から株を買い取り、２０％ほど出資す...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
松井証、ゆうちょ銀と出資協議を含め提携について検討 13:18 配信

［東京　２８日　ロイター］ - 松井証券は２８日、ゆうちょ銀行が松井証の創業家系企業から株を買い取り、２０％ほど出資する方針を固めたとの日本経済新聞の報道を受け「ゆうちょ銀と出資に関する協議等を含め、提携について検討していることは事実」とのコメントを発表した。

松井証券の和里田聡社長は同日の決算会見で、他社との提携について「仮にどこかと組むことがあれば、顧客基盤の拡充につながることと、商品・サービスの拡充につながることが条件になる」と述べた。

一方で、「今すぐそうしなければいけない状況ではない」とし、足元で提携を急ぐ状況にはないとの認識を示した。「新規口座開設数や信用取引残高シェアを見る限り、ＳＢＩ証券や楽天証券の手数料無料化の影響は限定的だ」と指摘。同社は独立系として能動的に顧客を取りにいく戦略を採っており、ポジショニングがうまく機能しているとも述べた。

現時点で決定した事実はなく開示すべき事実が発生した場合は速やかに公表するとしている。

ゆうちょ銀は、中期経営計画で示したコンサルティング事業戦略の中で、松井証を含む証券会社との提携などさまざまな検討をしているとした上で、何ら決定した事実はないとコメントした。

item.title: 午前の日経平均は続伸、ＡＩ株牽引で6万4000円回復 決算見極めムードも
item.description:
Noriyuki Hirata
[東京 ２８日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は続伸し、前営業日比１．２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
午前の日経平均は続伸、ＡＩ株牽引で6万4000円回復　決算見極めムードも 11:55 配信

写真は2024年12月、都内の東京証券取引所で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon（ロイター） Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 ２８日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は続伸し、前営業日比１．２６％（７９８円７３銭）高の６万４０６７円１０銭となった。米国市場での人工知能（ＡＩ）・半導体関連株高の流れが波及し、国内関連株の上昇が指数を押し上げた。韓国株の堅調な推移も投資家心理を支援した。一方、国内企業決算やＡＩデータセンターに大規模投資する米ハイパースケーラーの決算などを控えて手掛けにくさも意識された。ＴＯＰＩＸは小幅マイナスだった。

・日経平均はＡＩ株を中心に買いが先行し４営業日ぶりに６万４０００円を回復。一時１．５７％（９９２円４９銭）高の６万４２６０円８６銭に上昇。

・アドバンテストのほか、東京エレクトロン、ソフトバンクグループ、キオクシアホールディングスといった国内の主要ＡＩ関連株が上昇。これら４銘柄で日経平均を８００円程度押し上げ。

・韓国半導体大手ＳＫハイニックスが朝方に７─９月決算を発表。営業利益が前年同期の７倍超に増え、過去最高を更新し市場予想を上振れ。

・韓国ＫＯＳＰＩは５％超高、日経平均はつれ高の場面も

・東証プライム市場の６割が値下がりし、ＡＩ株に偏った株高に

・前日に見通しの下方修正を発表したキヤノンや、高進捗でも見通しを据え置いたカプコンなどが売られた一方、信越化学工業やシマノは堅調

・日経平均は買い一巡後に高値もみ合い、日米で注目企業の決算発表や中銀会合を控え手掛けにくさも

・明日朝には米アルファベットや米マイクロソフトが決算を発表の予定

・ＴＯＰＩＸは０．０２％安の３９９６．５３ポイントで午前の取引を終了。東証プライム市場の売買代金は３兆８２８７億０４００万円。

・東証３３業種で上昇したのは、ガラス・土石、非鉄金属、電気機器など８業種、下落は保険、食料品、その他製品など２５業種。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが４９１銘柄（３１％）、値下がりは１０２８銘柄（６６％）、変わらずは３４銘柄（２％）。

＜フィリップ・キャピタル証券　株式部トレーディング・ヘッド　増沢丈彦氏＞

「韓国ＫＯＳＰＩの上昇と歩調を合わせて先物に買いが入り、短期筋主導の値動きの様相」

「長期投資家は国内ＡＩ関連企業や米ハイパースケーラーの決算を見極める姿勢か」

「市場では１１月以降の株高アノマリーを意識し、買い場を探る動きも」

item.title: Netanyahu survives another day with unexpectedly clear backing of Israeli Jews
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu won the support of an unexpectedly clear majority of Israeli Jews in an election billed as a major turning point in his nation's history, apparently ensuring he will survive as prime minister at least in a caretaker role.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Rami Ayyub, Lina Obeid
item.content:encoded: Benjamin Netanyahu won the support of an unexpectedly clear majority of Israeli Jews in an election billed as a major turning point in his nation's history, apparently ensuring he will survive as prime minister at least in a caretaker role. With [USN:L2N46E0B8 TEXT:"around 77.6% of votes tallied"] on Wednesday morning, Israeli media forecast Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties winning 54 seats in parliament, far surpassing 49 for the opposition bloc of [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"rival Gadi Eisenkot"]. Parties representing Israelis of Arab descent would win 17, a record, following high turnout from passionately motivated voters. The results could still change as counting continued, but a victory for Eisenkot appeared increasingly out of reach, as his bloc of anti-Netanyahu parties from centre-left to hard-right underperformed pre-election polls that forecast a tight race. While Netanyahu lost his bloc's majority in the 120-seat Knesset, as expected, his opponents were left with no hope of unseating him without an unlikely deal to accept broad backing from Arab parties, which many Jewish leaders reject. Even then, he would remain as caretaker during any [USN:L8N46117V TEXT:"coalition negotiations"], or until a new election next year. SECURITY FIGHT SHARPENS Netanyahu, addressing his Likud party's faithful after 3 a.m. (0100 GMT) at the party's election headquarters in Jerusalem, called for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government". He also highlighted Israel's military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint military action against Iran alongside his ally, US President Donald Trump. "Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he said. Trump, who had called on Israeli voters to keep Netanyahu in power so the two leaders could "finish the job" in Iran, said Netanyahu had done "very well" thanks to his own endorsement that "helped him a lot". "It might be winning or tie. The tie is sort of considered a win in that case because it's a big chess match," Trump said early on Wednesday at a campaign stop in Texas. The likelihood of a caretaker government with no parliamentary majority [USN:L5N46E0V3 TEXT:"weighed on Israel's financial markets"]. The shekel currency weakened around 1.6% to 3.10 to the US dollar. Tel Aviv's key benchmark stock indexes fell more than 3% (.TA35) , (.TA125) . EISENKOT CALLS ON SECURITY CHIEFS TO RESIST PRESSURE Eisenkot acknowledged that Netanyahu was still in office as a caretaker, but said the prime minister had lost public support and urged him to retire from politics. He also issued a warning that Netanyahu might use security for political ends. "I call on the heads of the security establishment and the civil service: Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust," he said. "Remember that you serve only the state and the interests of Israel's citizens. Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you," he said. "Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel’s security for your political needs." The election was the first held in Israel since Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and carried off 251 hostages in attacks that shattered the country's sense of security and plunged it into war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The war in Gaza , which flattened the territory and killed 74,000 Palestinians, has left Israel increasingly isolated on the world stage, with a decisive shift in global public opinion against it, including in its closest ally the United States. Netanyahu himself is wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague on war crimes charges he calls absurd, and faces corruption charges in Israel that he dismisses as an establishment plot. DECISIVE SHIFT IN ISRAELI POLITICS The continued support for Netanyahu from most Israeli Jews was a clear sign of the decisive shift in Israeli politics that he has presided over as the dominant political figure of the era. His brand of unapologetic Jewish nationalism, support for settlement on occupied Palestinian land and contempt for all foreign criticism is now firmly entrenched as the Israeli mainstream. The centre-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history and had led negotiations to disentangle Israel from the Palestinian territories has been reduced to a small fringe. Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu's rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace talks since the 1990s, when he first came to power as Israel's youngest-ever leader. After a spell in the wilderness, he returned to power in 2009 and has remained ever since, apart from a period of 18 months when a rickety coalition of opponents managed to lever him out after four inconclusive elections in two years. TURNING POINT Netanyahu's supporters and opponents alike saw Tuesday's election as a decisive turning point for the nation, driving turnout to 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades. Turnout was particularly high among [USN:L5N46D0XS TEXT:"Israelis of Palestinian descent"], who make up more than a fifth of the population but whose representatives have historically been excluded from the cabinet. Many were motivated by what they see as open racism from Netanyahu's cabinet, which includes a party leader convicted of inciting racial hatred against Arabs. The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Joint List candidate Faten Gattas. The coalition that last toppled Netanyahu relied on one small Arab party, but Eisenkot's underperformance means the opposition would now need backing from the Joint List itself, anathema to Jewish leaders since the nation's founding.

item.title: 米ベーカー・ヒューズ、第3四半期は減益 中東紛争が打撃
item.description:
Vallari Srivastava
［２７日 ロイター］ - 米エネルギーサービス会社ベーカー・ヒューズが２７日発表...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ベーカー・ヒューズ、第3四半期は減益　中東紛争が打撃 11:14 配信

写真はベーカー・ヒューズのロゴ。2023年7月、カナダのバンクーバーで撮影。 REUTERS/Chris Helgren（ロイター） Vallari Srivastava

［２７日　ロイター］ - 米エネルギーサービス会社ベーカー・ヒューズが２７日発表した第３・四半期決算は、純利益が４億１１００万ドル（１株当たり０．４１ドル）となり、前年同期の６億０９００万ドル（同０．６１ドル）から減少した。中東紛争の長期化で主要産油地域におけるサービス・機器需要が低迷した。

現在８カ月目に突入している中東紛争の度重なる激化で、プロジェクト決定の遅れ、操業の混乱、顧客による支出ペースを巡る懸念が重なり、油田サービス業界の利益率は圧迫されている。

ベーカー・ヒューズの売上高の４０％近くは中東が占める。中東地域への依存度は競合するＳＬＢ（旧シュルンベルジェ）やハリバートンと比べて高い。

第３・四半期の油田サービス・機器部門売上高は、北米が９億５５００万ドルで前年同期の９億８０００万ドルから減少。中東・アジア地域の売上高は、１４億５０００万ドルから１２億６０００万ドルに減った。

ベーカー・ヒューズは、物流コストの上昇やサプライチェーン（供給網）の課題が事業に影響を与えると見込んでいる。中東での事業活動は第４・四半期に前期比で減少すると予想している。

また、７月に１３６億ドルで買収した産業機器メーカー、チャートの年間売上高見通しを、従来の２０億５０００万ドルから１９億９０００万ドルに引き下げた。ＬＮＧ（液化天然ガス）関連機器の出荷時期や水素需要の低迷が背景にある。

全体的な売上高見通しは据え置いた。ロレンツォ・シモネリ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、中東地域で確かな改善がみられたとし、顧客が回収率の最大化と資産寿命の延長をますます優先するにつれ、さらなる機会が期待されると述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：ホルムズ封鎖で石油貿易に変化、米州が最大の受益者に コラム：ドローン攻撃とエネルギーインフラ、露呈した世界経済の弱点 アングル：戦場を超えるドローン脅威、対抗技術市場が急拡大 コラム：米イラン合意、エネルギー供給に安心感と消えない構造的リスク コラム：ホルムズ海峡でタンカーの「闇航行」増加、原油市場が不透明化 10/28(水) 11:14 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: US closes $5.1 billion loan to Alliant Energy for new gas power generation, energy storage
item.description: The US Department of Energy said on Wednesday it has closed a $5.1 billion loan package to Alliant Energy to expand power generation and bolster the grid at plants in Iowa and Wisconsin.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Energy said on Wednesday it has closed a $5.1 billion loan package to Alliant Energy (LNT.O) to expand power generation and bolster the grid at plants in Iowa and Wisconsin. The 30-year loans will support new natural gas-fired power plants, systems to store energy using batteries, and upgrades to existing generation facilities, it said. They will also create hundreds of construction-related jobs and deliver more than 2.6 gigawatts of new or upgraded power generation capacity, it said. That's enough power for nearly 1.8 million homes. Lisa Barton, president and CEO of Alliant, said in a statement that the financing helps lower the cost of building power generation capacity and infrastructure while strengthening the grid and supporting long-term savings. Alliant, based in Wisconsin, said it projects that over the lifetime of the loans, customers would save up to $1.2 billion in power bills. The loan had originally been proposed by the administration of former President Joe Biden, in his last days in office in January 2025, when it was only a conditional loan of $3 billion. The office of Energy Dominance Financing, called the Loan Programs Office under Biden, has hundreds of billions of dollars in financing available, the bulk of which Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said will support nuclear power. More than the name of the office has changed. Its mission during the Biden administration was to provide support to emerging clean energy projects and alternative vehicles that struggled to get bank loans. Now it includes support to projects such as natural gas that have typically been able to get bank loans. Energy storage, which typically includes batteries, was supported in both the initial and the closed loan. "By bringing new, dependable power online, we are strengthening our nation’s energy security and lowering electricity costs for families and businesses across Iowa and Wisconsin," the loan office director, Gregory Beard, said in a release. Any lowering of electricity costs could take many years as the loans take place over decades.

item.title: UK economy set to grow 1.2% this year, slow in 2027, Healey says in budget speech
item.description: Britain's economy is due to grow this year by only slightly more than expected previously and a forecast for 2027 was slashed, finance minister John Healey said in a budget speech that is expected to include measures to help ease the cost of living.
item.dc:creator: David Milliken, Suban Abdulla
item.content:encoded: Britain's economy is due to grow this year by only slightly more than expected previously and a forecast for 2027 was slashed, finance minister John Healey said in a budget speech that is expected to include measures to help ease the cost of living. [USN:L5N46D165 TEXT:"Projections"] from the independent Office for Budget Responsibility showed gross domestic product was on course to expand by 1.2% in 2026, Healey said in his first budget address to parliament on Wednesday. That was up from a previous forecast of 1.1% announced by the OBR in March. Britain's economy has withstood the energy price shock from the Iran war so far. But rising inflation and the prospect of higher interest rates is likely to slow the economy next year. Healey said the economy faced a hit from the conflict in the Gulf as well from global trade tensions and the war in Ukraine. "Those are the storms we face. We can't wish them away. We must choose the course we steer through them," he said. Healey said the OBR now expected GDP to grow by 1.0% in 2027 compared with its March forecast of 1.6%. Economic output was seen expanding by 1.6%, 1.8% and 1.7% in 2028, 2029 and 2030 respectively. Those projections compared with the budget watchdog's previous growth forecasts of 1.6% in 2028 and 1.5% in 2029 and in 2030. Healey, a [USN:L8N44P1EA TEXT:"former trade union official"], was set to announce a cautious set of tax and spending plans in an attempt to avoid piling more bond market pressure on the new government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. [USN:L8N4610PT TEXT:"Banks"], gambling firms and online marketplaces such as Amazon (AMZN.O) and Temu (PDD.O) were expected to be hit with higher taxes to help pay for cost-of-living support. Measures announced prior to his speech in parliament included the removal of [USN:L5N46E0IA TEXT:"standing charges"] on gas bills which would bring down costs for most households. The Treasury has also announced tariff cuts on some imported goods including gherkins and marmalade. More than [USN:L6N46A01K TEXT:"£20 billion"] in extra support will go to state finance institutions to spur investment in artificial intelligence, defence and green energy by the early 2030s. Healey has said he will [USN:L8N4682B4 TEXT:"reduce paperwork"] for businesses to save them £800 million a year. The speech is expected to include details of how the government plans to give regional mayors more control over tax revenues, part of Burnham's [USN:L8N4691W8 TEXT:"devolution push"]. On entering Downing Street in July, Burnham promised "the biggest changes in the last 40 years", including a bigger role for the state in the economy. But Healey's spending options are limited by the surge in borrowing costs in Britain and around the world since the start of the Iran war which has eaten into his margin for meeting his main target for repairing the public finances. After big tax and spending increases in the two budgets of the previous finance minister Rachel Reeves, Wednesday has been framed as a "steady as she goes" moment for Britain's economy. Healey's biggest hope is for an end to the Iran war, which would lower the government's bill for servicing £3 trillion of public debt. That was already on course to gobble up more than 10% of public spending before the war began. Healey said debt interest in the current financial year would cost more than £14 billion.

item.title: Rare Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for USD 47.3m at New York auction
item.description: A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton, belonging to a smaller relative of the T. rex, has sold for USD 47.3 million at an auction at Sotheby’s in New York following a fierce 12-minute bidding war among six ...
item.content:encoded:
Rare Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for USD 47.3m at New York auction A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton, belonging to a smaller relative of the T. rex, has sold for USD 47.3 million at an auction at Sotheby’s in New York following a fierce 12-minute bidding war among six contenders. ANI | Updated: 28-10-2026 11:54 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 11:54 IST

Nanotyrannus skeleton (Image source: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton, belonging to a smaller relative of the T. rex, has sold for USD 47.3 million at an auction at Sotheby’s in New York following a fierce 12-minute bidding war among six contenders. The specimen, named Jodi, is one of only three relatively complete Nanotyrannus skeletons known to science. Blowing well past an estimate of USD 6 to USD 9 million, the sale narrowly missed the auction record for a fossil, set in July with the sale of Gus — an exceptional T. rex skeleton that went under the hammer for USD 50.1 million, as per CNN. Standing 9.6 feet tall and measuring 19.6 feet long, Jodi is just over half the length of Gus. The scarcity of comparable specimens is likely to have contributed to the eye-watering sale price. However, the very existence of Nanotyrannus as a distinct species remains hotly debated among paleontologists. Only recently have researchers increasingly come to favor the view that Nanotyrannus was a separate species rather than a juvenile T. rex. The specimen, according to Sotheby’s, is exceptionally preserved, made up of 191 bone elements, and includes a “virtually complete” skull. The skeleton was discovered in 2019 by Montana rancher Jodi Pierson, who inspired its name, and excavated by Clayton Phipps, a commercial paleontologist nicknamed the “Dinosaur Cowboy.” Like several other important fossils previously sold at auction, Jodi comes from Hell Creek Formation, a geological boneyard stretching across Montana, Wyoming and the Dakotas. One of the first skeletons of T. rex was found there in 1902, and the name T. rex was given to the species based on fossils unearthed in the area, according to CNN. Based on the overall size and bone development, Jodi is an adult specimen, according to Sotheby’s. The missing bones have been replaced with custom 3D printed and sculpted elements, and the fossil was offered with “full rights,” meaning it doesn’t contain any copyrighted elements from other dinosaurs. Its new owner — whose identity is unknown — can therefore create replicas of the skeleton and sell them to museums or collectors. (ANI)

item.title: Three killed, thousands evacuated as Cyclone Arnab hits eastern India
item.description: At least three people were killed, dozens of houses damaged and crops destroyed as a powerful cyclone struck India's eastern coast from the Bay of Bengal on Wednesday, bringing heavy rain and strong winds, authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Jatindra Dash, Rishika Sadam
item.content:encoded: At least three people were killed, dozens of houses damaged and crops destroyed as a powerful cyclone struck India's eastern coast from the Bay of Bengal on Wednesday, bringing heavy rain and strong winds, authorities said. Cyclone Arnab, classified by the India Meteorological Department as a very severe cyclonic storm – the third-highest category on its scale – made landfall in Andhra Pradesh state early on Wednesday, with its centre then moving fully inland, the agency said. "Andhra Pradesh has been most affected ... three people have lost their lives," Narendra Singh Bundela, a top official at the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), told reporters. Heavy rain and high winds destroyed at least 180 houses, brought down 220 trees and disrupted power supply in several areas, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said in a letter to federal Home Minister Amit Shah, updating him on the situation. Two of the deaths were caused by a tree falling and electrocution, officials in Naidu's office told Reuters. Neighbouring Odisha state was not as badly affected, Bundela said, adding that wind-speeds were expected to reduce as the cyclone moved inland. More than 180,000 people had been [USN:L6N46D0NN TEXT:"evacuated"] in the states of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha ahead of the cyclone's arrival. Some schools were closed and some train and flight services cancelled along the eastern coast. Several NDRF and state teams were working in the affected areas, Bundela said, adding that some neighbouring states were also likely to be affected by heavy rain. Television images showed trees fallen on highways as workers in rain gear worked to clear the road of branches and leaves. "No one knew whose house the water would rush into next, or whose home would be submerged," said Nagi, a resident of Andhra's Kakinada district. "Trees have fallen, houses have been damaged, and all our belongings, including our books, have been destroyed," said Nagi, who did not give a last name. Fishermen along the coast had been advised against going out to sea, and the weather department said it anticipated losses to crops, as well as damage to thatched houses and communication lines. Winds of 125 kph to 135 kph (77.7 mph to 83.9 mph) and gusts of up to 150 kph are forecast, with a storm surge of 1 metre to 1.5 metres (3.28 feet to 4.92 feet) above normal tide likely to inundate low-lying areas of Andhra Pradesh, it said. Operations at three Andhra Pradesh airports were suspended, India's civil aviation ministry said. NEPAL SUSPENDS TREKKING PERMITS In neighbouring Nepal, authorities suspended the issuing of trekking permits to high mountain areas for three days because of the risk of rain and blizzards due to the cyclone, Immigration Department information officer Gita Ghimire told Reuters. This is peak trekking season in Nepal with around 750 hikers getting permits per day. On Tuesday, Nepal warned tourists against venturing into high-altitude areas due to fears that Arnab could trigger torrential downpours, snowstorms and avalanches in the Himalayan region from Thursday night through Saturday. Arnab formed over the Bay of Bengal, a major region for tropical cyclones that has spawned deadly storms on India's east coast. A super cyclone that killed nearly 10,000 people when it hit Odisha in October 1999 remains one of the country's deadliest natural disasters. India, however, has over the years developed early-warning systems and preventive measures to minimise loss of life.

item.title: Food and household brands warn of more price hikes as Iran war costs bite
item.description: The world's top consumer goods and food companies, from Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble to Nestle and Reckitt, have warned of further price hikes next year to cover rising costs even as shoppers remain reluctant to splurge on groceries.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Marrow, Anuja Mistry
item.content:encoded: The world's top consumer goods and food companies, from Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble to Nestle and Reckitt, have warned of further price hikes next year to cover rising costs even as shoppers remain reluctant to splurge on groceries. Higher energy, raw material and freight costs as a result of the US war on Iran mean that the companies making everything from laundry detergent to soda and snacks face a balancing act to protect profit margins. Even higher prices on everyday items will fuel concerns that inflation will persist into next year. High gas and grocery bills are a big factor in next week's US midterm elections . Soaring costs related to the war are the latest headache for consumer goods, food and drink companies, which have struggled with lacklustre sales since the pandemic, as shoppers have baulked at increasingly expensive name-brand packaged food. Last year, they had to contend with tariffs on imported goods imposed by US President Donald Trump. "Pricing is the last lever these companies have left, and they’re pulling it into a consumer who’s already tapped out on paying more," said David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at PepsiCo investor Aptus Capital Advisors. On Tuesday, Coca-Cola (KO.N) CEO Henrique Braun said pressure on consumers could extend into 2027. "We are seeing elevated cost pressures ... driven by increased logistics and transportation costs," he said as the company [USN:L3N46D109 TEXT:"raised its annual profit forecast"]. HOW HIGH CAN PRICES GO? The challenge is working out how high prices can rise before shoppers walk away. The chair of Lindt & Sprüngli (LISN.S) said the Swiss chocolate maker is struggling because it [USN:L2N46A04K TEXT:"misjudged"] how consumers would respond to price increases. He spoke days after the company [USN:L6N4650EX TEXT:"ousted its CEO"] over concerns about its performance. Companies are running out of ways to absorb costs. Consumers in Europe and North America are particularly squeezed, said Reckitt (RKT.L) CEO Kris Licht. He said companies must decide how much of the cost increase to pass on through pricing and how much to offset with more promotional spending. "We will probably have to price more at this level of commodity costs and input costs," Licht said after the Durex maker trimmed its annual revenue forecast, sending its shares down around 5% on Tuesday. Procter & Gamble (PG.N) CFO Andre Schulten expressed a similar view after the Tide detergent maker last week hiked its expected [USN:L4N46811U TEXT:"hit to profit"] from rising raw material, energy and freight costs to $1.4 billion from $1 billion. "At this level of commodity pressure ... the industry generally is pricing up because there is no way to recover this level of commodity pressure without pricing," Schulten said. Procter & Gamble's pricing and sales held steady in the last quarter, but higher costs really hurt margins, said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. "Consumers are still spending if they see the value ... but we likely are near the upper limit of what consumers are willing to pay for snacks," Mulberry said. PepsiCo (PEP.O) has swung between price rises and cuts this year in an effort to boost sluggish sales and it [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"suffered a margin hit"] last quarter. Raising prices risks losing customers. Nestle (NESN.S) CFO Anna Manz said last week that volumes can dip in the short term when the company raises prices, as consumers adjust. "Looking forward, there's now again some upward pressure on input costs," Manz said as Nestle posted faster quarterly volume growth than pricing growth [USN:L6N4680BP TEXT:"for the first time"] since 2024. "We'll take pricing to the extent we can without damaging medium-term consumer penetration," she said.

Pope Leo will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru to meet victims of abuse by members of the clergy and the Church.

Pope Leo XIV greets participants in an audience with the Jesus Youth International Conference in the Paul VI Hall at the Vatican, Saturday, Oct 24, 2026. (Photo: AP/Alessandra Tarantino)

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo will meet with survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy during his Nov 6 to 17 three-country tour of South America , the Vatican said on Tuesday (Oct 27). The pontiff , who is recovering from lung cancer surgery , will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense foreign trips taken by a pope in decades, after being deemed fit for the journey by his doctor on Monday. "Several meet ings are planned with people who have been victims of abuse by members of the clergy and the Church," the Vatican said in its Tuesday statement. "These meet ings reflect the pope 's desire to express his closeness to those who have suffered, and who still suffer, because of this violence," it said. Pope Leo , 71, has held meet ings with survivors of abuse by clergy on several of his foreign visits, including in France last month. In that encounter, the pope met for two hours with seven French victims and reaffirmed his commitment to ending abuse of children by Catholic priests, the Vatican said afterwards. Pope Leo , originally from the US, served as a missionary and bishop in Peru for decades before becoming the head of the Catholic Church .

LONDON: GSK said on Tuesday (Oct 27) that it expects to almost double the number of cancer medicines it has in clinical trials next year , including those in early-stage studies, as it tries to rebuild its oncology business. The drugmaker's clinical -stage portfolio of about 15 assets would likely "come close to doubling" in 2027, Hesham Abdullah, who heads GSK 's oncology research and development, told the Wall Street Journal earlier on Tuesday. The British drugmaker has bet big on cancer drugs under CEO Luke Miels, including its US$10.6 billion takeover of US biotech Nuvalent earlier this year . One of the drugs acquired in the process received approval in July while a regulatory decision on another is expected by November. Miels faces the task of reassuring investors that the company can navigate looming patent cliffs for its blockbuster HIV drugs.

"We may have close to 20 phase threes ongoing in 2027," Eric Richards, who heads oncology product development at GSK , told Reuters earlier in the week at a medical meeting. Cancer drugs such as ris-rez and mo-rez are at the centre of GSK 's ambitions. On Monday, data from GSK and Hansoh's ris-rez showed that it helped patients with a hard-to-treat cancer live longer without the disease worsening. Five late-stage studies for mo-rez are ongoing as are two of four planned late-stage trials for ris-rez. Cancer drugs contributed £1.08 billion (US$1.44 billion) to GSK 's first-half sales. The company is due to report third-quarter earnings on Wednesday.

Palestinians protest against military demolitions in West Bank as Israelis vote

Over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Oct 23, the United Nations said.

Palestinians argue with Israeli army soldiers during a protest of Palestinian residents against their displacement from a neighbourhood, amid ongoing Israeli military operations, in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Mussa Qawasma)

HEBRON, West Bank: Israeli troops fired a stun grenade on Tuesday (Oct 27) to disperse Palestinians who gathered to protest against an Israeli military operation that has displaced thousands of residents from a neighbourhood in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. The unrest, which follows the deaths of two Israeli soldiers shot by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint last week, unfolded as Israelis were voting in an election in which the country's posture in the West Bank has been a major political issue. Some Palestinian officials have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of launching a crackdown in the West Bank to coincide with the vote, as a way to energise his right-wing supporters. The government says its operation is a response to the attack on its soldiers. A group of Palestinian men, women and children gathered at Tuesday's protest. One elderly man held a placard that said: "No to collective punishment, no to closures, and no to displacement."

The military said it had fired a stun grenade to disperse them so that its operation could continue.

A Palestinian man holds a placard which reads: "No to collective punishment / No to closure and no to displacement" during a protest in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Mussa Qawasma)

On Monday, the United Nations said that over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Friday. "Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," said UN human rights chief Volker Türk in a statement. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighbourhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing." The Israeli military said in a statement on Sunday that troops would carry out demolitions in the area. It said soldiers had not located any weapons in searches of the houses. Since Friday's attack on the checkpoint, Israel has blocked the entrances to most Palestinian cities and towns across the West Bank, severely curtailing Palestinians' freedom of movement. Noura Nassar, a displaced resident who attended the protests, said she had struggled to get medical treatment because of the blockages. "Where is the democracy in all of this? Their elections are today, sure, but what about us? Aren't we human beings? We want to go out, we want to visit the doctor," said Nassar.

A child looks at a banner depicting Israeli Prime Minister and Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu, during the country's national elections in Jerusalem, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ronen Zvulun)

Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both oppose the creation of an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. Residents expelled from the Hebron neighbourhood said Tuesday's election in Israel would do little to change the reality on the ground in territories Israel has occupied since 1967. "Among themselves they will elect who is the oppressor and who will destroy the Palestinian people. That is their election," said Sana' Salman Abu Sneineh, another expelled resident. Netanyahu's government has presided over a rapid expansion of Israeli settlements, which are deemed illegal by UN bodies and most countries, though Israel disputes this. Under Netanyahu's right-wing coalition there has also been a surge of militant settler violence against Palestinians.

item.title: GM moves to Nasdaq as first legacy automaker on the exchange
item.description: General Motors said on Tuesday it would transfer the listing of its common stock to Nasdaq from the New York Stock Exchange, joining a growing number of companies looking to align themselves with the tech-heavy exchange.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 27 story has been refiled to correct syntax in paragraph 3.) General Motors (GM.N) said on Tuesday it would transfer the listing of its common stock to Nasdaq from the New York Stock Exchange, joining a growing number of companies looking to align themselves with the tech-heavy exchange. [USN:L4N3WW11D TEXT:"Walmart"] (WMT.O) , Hilton (HLT.N) and Palantir (PLTR.O) are among the other companies that have recently made the shift to the Nasdaq, chasing proximity to tech stocks as investors rush to invest in the AI buildout. The Detroit automaker's shares rose by about 2% in premarket trade as it was set to become the first legacy automaker on the Nasdaq. The company has been injecting capital towards [USN:L6N46714Q TEXT:"modern technology"] including "eyes-off" autonomous driving on some models as it seeks fresh revenue streams from other products. "GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," said finance chief Paul Jacobson. The automaker is also developing a new software backbone for future vehicles to deliver the automated-driving system and other digital features, expecting drivers will be willing to pay for them. The move also comes at a time when legacy automakers, pressured by higher costs, have been trying their hand at producing cheaper, software-heavy vehicles as they try to keep up with Chinese automakers. GM has a market value of around $64.4 billion, according to data from LSEG. It expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq-listed company on November 17, and will retain its existing ticker symbol.

item.title: Stocks rise ahead of tech earnings, Fed decision
item.description: MSCI's global equities gauge rose on Tuesday as investors awaited earnings from US technology companies and the Federal Reserve's next policy decision.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: MSCI's global equities gauge rose on Tuesday as investors awaited earnings from [USN:L3N46A020 TEXT:"US technology companies"] and the Federal Reserve's next policy decision. [USN:L2N46D00J TEXT:"Oil futures"] settled down nearly $2 as investors turned to the prospect of Middle East peace talks, although prices remained near multimonth highs due to shipping disruptions. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei [USN:L2N46D0FZ TEXT:"met"] Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday, a day after holding talks with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. State media said Khamenei had stressed the importance of pursuing Iran's interests and maintaining its conditions for ending the war. A series of AI-related funding announcements on Monday from Meta (META.O) , SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) encouraged investors, along with [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"Anthropic's"] unveiling of its initial public offering filing. "The AI news gave headway to the bulls and got the bond market settled. That's been helping and we've seen small caps perform better," said Sahak Manuelian, managing director for global equities sales and trading at Wedbush Securities. "There seems to be more noise around coming up with some kind of solution to the conflict in the Middle East. Who knows what that means but, having said that, crude oil is trading down and that's a tailwind for stocks," said Manuelian. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 15.99 points, or 0.03%, to 52,377.57, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 45.83 points, or 0.60%, to 7,722.60 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) rose 308.43 points, or 1.18%, to 26,477.81. The Russell 2000 small-cap index (.RUT) finished up 1.2% for its second straight daily advance. Investors were awaiting earnings reports due this week from AI hyperscalers Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) and Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , looking for signs their spending is yielding returns as expected. Big Tech earnings could also influence investor appetites for the [USN:L6N46C148 TEXT:"Anthropic"] IPO and Meta's $95 billion equity fundraising. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) rose 6.58 points, or 0.59%, to 1,129.74. Earlier, the pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index finished up 0.47%. CENTRAL BANKS EXPECTED TO STAY ON HOLD Fed [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"policymakers"] have indicated they will not raise short-term borrowing costs again on Wednesday, but with inflation concerns front and center, investors think a pause in rate hikes will not last long. Traders are pricing in an increase from the Fed in December. Along with the [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"Fed"], the European Central Bank and the [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] are due to make policy decisions this week, with economists expecting all three to stand pat on interest rates, leaving investors to focus on comments from policymakers to gauge the rates outlook. In [USN:L2N46D0G8 TEXT:"currencies"], the dollar nudged higher against the euro, Japanese yen and sterling as traders prepared for the central bank meetings. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.35% to 102.38, with the euro down 0.43% at $1.1124. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.28% to 157.94. In [USN:L6N46D13Y TEXT:"fixed income"], US Treasury yields mostly edged higher with investors weighing the outlook for interest rate hikes ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 1.28 basis points to 4.999% while the 30-year bond yield rose 1.25 basis points to 5.3135%. The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, rose 2.8 basis points to 4.739%. US crude settled down 1.83%, or $1.86, to $99.90 a barrel and Brent finished at $113.88 per barrel, down 1.67%, or $1.93. In [USN:L2N46D0ZD TEXT:"precious metals"], spot gold rose 1.09% to $4,060.29 an ounce, while spot silver rose 0.95% to $54.44 an ounce.

item.title: What happens next after Israel's election?
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies appear on track to win the most seats in Israel's parliament after Tuesday's election, though neither he nor his main competitor, Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a majority.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies appear on track to win the most seats in Israel's parliament after [USN:L6N46E056 TEXT:"Tuesday's election"], though neither he nor his main competitor, Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a majority. Votes are now being tallied, followed by potentially long negotiations as parties try to assemble a governing coalition. If those talks fail, Israel could head to another round of elections. With [USN:L2N46E0B8 TEXT:"around 77.6% of votes tallied"] on Wednesday morning, Israeli media forecast Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties winning 54 seats in parliament, far surpassing 49 for [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot"]'s opposition bloc. WHEN WILL WE KNOW IF ANYONE WON? Israel's Central Election Committee was still tallying votes on Wednesday, and it will likely take until Thursday before definitive results of the election are known. The committee will also tally hundreds of thousands of ballots by Israeli soldiers, as well as diplomats, who voted from outside the country. The committee's tallying followed exit polls from major Israeli TV channels. Those polls can help give a general sense of each party’s relative strength but are not considered a reliable barometer of precise results, particularly in Israel’s fragmented political system. The final vote tally is expected by October 30 and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4. WHY IS IT SO COMPLICATED? The Knesset seats are allocated by proportional representation to national party lists, with parties needing to pass a threshold of 3.25% of the national vote to secure seats. About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED? After the final tally is in, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders on whom they want as prime minister and then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. That nominee has up to 42 days to form a government. No single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks. Every Knesset seat counts and small parties can have a big impact by becoming kingmakers. If the nominee fails, others can get a chance to try. If no government emerges, another election is called, with the present cabinet staying on as a caretaker government.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe ouvre dans le rouge, prudente face aux résultats et au pétrole
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe ouvre dans le rouge, prudente face aux résultats et au pétrole 28 octobre (Reuters) - Les principales Bourses européennes sont dans le rouge en début de séance mercredi, la prudence face à la remontée des cours pétroliers prévalant sur les résultats, avant les annonces de politique monétaire. Santander: Résultat net sous-jacent en hausse de 19% au T3 mais plombé par le Brésil MADRID, 28 octobre (Reuters) - La banque espagnole Santander a affiché mercredi une hausse de 19% de son bénéfice net sous-jacent au troisième trimestre, porté par le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis après de récentes acquisitions sur ces marchés, bien que le Brésil ait partiellement terni ces résultats. Worldline bondit après un retour à la croissance au T3 28 octobre (Reuters) - L'action Worldline décolle mercredi, au lendemain de la publication des résultats trimestriels supérieurs aux attentes du spécialiste français des moyens de paiement, les analystes saluant les signes de stabilisation de son activité. SSAB: Bénéfice au T3 au-dessus des attentes avec la hausse des prix de l'acier en Europe 28 octobre (Reuters) - SSAB a annoncé mercredi une hausse de son résultat d'exploitation au troisième trimestre légèrement supérieure aux prévisions, le sidérurgiste suédois citant une amélioration des prix de l'acier et une augmentation des expéditions. Unilever relève ses prévisions de croissance des volumes après des ventes au T3 au-dessus des attentes 28 octobre (Reuters) - Le géant des biens de consommation Unilever a relevé mercredi ses prévisions annuelles de croissance des volumes après avoir dépassé les attentes au troisième trimestre, porté par ses divisions beauté, soins personnels et entretien de la maison, malgré la faiblesse de son activité alimentaire et l'impact de la guerre avec l'Iran sur ses coûts. UBS affiche un bénéfice de $2,7 mds et accélère ses rachats d'actions ZURICH, 28 octobre (Reuters) - UBS a affiché mercredi un bénéfice net globalement conforme aux attentes au troisième trimestre et a accéléré son programme de rachat d'actions, alors que la banque reste préoccupée par les nouvelles exigences suisses en matière de fonds propres. Heineken doit redoubler d'efforts pour assurer sa croissance, selon son nouveau PDG LONDRES, 28 octobre (Reuters) - Le président-directeur général d'Heineken Rafael Oliveira a déclaré mercredi que l'entreprise avait besoin d'une plus grande responsabilisation à tous les niveaux et d'une culture de la performance plus forte pour assurer une croissance soutenue, dans sa première déclaration depuis son arrivée à la tête du brasseur néerlandais ce mois-ci. BASF relève à nouveau sa prévision de bénéfice récurrent 2026 28 octobre (Reuters) - Le groupe chimique allemand BASF a rehaussé mercredi ses prévisions pour 2026 pour la deuxième fois cette année, après un résultat opérationnel du troisième trimestre supérieur aux attentes, les fournisseurs européens de produits chimiques bénéficiant d'une hausse de la demande liée à la guerre en Iran. Allemagne: Le moral des consommateurs devrait se dégrader moins que prévu en novembre-GfK 28 octobre (Reuters) - Le moral des consommateurs allemands devrait se dégrader moins que prévu à l'approche du mois de novembre, montre une enquête publiée mercredi. Stellantis-Marge opérationnelle en hausse, €4mds de cash encore brûlés au T3 PARIS/MILAN, 28 octobre (Reuters) - Stellantis a annoncé mercredi une amélioration de sa marge opérationnelle au troisième trimestre, preuve selon lui de la progression de son plan de redressement, mais aussi un free cash flow industriel encore lourdement négatif, à hauteur de quatre milliards d'euros.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: Au moins 30 morts dans une collision ferroviaire en Castille-La Manche
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Au moins 30 morts dans une collision ferroviaire en Castille-La Manche MADRID, 28 octobre (Reuters) - Une collision survenue mercredi matin entre deux trains à grande vitesse près d'Urda, dans le centre de l'Espagne, sur la ligne reliant Madrid à l'Andalousie (sud), a fait au moins 30 morts, ont rapporté les autorités locales. Israël-Le bloc Netanyahu en tête, forte progression des partis arabes JÉRUSALEM, 27 octobre (Reuters) - Benjamin Netanyahu et sa coalition étaient en tête mercredi après dépouillement de près des trois quarts des bulletins de vote en Israël, sans toutefois réunir de majorité, au lendemain d'élections législatives marquées par une percée historique des partis arabes. L'Iran rejette le plan qatari pour un règlement du conflit avec les USA-responsable DUBAÏ, 28 octobre (Reuters) - L'Iran rejette les propositions des médiateurs qataris en vue d'un règlement diplomatique du conflit l'opposant aux Etats-Unis, car ce sont des "idées inacceptables", a déclaré mercredi un haut responsable iranien à Reuters. Ukraine: Une frappe russe fait cinq blessés à Kharkiv-services d'urgence 28 octobre (Reuters) - Une frappe de drone russe a fait cinq blessés, donc un enfant de quatre ans, à Kharkiv, la deuxième ville d'Ukraine, ont annoncé les services d'urgence ukrainiens. Trump prêt à accueillir Flavio Bolsonaro aux Etats-Unis WASHINGTON, 28 octobre (Reuters) - Donald Trump s'est dit prêt mercredi à accueillir aux Etats-Unis Flavio Bolsonaro, qui a quitté le Brésil après sa défaite au second tour de l'élection présidentielle et qui est visé dans son pays par une enquête pour blanchiment d'argent. L'Egypte et l'Arabie saoudite ont discuté des moyens de maîtriser la crise au Moyen-Orient LE CAIRE, 28 octobre (Reuters) - Le ministre égyptien des Affaires étrangères, Badr Abdelatty, a discuté mardi avec son homologue saoudien, le prince Faiçal ben Farhan, des moyens de maîtriser la crise au Moyen-Orient, a annoncé mercredi le ministère égyptien des Affaires étrangères. L’UE propose de renforcer les pouvoirs de Frontex BRUXELLES, 27 octobre (Reuters) - La Commission européenne a proposé mardi un élargissement majeur des pouvoirs de l'agence européenne des frontières Frontex, lui conférant notamment la capacité d'intervenir au-delà du territoire de l’Union européenne (UE), après l’afflux massif de migrants vers l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta l’été dernier. La Jordanie dit avoir tué plus de 20 combattants de l'EI en Syrie La Jordanie a tué plus de 20 combattants du groupe État islamique (EI) lors de frappes aériennes menées lundi soir dans le sud de la Syrie, à la suite d'un attentat meurtrier perpétré contre une église en Jordanie, a déclaré mardi le ministre de la Communication, Mohamed al Momani. Brésil: Le parti de Bolsonaro reconnaît le résultat de la présidentielle Le parti de Flavio Bolsonaro a reconnu lundi le résultat de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, qui a vu le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva obtenir un quatrième mandat, dans un communiqué. "Retour vers le futur" au Brésil? Flavio Bolsonaro, comme jadis son père, refuse de reconnaître la victoire de Lula Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a remporté dimanche un quatrième mandat historique.

item.title: OFRTP Summary
item.description: Un hommage national sera rendu aux victimes de l'attentat de Trappes
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un hommage national sera rendu aux victimes de l'attentat de Trappes PARIS, 28 octobre (Reuters) - "Un hommage national sera rendu" en soutien aux victimes de "l'acte terroriste raciste" qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves vendredi à Trappes et La Verrière dans les Yvelines, a annoncé mercredi la porte-parole du gouvernement, Maud Bregeon. Mbappé présente ses excuses après la polémique sur Mao Zedong Kylian Mbappé, lâché par plusieurs entreprises chinoises après des propos polémiques sur le "dictateur" Mao Zedong, a présenté mardi ses excuses, soulignant son "profond respect pour le peuple chinois et son histoire". Irak: Six Français condamnés à la perpétuité pour appartenance à l'EI Un tribunal irakien a condamné mardi six ressortissants français à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité et un septième à 15 ans de prison pour appartenance au groupe Etat islamique. France: Le tireur présumé de Trappes placé de nouveau en garde à vue, conteste toute visée raciste L'auteur présumé du "périple meurtrier" terroriste qui a fait un mort et sept blessés, dont quatre graves, le 23 octobre dans les Yvelines a de nouveau été placé en garde à vue lundi après une expertise psychiatrique le jugeant apte à des auditions, a annoncé le procureur national antiterroriste. Reçus à Matignon, les syndicats lycéens appellent à continuer la mobilisation Reçues par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu à Matignon lundi, les organisations lycéennes et étudiantes se sont félicitées des premières mesures annoncées par le gouvernement mais appellent à continuer la mobilisation. France: "Plus jamais le 17 octobre", promet Emmanuel Macron Emmanuel Macron a promis lundi de "continuer à tenir" face aux prochaines journées de mobilisation sociale en France et de tout faire pour ne pas réitérer le "traumatisme" du 17 octobre, marqué par des violences, pillages et saccages dans le pays. France: Laurent Nuñez s'attend à un nouveau samedi "compliqué" le 31 octobre Le gouvernement s'attend à un nouveau samedi "compliqué" le 31 octobre prochain, journée de mobilisation en France à l'appel des "Gilets jaunes" et a prévu un dispositif de sécurité "extrêmement robuste", a déclaré lundi le ministre de l'Intérieur. Marine Le Pen dit vouloir présider à la "Renaissance" de la France La candidate du Rassemblement National (RN) à l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Marine Le Pen, a dit dimanche vouloir oeuvrer au "redressement" et même à la "renaissance" de la France, en combattant la résignation et le défaitisme qui prévalent selon elle dans le pays. Le suspect de l'attaque dans les Yvelines placé en observation psychiatrique Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque de Trappes prolongée La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été prolongée, a annoncé samedi le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT).

item.title: Spain's deadliest train disasters
item.description: At least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, regional authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, regional authorities said. It is the [USN:L5N46E0V0 TEXT:"second deadly accident"] in less than a year on the line and will likely raise further questions over the country's train infrastructure ahead of [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"November's snap election"]. Here are some of Spain's deadliest train disasters, starting from the most recent: ADAMUZ (2026) Forty six people died and more than 120 were injured in southern Spain after a high-speed [USN:L8N3YK05S TEXT:"train derailed"] and collided with an oncoming one on January 18 near Adamuz, in the province of Cordoba. The accident is still under investigation. A preliminary report by Spain's Civil Guard in February pointed to defects in the track, rail or weld between two sections of track as the main hypothesis for the accident, but kept seven other theories open. SANTIAGO DE COMPOSTELA (2013) A [USN:L8N3154L8 TEXT:"railway accident"] in the summer of 2013 left 80 people dead and 145 injured when an eight-carriage high-speed train veered off the track on a sharp bend near the northwestern city of Santiago de Compostela, slamming into a concrete wall and bursting into flames. A Transport Ministry commission concluded that the accident was caused by speeding and the driver being distracted by a call from a superior, but a victims' association blamed the accident not only on human error but also on the railway's security systems. MADRID COMMUTER TRAIN BOMBINGS (2004) On March 11, 2004, 10 backpack bombs detonated on four Cercanias commuter trains, killing 193 people and injuring thousands of others during Madrid's rush hour. The attacks were carried out by Islamists opposing Spain's participation in the Iraq war. EL CUERVO (1972) An accident caused by a head-on collision between two trains on the Cadiz-Seville route left 86 people dead and more than 150 injured near the southern town of El Cuervo in 1972. The accident was caused by a driver's failure to stop at a red light at El Cuervo station, according to an investigation by state-owned rail operator Renfe. URDULIZ (1970) A head-on collision of two trains killed 33 people in the town of Urduliz, near the northern city of Bilbao, in the summer of 1970. A stationmaster was initially blamed for the accident, but it later emerged that he had been working 16-hour shifts for the previous four days. GRISEN (1965) A train on the Madrid-Barcelona route caught fire in 1965 in the town of Grisen, near northeastern Zaragoza, killing dozens of passengers. Though the train operator said at the time that 30 people died, later reports have said the real death toll was up to 80 and that the Francoist leadership tried to play it down. TORRE DEL BIERZO (1944) The 1944 crash of three trains in the El Bierzo region of León province is considered one of the deadliest railway disasters in Spain, with the estimated death toll of 78 still being debated due to censorship under Francisco Franco. A train travelling from Madrid to A Coruña suffered a brake failure and collided with a locomotive inside a tunnel, just before a third train entered the same gallery and crashed into the wreckage.
